NFL Harshly Fines Cardinals TE $20,411
full_text:
ARIZONA — Arizona Cardinals tight end Elijah Higgins was fined $20,411 for this play last week, which the NFL deemed "unnecessary use of the helmet" on what appeared to be a typical play that wasn't flagged during the game.
The NFL fined #AZCardinals TE Elijah Higgins $20,411 for this play last week. The league cited "unnecessary use of the helmet" and the play was one of four fines north of $20k last week pic.twitter.com/kefRzuJChx
Out of the 23 plays fined from Week, Higgins' total dollar amount ranked the fourth-highest. He now joins the likes of Trey McBride (Week 5, $17,911) and Karson Sharar (Week 2, $5,372) as Cardinals that have been fined by the NFL this season.
This seems like a fairly large fine for the ultimate outcome of the play, and while the NFL is trying to get head injuries lowered by discouraging players to lead with their helmets, Higgins being fined a large amount for lowering his head (especially when the defender began leading with his own head before Higgins dropped his shoulders) is a bit much.
Higgins is part of a strong Cardinals tight end room that often utilizes 13 personnel (one running back, three tight ends). Higgins' abilities in the run and pass game makes him a permanent piece in Arizona's offense.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur was recently asked about the usage of 13 personnel and its success in the passin game, which does involve Higgins:
“I’m guessing if you broke that down by the down and distance — obviously third down being when you’re in 11 a little bit more for obvious reasons (there's) not as much of a threat of run. You’re going to get- not that our tight ends are slow but we’re going to get our receivers out there and try to space out the field. In some aspects, (we’ve) been okay on third down, but in other aspects had more opportunities for growth and for first downs, if you will. I’d say that’s kind of mainly it. First and second down, you get a little bit more structured defenses, if you will. I thought the guys have done a good job understanding the space, getting the ball in their hands and being productive in that facet.”
Higgins has eight receptions for 96 yards and one touchdown through the first five weeks of the season.

title: Cardinals Make Last-Minute Roster Moves Before Rams Game
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have made the following roster moves ahead of their Week 6 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams:
The Cardinals previously ruled out RB Jeremiyah Love and safeties Wydett Williams and Andrew Wingard on Friday. Questionable is S Budda Baker, OLB Zaven Collins and P Blake Gillikin.
Arizona's practice squad moves could indicate they're confident in Collins and Gillikin playing since neither position received upgrades over the weekend. It's still 50/50 when it comes to Baker.
The Cardinals are hoping to stop a four-game losing skid when they visit SoFi Stadium this Sunday, a place familiar for head coach Mike LaFleur after spending the last two years as Los Angeles' offensive coordinator.
LaFleur's had some tough sledding to begin his Cardinals tenure, which has prompted many on the outside to demand change at several spots such as quarterback and defensive coordinator among others.
LaFleur, speaking with reporters this week, dove into why he hasn't made any sweeping changes to his Cardinals football team:
“My philosophy is to approach each week to try to give our team the best chance to win a football game. My philosophy as a coordinator was to put together the best plan that you could to have the offense go have success. Same thing with the defensive coordinator, same thing with special teams and then a position coach — the philosophy of making sure those players are ready to go on Sunday, mentally and physically," he said.
"To go back to what I said, every decision I’m going to make is based on what is best for Sunday if we’re playing on that Sunday. Then after that, re-evaluate and figure out what the next week entails. I can’t look further ahead. I’ve told you guys that. I told you guys that a couple of months ago. That’s still the way I feel. It’s what is going to give us the best chance to have success this Sunday. We are in a one-game season every single time. It is my job to look to the future. I do believe the work that we put in today will impact us not only for Sunday, but for the future.
"We’re working our butts off to get this thing fixed and we’re not going to stop until we do.”

title: Injury Report: Cardinals Officially Rule 3 Out, 4 Questionable vs Rams
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have a lengthy injury report entering this weekend's clash with the Los Angeles Rams.
The Cardinals are officially ruling out Jeremiyah Love (ankle), Wydett Williams (concussion) and Andrew Wingard (knee) ahead of Week 6's battle at SoFi Stadium.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur dove deeper into Love's absence, which you can read about here .
Questionable for Arizona is all of Budda Baker (groin), Zaven Collins (hip), Kitan Crawford (ankle) and Blake Gillikin (back). Neither Baker or Collins practiced on Friday while Crawford and Gillikin did in limited fashion.
Off the Cardinals' injury report is all of Carson Beck (back), Devin Duvernay (ribs), Isaac Seumalo (rest) and Josh Sweat (rest).
For the Rams, both Kam Curl (ankle) and Trent McDuffie (groin) are questionable entering the weekend. Neither practiced on Friday for Los Angeles.
The likes of Davis Allen (foot), Alex Bachman (wrist), Tyler Higbee (rest), Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder), Colby Parkinson (shoulder), Omar Speights (knee), Kegan Trost (hamstring), Josh Wallace (shoulder) and Byron Young (rest) were fully removed from Los Angeles' injury report and are good to go.
It's a familiar battle for both sides entering the week, as LaFleur spent the last few seasons under head coach Sean McVay in Los Angeles as the team's offensive coordinator, putting him against Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula.
"There's obviously familiarity with just going against him for two of the three years. First year was with Raheem [Morris], but that defense has evolved a lot over the last — since he took over to last year to this year. Obviously, similar foundations and characteristics, but they definitely put their new little twists on it," LaFleur said on facing Shula on Sunday.
"You got Jimmy Lake as kind of his right hand man in the defensive backfield, so there's definitely technique changes and different coverages and tools that they're using. And then I think just probably building it when when they had Myles [Garrett] too in terms of some of the stuff they were doing. So they throw a lot out at you. I asked him the other day. I said, 'So which one are you going to go with? You go with this, or you going to go with that?' And I just got a little chuckle. So, we'll see, and we'll be ready for it all."

title: Rams vs Cardinals: How to Watch, TV Map, Uniform Matchup
full_text:
Who : Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams What : NFL Regular Season Action, Week 6 When : Sunday, Oct. 18 at 1:05 PM MST Where : SoFi Stadium, Inglewood, CA
The Arizona Cardinals (1-4) and Los Angeles Rams (2-3) will meet for the first time this season when Sunday action at SoFi Stadium finally rolls around.
The two NFC West squads couldn't have more opposite trajectories or expectations as the 2026 regular season begins to take shape. Los Angeles is fully expected to be in the Super Bowl after their offseason investments while Arizona again is trending towards the basement of the NFL.
Cardinals-Rams can be found on FOX this week as their only late game in their broadcast window. Kenny Albert and Greg Olsen will be on the call with Pam Oliver on the sideline.
For those in market, if you have NFL+ you can stream it on mobile devices.
Cardinals vs Rams is the only late game for FOX this week (pictured in yellow on the map, h/t 506 Sports) pic.twitter.com/CGMzAzbrUk
In the post above, Cardinals-Rams is yellow on the coverage map. Practically all of Arizona and the Los Angeles local market will see the game alongside some of northern California, Washington, some of Idaho, Pittsburgh, Charlotte, Philadelphia and Boston.
In Arizona, you can catch the radio call on Arizona Sports' 98.7 FM with J.P. Shadrick (play-by-play), A.Q. Shipley (analyst) and Dani Sureck (sideline) the voices you'll hear.
In Los Angeles, ESPN's 710 AM will feature game coverage with J.B. Long (play by play), Maurice Jones-Drew (color) and D'Marco Farr (sideline) on the call.
The Rams, with a plethora of uniform options, are wearing their typical home looks with the blue/gold helmet, gold numbers on blue jerseys and gold pants with blue socks.
Gameday threads 🧵 pic.twitter.com/W5a6mGcfNS
Arizona continues to stick with their monochrome looks with all-white uniforms (with red numbers) being worn in Week 6:
Sunday's 🧵 pic.twitter.com/0RnbVMVemf
Mike LaFleur spoke incredibly high of Matthew Stafford and his process to get ready throughout the week:
“Well, it starts with his process. His process is the most consistent I’ve ever been around in my life. It’s daily, and I won’t even take you through it because it’d take me an hour, but it was fascinating to watch him go through it Monday. Putting a game to bed and giving himself some time on a Tuesday. It was kind of cool. He’d bring his wife and kids in, get some breakfast and stuff like that. I’d always get to see the kids on Tuesday morning and then he’d go do what he needed to do after he dropped them off. He’s a great father too, as I’m kind of saying that.
"Then he’d clear his mind on Tuesday, as much as a quarterback can, and then get right back at it on Wednesday. He was there when the coffee machines were starting. By the time you got to install, he’d already kind of heard it three or four times. When I would be installing, I’d be kind of looking at him and you could tell when he’s listening and then you could also tell when he’s memorizing all the play calls, so you didn’t want to ask him a question, if you will, or ask him to speak because you kind of had that vibe. You know where he was at. He’s getting these plays and he’s visualizing it. Then it just goes on to practice and all those kinds of things. An ultimate professional. A better person, obviously an MVP, Hall of Fame quarterback and I look forward to going against that challenge.
"When I took this, I told him how grateful I am for him, but at the same time when it’s time to go on Sunday, let’s go. I’m excited to watch our guys go compete.”

title: Cardinals Make Official Jeremiyah Love Injury Call vs Rams
full_text:
TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals have ruled out running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 6.
"There's no discussion of IR or anything like that. Got to really reevaluate [his ankle injury]. I mean, really every single day. Not good enough obviously right now to go Sunday. It wouldn't be in the best interest of him, and then we'll reevaluate on Monday," LaFleur told reporters on Friday morning.
Arizona also ruled out starting safety Andrew Wingard.
The Cardinals will rely on Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to steady their backfield against a tough Rams defensive front at SoFi Stadium.
Love has been dealing with multiple ankle injuries dating back to preseason, though he's managed to play in every regular season game until now.
Love hasn't practiced all week in the build-up to Week 6.
"I told you guys on Wednesday — we knew on Monday after just kind of watching the game, talking with him, seeing where he was at, that we were going to give him Wednesday off and you know reassess, I guess you could say on Wednesday with knowing that probably Sunday was a longshot," said LaFleur.
"He's doing good, but you guys see the way he cuts. Like just being candid, he cuts hard. That's a superpower of his, and when he's putting his left foot in the ground, it's just not right right now. And to get him to be to his best ability, it's what's right so he can go out and perform the way that he wants. So he can go out and honestly run the routes that he wants, because to run routes and separate, you got to be able to put those feet in the ground, and it's got to be deliberate. We want to get him healed so he can do that in the pass game and in the run game.
"I didn't totally answer your guys' question on Monday because I wasn't going to tell you exactly what was going on, but he is going to be a big part of our pass game when we feel like he's capable of doing that because he has it in his body. We just need to get him healthy."
The Cardinals will reveal their final practice reports of the week later today, though Arizona will be without their top draft pick for the first time all season.

title: Cardinals vs Rams Week 6 Expert Picks, Prediction Roundup
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Rams are set to meet in Week 6 action at SoFi Stadium, and in the least shocking development, the home team is heavily favored to win on Sunday.
The Cardinals are massive underdogs entering Week 6, and perhaps rightfully so. Arizona's shown little to inspire upset hopes of a Rams team that's coming off a short week and a loss on Monday Night Football.
National picks are heavily slanted towards Los Angeles:
Maldonado's pick: Rams 28, Cardinals 7 Moody's pick: Rams 38, Cardinals 17 Walder's pick: Rams 31, Cardinals 16 FPI prediction: LAR, 87.3% (by an average of 11.9 points)
It was a clean sweep of Rams picks again from Jeremy Bergman, Brooke Cersosimo, Gennaro Filice, Bobby Kownack, Dan Parr.
Cersosimo provided an explanation as to why she chose Los Angeles:
"Weird things happen in this league, but this one feels pretty straightforward. The Rams' offense is averaging 424.4 yards per game, and to be honest, it feels like they haven't come close to reaching peak performance in 2026. Sean McVay has a pick-your-poison attack that makes defenses pay on the regular, and Arizona's league-worst scoring defense will be no match for Matthew Stafford and Co.
"On the other side of the ball, Los Angeles' defense has been steady, ranking third in yards allowed and fifth on third down, and should do enough to stall an Arizona offense that'll likely have its share of chunk plays featuring Trey McBride but ultimately won't sustain most drives. The Rams' biggest issue has been their special teams, and they didn't waste time replacing kicker Harrison Mevis for Blake Grupeafter Monday night's fiasco. We'll see if one change does the trick."
Divisional battles are always tough, so there's credence to this being a close game. However, unless Arizona's really turned a corner this week in practice, it's really hard to imagine the Rams losing this game.
Final prediction: Cardinals 17, Rams 26

title: Rams-Cardinals Injury Report Sounds Alarm Bells for Jeremiyah Love
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Rams have unveiled their Thursday injury reports ahead of Week 6's battle at SoFi Stadium.
Another day, another practice that didn't involve Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love due to his ongoing ankle issues.
Two consecutive missed practice days doesn't spell good news for the Cardinals' top running back, putting his Week 6 status in heavy question. Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur should give us an update on Friday morning, though he was pretty adamant on wanting to give Love's ankle some rest.
Full reports for both sides:
Along with Love, Wingard missed a second straight day due to his knee issues.
Baker, Sweat and Seumalo all returned from their respective rest days yesterday. Those were the only changes on Arizona's side of the injury report.
Alex Bachman (rest), Keegan Trost (hamstring)
With yesterday's report being an estimation (due to Monday Night Football), the Rams hit the practice field for the first time on Thursday with some participation changes.
Trost and Curl were new names added to Los Angeles' injury report today while Bachman was upgraded from his previous limited participation yesterday.
Speaking with reporters earlier this week, Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett wasn't exactly excited to face a tough Rams defense.
“Everything-- from top to bottom. They are only getting better each week," he said. "They’re obviously ascending, and bringing (Rams DE) Aaron Donald back didn’t do us any justice, but we have to go out there and do our job. We look forward to this challenge coming into this week and I think we’ll be ready.”

title: State of the Arizona Cardinals, Part 2: How Things Turn Around
full_text:
The first part of our "Arizona Cardinals State of the Franchise" addressed the result of the first five games of the season and the current state of the roster, including injuries and the recent trade of Marvin Harrison Jr.
This part will address what I think has gone wrong this year and where the Cardinals can go from here:
The reality of football is that everything starts and ends up front and right now the Cardinals are losing the physicality game every week along the offensive line.
Part of the problem is outside of human control, injuries have taken two originals starters out of the lineup including left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. but even before injuries starting to affect things the line was not holding up its end of the bargain for the offense.
Unfortunately, it seems the Cardinals jumped the gun with the Jeremiyah Love selection. There is no doubt about his innate talent, but you can't evaluate a young running back if he's getting hit behind the line of scrimmage. Runners like Love that rely on their explosiveness and agility need creases and push from their offensive line. Instead, Love is getting blocked up and is routinely running into unblocked defenders and collapsed gaps.
Bad protection is also impacting quarterback Jacoby Brissett. He is a statue of a pocket passer, meaning he requires clean pockets to cycle through his reads. Brissett is currently second to last in the league for time to throw, averaging only 2.2 seconds before he has to get the ball out. With that subpar protections, his internal clock seems to be spazzing out and the panic has set into him in a way that we didn't see last year when he looked  like the cool, calm, and collected point guard.
Brissett has had his moments, but ultimately he is what he has always been. The ultimate professional journeyman, but fundamentally a mid-tier player. He can be a floor raiser in a pinch, but he is not, and was never designed to be, a foundational piece of this team's future.
When the scheme and protection are pristine, he can usually execute. Asking Brissett to elevate a unit is a different question altogether. He is not the type of player that can create something out of nothing (ironically one of Kyler Murray's great strengths), he is the type of player that can be tossed into an already functioning system and keep the wheels turning.
It seems like LaFleur is having to adjust what that system is on the fly as he faces the stark realities of being the head coach of a struggling team and Brissett will not be the solution that helps him find that truth.
This one is pretty simple. A lack of consistent, organic pressure from the Cardinals defensive front is straining every level of the defense.
When the pass rush can't effectively pressure an opposing quarterback, cornerbacks and safeties are asked to cover for extended, unreasonable lengths of time. Missed assignments and blown coverages are often the result and they aren't always necessarily the fault of the secondary.
Defenses are their own little ecosystems and when one part is pulling their weight the consequences are usually seen in other levels. The Cardinals have managed 11 sacks on the season but their pressure rate at 19.9% is the bottom third of the NFL.
It is far too early to start giving up on Mike LaFleur as the head coach of the Cardinals. He stepped into a tough situation, a roster he largely had no say in, and a generally dysfunctional organization. He deserves a certain element of grace.
He has been visibly frustrated on the sidelines which can be interpreted positively. He clearly cares and wants his team to succeed. Now, whether the season spirals into a complete, unadulterated disaster or stabilizes into a gritty, developmental rebuild year comes to the leadership and resiliency of LaFleur.
The early read on this is that LaFleur has the temperament to weather the storm and keep the locker room from fracturing. Let' s hope that is the case.
A hard look at Monti Ossenfort’s draft history reveals a concerning trend: the incoming volume of picks hasn't translated into immediate, difference-making contributors. Four drafts deep without generating clear Pro Bowl or All-Pro foundational pillars is an indicator that the talent acquisition model needs to be reevaluated.
The recent trade of the former No. 4 overall selection, Marvin Harrison, Jr. points toward a truth about Ossenfort. His teambuilding strategy still seems like it was generally the right direction for the team from when he took over, but his talent evaluation has led to picking the right positions but the wrong players.
Someone else needs to be making the selections in 2027 as the Cardinals attempt to fulfill LaFleur's vision for the team.
Rookie Carson Beck needs to start sooner rather than later.
The biggest decision the Cardinals will face this offseason will be what to do about the quarterback situation. As the most important position in the game, the entire future of the team rests on figuring out this situation.
If it was not before, it is now crystal clear that Brissett does not represent even a short term solution moving forward. Beck was a third round pick, a decently high selection that could have been used on another position of need. Clearly the team saw something in him. It is now time to see if that vision has any legs in the real world.
Beck needs to see some significant playing this season. The Cardinals needs to collect data that will influence the direction they take in the offseason and in the draft. If Beck has an arc similar to Tyler Shough in New Orleans is it possible that the team can use what will likely be another high draft pick and get an elite offensive or defensive linemen instead of being forced to use it on a quarterback?
That situation might be unlikely, but the truth is that the Cardinals needs to start evaluating Beck soon so that that sort of planning for the future of the team can start.
Kyler Burd has contributed work to several online publications covering his favorite team, the Arizona Cardinals. He is currently a staff writer for SI's All Cardinals/Fan Nation. title: Cardinals Fans Take Aim at Michael Bidwill With Blunt ‘Sell the Team’ Billboard
full_text:
Arizona Cardinals fans are making their voices heard loud and clear.
The team's 1-4 start to the 2026 regular season has been one of many final straws for the Red Sea, who have now taken out billboards to voice their frustrations towards owner Michael Bidwill.
"Michael. Please sell the team," one billboard reads.
Arizona Cardinals fans are voicing their frustrations with the state of the franchise and owner Michael Bidwill. A fundraiser started by Arizona sports influencer Nathan Kropp, who goes by Mr. AZ Sports on social media, raised money to post a pair of digital billboards in the… pic.twitter.com/iOZqrp4v4r
Public pressure is ramping up on Bidwill and the Cardinals' organization as a whole to turn things around. Arizona hasn't made the playoffs since 2021 while their last NFC West title came in 2015. From 2021-25, the Cardinals pieced together just 30 total wins.
Fed up Arizona Cardinals fans have started putting digital billboards up. pic.twitter.com/egROtHynGO
Hashtags on social media such as #Bidwillout have gained traction in the last few days, and so too has multiple petitions to get Bidwill to sell the franchise. This comes on the heels of two recently revealed lawsuits towards Bidwill by two former employees concerning, "racial discrimination, constructive termination, defamation and intentional infliction of emotional distress."
In a statement provided to The Athletic , the Cardinals said, "The team strongly denies these claims and will prove they have no merit. Because it is an active legal matter, the team will refrain from further comment.”
Fan dissatisfaction has ramped up towards Bidwill in recent years. The Cardinals' owner has refused to hire a team president to oversee football operations while replacing several season-ticket holder seats with luxury casita options.
Bidwill has not spoken to Cardinals reporters since the groundbreaking of the team's future facilities earlier this spring. He typically only does press conferences when a new coach or general manager is hired or fired.
The Bidwills have owned and ran the Cardinals dating back to 1933, where Charles Bidwill purchased the then-Chicago Cardinals for $50,000. Michael assumed most of his operating powers in 2007 when his father and prior owner Bill Bidwill named Michael the team's president.
After his father's passing in 2019, he became chairman/owner of the Cardinals.
Bidwill is unlikely to sell the organization unless circumstances such as the NFL forcing a sale happens.
However, fans in the desert are hoping for some sort of meaningful change that will translate into a winning product.

title: Cardinals, Marvin Harrison Jr. Didn’t Part on Good Terms
full_text:
ARIZONA — We're learning more and more about the Arizona Cardinals' split with Marvin Harrison Jr. by the day.
It was a whirlwind weekend for both parties as a trade was completed with the Houston Texans, one that netted the Cardinals a second-round pick for Harrison among other minor assets exchanged.
Yet as people from both sides begin to open up, it's pretty clear exactly where Harrison and the Cardinals stood.
"Those things I keep to myself really truthfully," Harrison said to Texans reporters in his first press conference. "What I learned in Arizona, I think I definitely learned a lot. Moving forward, I'm really just looking forward."
The Cardinals made Harrison the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, though the Ohio State product has failed to make good on his talent shown at the college level. There's been flashes, surely, though no consistency has been established.
"I'm not going to totally get into that right now. I really like Marvin Harrison," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said after their Week 5 loss to the Detroit Lions.
"He's a good person. I wish him well. We did what we thought was in the best interest of the Cardinals. Any guy that does not play to the level that I feel like they're capable of, I'm always going to put that on me and  coaching in general."
There was hope LaFleur would be able to unlock Harrison, though the wideout was clearly not a part of the Cardinals' offensive plans after he tallied just five catches in four games.
When asked when he knew his time in Arizona was coming to an end, Harrison said:
"It's hard to pinpoint an exact moment. When I knew, I think just kind of playing the game, understanding the business side of it, kind of get a feel for some things."
Eyebrows were raised when Harrison hired two agents to help facilitate a trade. When LaFleur was asked if Harrison wanted to be in Arizona, the Cardinals coach responded with:
"I'm not going to answer for 'Marv' (Marvin Harrison Jr.)."
It's clear the relationship between the two sides deteriorated, quickly, putting an unfortunate end to what was once a promising addition in the desert.
And while the bad blood will never be straight-up acknowledged, the short and refusing answers from both the Cardinals and Harrison tells us all we need to know.

title: Star-Crossed Falcons Draft Pick Comes Full Circle with Latest Roster Moves
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have made several defensive roster moves ahead of Sunday’s Week 6 matchup against the Chicago Bears, signing linebacker edge rusher Bralen Trice to the active roster and bringing safety Jammie Robinson back to the practice squad .
Atlanta also elevated Robinson and defensive end Drake Jackson as standard practice squad elevations, adding depth to the defense for Sunday’s contest.
Trice’s promotion comes after the third-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft made an impression during his opportunities with Atlanta this season. The former Washington standout spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons on injured reserve before returning to the field this year. He was out of practice squad elevations, and the Falcons had the choice of waiving him, hoping he'd pass through waivers and re-sign him to the practice squad, or signing him to the 53.
In three games this season, Trice has recorded one tackle and one pass defensed. He has also contributed to the defensive line rotation, playing approximately 26% of Atlanta’s defensive snaps during his three practice squad elevations.
His most notable performance came against the Green Bay Packers in Week 3, when he registered four quarterback hurries against Jordan Love. Those opportunities helped demonstrate his potential as a contributor to Atlanta’s pass rush.
Trice recorded 101 tackles, 28.5 tackles for loss, and 18 sacks during his three seasons at Washington, establishing himself as a productive defender before entering the NFL.
The Falcons also signed Robinson to the practice squad after releasing him from the active roster earlier in the week. Atlanta subsequently elevated the safety for Sunday’s game.
Robinson has appeared in two games for the Falcons this season, recording two solo tackles. He previously played six games for Atlanta in 2025 after spending his first two NFL seasons with the Carolina Panthers.
Across 29 career regular-season games, Robinson has recorded 19 tackles, including 15 solo stops. His experience in the secondary and contributions on special teams give Atlanta additional depth against Chicago.
Jackson will also be available Sunday after receiving his second consecutive standard practice squad elevation. The Falcons hope this is precautionary, as they continue to monitor the status of edge rusher Za'Darius Smith, who remains questionable with a neck injury .
The defensive end has appeared in one game for Atlanta this season. Across his NFL career, he has recorded 24 tackles, six sacks, nine passes defensed, and one interception.
Jackson previously played for the San Francisco 49ers and Washington Commanders before joining Atlanta.

title: Jeff Ulbrich Reveals Falcons' Biggest Challenge Against Ben Johnson's Bears
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH – The Atlanta Falcons face a unique challenge against the Chicago Bears this Sunday. Caleb Williams will start for the first time since Week 2, and his presence unlocks another level of this offense.
While Williams will get the attention, the Falcons face another underlying challenge that will likely play a bigger role in this game's outcome. It all starts with the guy up top.
Head coach Ben Johnson is renowned as an offensive genius and was a highly sought-after candidate after leading a record-setting Lions offense. He can open up the passing game and punish defenses with a potent rushing attack.
The Falcons defense knows it needs to be at its best on Sunday.
“There's very little weakness to his offense, and it starts with the run game,” Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said this week about Johnson. “They're number one in the rush for the entire league. And it's not a real close second, in my opinion, to what they do. The level of precision and execution (in the) scheme is elite, but then you combine that with a real style of play: physicality, a finish.
“They're going to test you schematically, technically, and physically, and everything in between. It's a great challenge in that way.”
At their best, the Bears have punished teams, like in Week 1 when they ran up 59 points on the Panthers. Since then, Chicago has been a lot of Jekyll and Hyde, producing scorelines of 3 points (with Williams going down at the end of regulation) in Week 2, 27 points in Week 3, 23 points in Week 4, and 7 points in Week 5.
Williams will get most of the attention for the Bears, but as Ulbrich mentioned, it starts with slowing down the rushing attack. With or without the former No. 1 overall pick under center, Chicago wants to run the football.
They lead the NFL in rushing, averaging 173.2 yards per game, but will be without bruiser Kyle Monangai for a second straight week, and starter D’Andre Swift is working through both a hip and knee injury that limited him to a single carry in the second half last Sunday. With Swift banged up and Monangai sidelined, the Bears ran for a season-worst 81 yards in a forgettable offensive performance against the Packers.
Either way, Johnson will have his unit in position to make an impact.
“There's countless challenges, to tell you the truth,” Ulbrich said. “They do it at the highest level. You can tell there's high-level precision, there's great coaching, there's great detail. And like I already said, there's a great style of play that comes with all that, which is very unique.”
The Falcons and their resurgent run defense have leaned on the four-man rush, using a league-high 72 unique four-man pass-rush combinations this season (third-most by any defense through the first five weeks of a season in the Next Gen Stats era), and it has paid off. Even after the Ravens poured in 208 yards, the Falcons boast a top-four rush defense.
That healthy utilization has unlocked the Falcons’ defense, allowing Ulbrich to deploy his second-level defenders elsewhere.
While Chicago won’t feature a Derrick Henry on Sunday, Johnson will present the Falcons with a different challenge, one they need to be ready for if they want to come out on top. The Bears' rushing production is built around Johnson's scheme and the entire offense's execution, forcing Atlanta to account for more than one player.
“You’ve got to be very diligent about what you're calling and when you're calling it,” Ulbrich said. “It's going to be a great challenge for the players. It's going to be a great challenge for our coaches and myself as well.”
If the Falcons’ four-man rush can control the Bears’ running game as it did against Green Bay and New Orleans, Williams’ return matters less. If it can’t, Johnson’s offense will make them pay regardless of who’s under center.

title: Falcons Rookie Avieon Terrell Ready to Step Into Big Role vs. Chicago Bears
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons will turn to rookie cornerback Avieon Terrell to help stabilize their secondary Sunday against the Chicago Bears.
With C.J. Henderson ruled out because of a groin injury, Terrell is expected to step into the starting lineup and receive a significant opportunity to prove himself at the NFL level.
“That's where we're fortunate to have depth in our corner room like we do," defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said. Mike Hughes is a top end starter in this league. Avieon [Terrell]’s emerging. We're fortunate that we have that depth. Billy [Bowman Jr.]’s had the ability to play that a little bit at times here and there in spots. Mike Ford has the ability to play a little bit of corner. So we've got candidates. We've got guys that can get it done outside and bring confidence in whoever goes out there."
Turns out, it's going to be Terrell.
Terrell enters the matchup with encouraging numbers in coverage. Through 100 coverage snaps this season, the rookie has allowed just five receptions for 39 yards, demonstrating his ability to limit opposing receivers when given opportunities.
With the Falcons looking to bounce back from their Week 5 loss to the Baltimore Ravens, Terrell will have an important role in helping Atlanta contain Chicago’s passing attack.
The Falcons are still without starting cornerback A.J. Terrell, who remains on injured reserve for at least this week, leaving Atlanta without one of its most experienced defensive backs.
Avieon Terrell was selected by the Falcons in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft with the 48th overall pick after a productive career at Clemson. He developed into a versatile defensive back during his collegiate tenure, showcasing his coverage ability, physicality, and willingness to contribute against the run.
During his final season at Clemson, Terrell recorded nine passes defended and five forced fumbles, demonstrating his playmaking potential. Those skills helped make him an appealing addition for Atlanta as the organization looked to strengthen its secondary for the future.
Now, the rookie will have an opportunity to translate that production to a starting role against an NFL opponent.
Avieon’s first start also comes with a personal connection. He is the younger brother of A.J. Terrell, who has been a key part of Atlanta’s defense since the Falcons selected him in the first round of the 2020 NFL Draft.
With A.J. sidelined on injured reserve, the brothers will have to wait for another opportunity to play together in Atlanta’s secondary. However, Avieon’s promotion gives the younger Terrell a chance to establish his own identity and demonstrate why the Falcons invested a second-round pick in him.
Sunday’s matchup against Chicago will present a different challenge as Terrell prepares for an expanded workload. If the rookie can maintain his early success, he could strengthen his case for a larger role in Atlanta’s defense moving forward.

title: Falcons vs. Bears Odds, How to Watch, Injuries for NFL Week 6
full_text:
ATLANTA – The Atlanta Falcons look to rebound at home in their first non-primetime game since Week 2, after narrowly missing a perfect 3-0 performance in front of a national audience. The Falcons squandered a late lead to the Ravens and eventually succumbed in overtime.
The Chicago Bears are also eager to put some bad Week 5 memories behind them. They fell to the Packers in a humbling fashion, but they will get some reinforcements in quarterback Caleb Williams. With both Williams and Michael Penix Jr. returning Sunday, it marks the first time the former 2024 top-10 picks and Pac-12 rivals will have faced off since college. Given how these offenses performed without them, Atlanta and Chicago fans are breathing a sigh of relief.
Beyond the quarterbacks, both offenses will lean heavily on the run, with these squads ranking No. 1 and No. 2 in the NFL in rushing offense. Both units will look to establish the ground game , taking pressure off their beat-up signal-callers.
Defensively, the Falcons will hope to get edge rusher Za’Darius Smith back from a concussion/neck injury that held him out last Sunday, while the Bears have a few question marks . It will also mark the first time former Falcon defensive lineman Grady Jarrett will play in Atlanta for another franchise.
The Falcons are slight underdogs at home (-1), but Vegas expects a high-scoring affair (54 o/u). Here’s everything you need to know to watch the Falcons’ Week 6 matchup with the Bears.

title: Falcons Injury Report: Atlanta Makes Final Call on Michael Penix Jr. for Bears
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons will have Michael Penix Jr. under center for Sunday’s Week 6 matchup against the Chicago Bears, providing a significant boost to the offense after the quarterback suffered a rib injury against the Baltimore Ravens.
Penix was a full participant in Friday’s practice and was not given a game designation on the Falcons’ final injury report. The lack of an injury designation indicates that Atlanta expects its starting quarterback to be available for Sunday’s home matchup.
The Falcons will look to bounce back after a disappointing 30-23 loss to Baltimore in Week 5, with Penix expected to lead the offense against a Chicago defense that Atlanta will need to challenge early.
Penix exited Sunday’s loss to the Ravens in the fourth quarter after taking a sack and suffering a rib injury. He missed one play before returning to throw an incompletion. During the long break between possessions in overtime, adrenaline wore off, and he missed the Falcons' final series.
Following the game, head coach Kevin Stefanski indicated that Penix should be ready to start against Chicago, provided his recovery progressed as expected.
“I’m not going to get into specifics, but he’s feeling better,” Stefanski said earlier in the week.
Friday’s full participation in practice and the absence of a game designation provide further optimism for the Falcons as they prepare for Sunday’s contest.
Having Penix available is particularly important as Atlanta looks to regain its offensive rhythm following the loss to Baltimore. The Falcons had opportunities to take control of that game but struggled to turn promising situations into touchdowns, settling for field goals on multiple occasions.
Penix will now have an opportunity to help Atlanta get back on track against a Bears team that presents another challenge for the Falcons .
While the quarterback’s availability is encouraging news, Atlanta will also have to navigate several injury concerns on the defensive side of the ball.
Cornerback C.J. Henderson has been ruled out after suffering a groin injury against Baltimore. The Falcons will likely lean on Mike Hughes and Avieon Terrell at outside cornerback, with Mike Ford potentially providing additional depth.
Veteran defensive end Za’Darius Smith is listed as questionable. Smith cleared concussion protocol Thursday but continues to deal with a neck injury. After missing Thursday’s practice, he was a limited participant Friday.
With Penix cleared to play, the Falcons can turn their attention toward preparing for a pivotal Week 6 matchup. Atlanta will look to protect its home field, improve its offensive execution and avoid a second consecutive loss as it continues its push in the NFC South.

title: Inside Rookie LB Kendal Daniels’ Growing Role as  Falcons' Swiss Army Knife
full_text:
In college, Kendal Daniels was a safety, the position he played when he won the 2022 Big 12 Defensive Freshman of the Year with Oklahoma State.
Then, in his latter years at OSU and his final college football season at Oklahoma, the bulked-up Daniels moved to linebacker and a hybrid role.
The rookie inside linebacker said he learned he could balance multiple roles under OU head coach Brent Venables.
“There’s crossover,” Daniels told reporters Thursday. “It just depends on the playcall. Sometimes it’s the same drop, just from a different position.”
But the 23-year-old had no idea those years were tailoring him for his role with the Atlanta Falcons , who picked him in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft this past April.
“Kendal knows every position on the defense,” said Divine Deablo, Falcons linebacker .
“That’s a credit to how hard he works. I walk by the linebacker room, and he’s in there studying. Major props to Kendal. He’s going to continue to grow and be a great player. Kendal’s going to be in this league for a very long time.”
Alongside playing Mike and Will linebackers in Atlanta under inside linebackers coach Barrett Ruud, Daniels has now picked up defensive end duties, most notably in the Falcons’ 30-23 overtime NFL Week 5 loss to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football.
“I’ve been around guys that can articulate it but can’t go out there on the grass and apply everything that they know,” said Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich . “I was hopeful that all of that would come to fruition, that he could apply. And then once we got into camp, you started to see it really quickly.”
Daniels played 50 defensive snaps and 13 as a special teamer.
“He’s done great. Kind of a big surprise for us, to be honest with you,” Atlanta special teams coordinator Craig Aukerman spoke highly of Daniels. “That’s a part of the communication aspect, how much is Kendal going to be playing this week. Everything that we’ve asked Kendal to do is attention to detail, being a pro, and asking a bunch of questions. Those things have really impressed me [on] how smart this kid is. Because he wants to learn, he wants to get better. He’s out there early, working early, trying to work on technique and fundamentals. I can see him only getting better.”
Daniels spent a portion of the offseason not fully participating in on-field work due to an Achilles injury.
But Ulbrich saw the 6-foot-5, 242-pounder as a jack of all trades. Especially when the Falcons lost young edge rushers, Jalon Walker to a torn ACL during preseason training camp , and James Pearce Jr. to an eight-game suspension for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy.
“Who can handle this burden of a little bit extra and a little bit more? And we found out right away that he was that guy,” Ulbrich recalled.
“A lot of this is new. It doesn’t feel new at times. But there’s huge room for growth, and there will be growth because of the way he’s wired. I can never see him as being a player that says, ‘I got it,’ and he kicks his feet up and feels like he’s arrived. He’s got humility, a great desire to work hard, and to be really good at this game. As long as he can keep that approach and mentality, which he will, he’s going to keep growing and getting better.”
In his first games in the trenches, Daniels revealed that his current challenge is learning to read the offensive line to determine whether a play is a pass or a run.
“Still trying to figure that out and trying to get better at that every day,” he said. “Moving out to the line of scrimmage and being able to play in the box, it’s fun but a lot of learning.”
In his multi-hyphenated role, Daniels has collected 23 tackles (17 solo), a sack, and a pass deflection. He’s fourth overall on the team in solo tackles but leads Atlanta’s linebacker position in the category.
“That’s rare for players, period, and very rare for a rookie to handle,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said about Daniels. “As you’re around Kendal and as you watch him work, it’s not that surprising. He’s certainly been proving to be capable of handling a lot.”
Daniels and the Falcons (2-3) next face the Chicago Bears (3-2) and their league-leading running game. Kickoff is at 1 p.m. on FOX as Atlanta hosts the NFL Week 6 game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

title: Is Falcons’ Run Defense Fact or Fiction? Bears To Test Atlanta
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons’ defense was riding high through the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL season.
They boasted a middle-of-the-pack ranking in total defense and were the No. 1 run-stopping unit across the league’s 32 teams.
And then they were humbled.
The Baltimore Ravens, led by running back Derrick Henry , visited Atlanta and gashed the Falcons for 208 rushing yards en route to a 30-23 overtime win on Sunday Night Football.
“I didn’t prepare them in the best of ways, and we didn’t have enough bullets in the chamber for game day for the style of play which we got,” Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich told reporters on Thursday.
Now, Atlanta faces its biggest test yet in the Chicago Bears. The Bears visit the Falcons this Sunday at 1 p.m. at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Per ESPN, the Bears own the No. 1 run offense in the NFL, averaging 173.2 yards per game. Coincidentally, the Falcons are No. 2 , and Atlanta’s most recent opponent, Baltimore, is third.
“It starts with the run game, obviously; they’re number one in the rush for the entire league,” Ulbrich said about the Bears. “And it’s not a real close second, in my opinion, to what they do.”
Chicago has a two-headed monster in the backfield in D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai. They combine for 678 yards on the ground and seven touchdowns, with Swift narrowly leading the way in the stat book.
“Kyle runs really hard, D’Andre is the more agile back,” said defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. , whom the Falcons acquired from Chicago this August. “When one comes out, the other one’s coming in and doing almost a completely different thing. They’ve got two great backs over there.”
The ground game has the Bears staying afloat even without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, out with a hamstring injury since Week 2. Williams is on track to play in Atlanta this week.
Ulbrich says second-year Chicago head coach Ben Johnson has no weaknesses in his offense.
Specializing in wide and outside zones, the Bears also thrive at backside blocking. With blockers away from the direction of the play, the scheme opens cutback lanes and prevents defenders from chasing down the ball carrier.
“Our backside pursuit, our cutback players, we have to fight the crossover, we have to have great discipline in that way,” Ulbrich explained. “And we got to trust that the front side is going to take care of their job.”
Stopping Chicago’s potent run game can force a freshly returning Williams to have to throw the football at volume.
But the Falcons have one of the best pass rushes in the NFL, collecting quarterback hits, pressures, and opportunistic sacks. In fact, Dexter and fellow defensive tackle Brandon Dorlus are tied for first in the NFL with 20 quarterback pressures.
It’s the most among the position and defensive tackle duos.
So if the Falcons can defend the run successfully, it can present a challenge for Williams and his recovering hamstring.
“We want to come in and try to stop the run so we can earn the right to rush,” Dexter said.
Falcons-Bears will be televised at 1 p.m. EST on FOX.

title: Falcons Release Safety 2 Days After Hosting Former Bronco for Tryout
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have released safety Jammie Robinson just days after signing him to the active roster, opening up a spot on the team’s roster as they continue evaluating their options in the secondary.
Robinson originally joined the Falcons’ practice squad at the start of the season and was one of the team’s standard practice squad elevations for their Week 4 matchup against the New Orleans Saints on Monday night.
Before Atlanta’s Week 5 prime time matchup against the Baltimore Ravens, the Falcons had an opening on the active roster after placing linebacker Yasir Abdullah on injured reserve. Robinson signed to the active roster last Saturday, filling the vacant spot before Atlanta’s loss to Baltimore.
Robinson primarily contributed on special teams during his appearances, recording 44 special teams snaps through Weeks 4 and 5, accounting for 72 percent of the team’s special teams snaps during that span.
The safety previously appeared in six games for Atlanta last season after joining the team’s practice squad in November. Before arriving in Atlanta, Robinson spent two seasons with the Carolina Panthers.
A fifth-round pick out of FSU by the Panthers in the 2023 NFL Draft, Robinson has appeared in 27 career games since entering the league. His departure comes shortly after the Falcons elevated him to the active roster, suggesting the team is continuing to evaluate its depth and potential options at safety.
Meanwhile, Atlanta has already begun exploring additional options in its secondary.
The Falcons hosted former Denver Broncos safety Delarrin Turner-Yell for a tryout on Wednesday. Turner-Yell was selected by the Denver Broncos in the fifth round of the 2022 NFL Draft and has appeared in 31 career games.
He missed all of 2024 with a knee injury, and injured his knee again last year after being activated in December. He was a special teams standout and depth player before the injury. The Falcons would consider him a potential depth option for a Falcons team that continues to assess its personnel in the defensive backfield.
Although a tryout does not guarantee a contract, Atlanta’s decision to bring Turner-Yell and then release Robinson two days later is a strong indication the team is considering alternative options at safety.
The Falcons will continue working to find the right combination of depth and special teams production as they prepare for their upcoming matchup against the Chicago Bears, scheduled for 1 p.m. EST at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

title: Bijan Robinson Discusses Atlanta Falcons Secret Weapon in Run Offense
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have found consistent production on the ground through the first five games of the 2026 season, and Bijan Robinson credits the offensive line’s experience and execution for helping fuel the rushing attack.
Atlanta enters Week 6 with the second-ranked rushing offense in the NFL, averaging 181 rushing yards per game and 5.2 yards per carry.
Robinson has rushed for 580 yards on 102 carries, averaging 5.7 yards per attempt with four touchdowns. He's also added 152 yards and a touchdown on 18 receptions, mostly screen passes. His production has helped Atlanta establish a physical offensive identity under head coach Kevin Stefanski, with offensive line coach Bill Callahan helping develop a rushing attack that blends outside zone concepts with power and gap schemes.
Robinson believes the familiarity between the offensive line has been very important, and Callahan, who joined the Falcons this year with Stefanski, has quietly helped bring it all together without much fanfare.
“That experience that offensive line has is key because, you know, that’s what we’ve been doing for a long time,” Robinson said. “They know every angle, they know where they’re supposed to be, and they know who they’re supposed to attack.”
The running back also understands his responsibility within the scheme.
“It’s my job to set them up, make them look good, understand where the holes are supposed to be,” Robinson said. “That’s how we continue to keep getting success on that run scheme.”
While outside zone remains a foundation of Atlanta’s offense, the Falcons have incorporated more gap concepts to give defenses additional looks.
Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. has praised Callahan’s ability to develop those concepts, describing the veteran offensive line coach as having “a genius of a mind” when discussing the run game.
“I love the new additions that we have in the run game because I came from that in college,” Robinson said. “I came from power, duo, even wide zone.”
Robinson believes those additions can make the offense more unpredictable and create opportunities for big plays.
“Just having those changeups, you really don’t know what we’re going to come out with,” Robinson said. “I think it’s just important to keep getting better at it, just keep running it because those little plays can pop for really, really long runs.”
The combination of established blocking principles and additional rushing concepts gives Atlanta multiple ways to attack opposing defensive fronts. Robinson’s production through five games demonstrates the potential of that approach, particularly when the offensive line creates opportunities for him to reach the second level.
The Falcons also have Brian Robinson Jr. providing another physical presence in the backfield, helping keep the rushing attack fresh throughout games.
“That’s what the run game is, man. That’s what wears teams out,” Bijan Robinson said. “When you’re effective in it, when you’re continuing to be physical in it, it opens up the pass.”
With Callahan working to develop the offensive line and Robinson averaging nearly six yards per carry, Atlanta has a foundation to build on. Continuing to execute its outside zone concepts while developing its power and gap schemes could make the Falcons increasingly difficult to defend as the season progresses.

title: Falcons Legend Grady Jarrett Opens Up On Returning Home as a Chicago Bear
full_text:
Former Atlanta Falcons defensive lineman Grady Jarrett went to high school roughly 25 miles east of Mercedes-Benz Stadium and spent 10 productive years with the Falcons.
He made two Pro Bowls, and probably would have made more if it weren't for the Falcons tax of playing his last seven years on a team with a losing record. His dad, Jessie Tuggle, is in the Falcons Ring of Honor, and is generally considered one of the greatest Atlanta Falcons of all-time.
By all accounts, Jarrett is Falcons royalty.
He was released by the Falcons at the opening of free agency in 2025 and was quickly scooped up by the Chicago Bears with a massive three-year contract that included $28.5 million of guaranteed money .
Jarrett only started four games last year, appearing in 14, but he's started all five of the Bears' games this season and is on track to start this week in his first return home to face the Atlanta Falcons.
"I mean, everybody kind of knows what that means to me," Jarrett said of the trip to Atlanta this week.
However, Jarrett is about business this week after the Bears were blown out by the Packers.
"But at the end of the day, I think the most thing I'm excited about is going out here competing, getting back on the right track, and, doing what we need to do," Jarrett said.
Jarrett also knows from experience how many Bears fans have fled the Chicago area and migrated south. They'll be heard on Sunday.
"It's gonna be a heck of a crowd out there," Jarrett said. "I think the Bears fans are gonna show up big time. I think they're excited to see us get back on the right track, and, we need to go out there and do what we need to do."
Jarrett was asked if he would take any time to soak in the nostalgia of being back in Atlanta, but he's content with his time with the Falcons and is looking forward, not back.
"My time in Atlanta was well served, 10 years, a lot of success, and struggles, but I mean I gave it its due time and respect. I think all my focus is here right now, doing what I need to do, and getting This team back on the right track," Jarrett said.
That doesn't mean Jarrett won't be happy to be home and see some familiar faces.
"I definitely think it's special; anytime I go back and play in the stadium like that and around those fans that I've been around for so long, I definitely got to acknowledge how special that is to me and and it means a lot, but I don't think there's much need for me to take a big reflection day and hit my knee and and think about this and that.
"I mean, I'm grateful to God to have me where I am right now, take me through everything I can, been through there, to make me who I am, to be the best me for this team here now, and, I acknowledge that, but the the main focus is getting this team on the right track back in the winning column, and going out out there and competing our tails off."
After watching Grady Jarrett do just that for a decade, Atlanta Falcons fans expect nothing less from a player whose jersey could one day be in the rafters alongside his dad's.

title: Three Primary Reasons The Ravens Should Beat The Browns Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens were projected to compete for a Super Bowl before the season began. The Browns were projected to compete for the first-overall pick.
While the injury report may be daunting for the Ravens and no Lamar Jackson (ankle) at quarterback is certainly a big deal, this is also a football game Sunday at Cleveland that they should find a way to win. It’s the last time they are certain to be a favorite for a while with teams like the Bengals and Jaguars and Bills looming and it’s Jesse Minter’s first AFC North game and plenty of individuals on this roster realize just how difficult winning in Cleveland has been for this organization.
As always, there are a handful of critical matchups that will go a long way to deciding this football game  and, like most divisional games, this will very likely come down to which team controls the line of scrimmage. Line play will be everything and the Ravens should have the combination of $30M/year edge rusher Trey Hendrickson and $20M/year defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike on the field for longer than ever before, and at closer to full health than ever before ( they’ve played just 32 snaps together all season ).
The Ravens have, on paper, three primary advantages heading into this game that they must lean into and find a way to exploit. They provide the path to victory and explain why Baltimore is still a field-goal favorite on the road despite their injuries. Here’s how and why they should win this game.
Rookie offensive play caller Declan Doyle said Derrick Henry would see a lot of the football and didn’t back off another 300-carry season for him (he’s never done it three straight years) and, well, Henry has run the ball more times through five weeks than any age 32 RB since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger.
Guess who leads the NFL with 113 carries? You got it, with eight more than Jahmyr Gibbs (Lions). The Browns are allowing 4.5/carry and are 30th in Expected Points Added and Success Rate against the run. Their premier defensive tackle and do-everything linebacker are both on the injury report. Every reason in the world to keep this close and test them over and over with volume and multiplicity on the run game (more carries for QB Snoop Huntley, we presume HYPE GAM and some receivers as well and not necessarily just Zay Flowers).
Baltimore is as healthy up front on defense as it has been all season, Madubuike is all the way back after missing more than a year with a neck injury and they just shutdown the best running back in the NFL – Bijan Robinson – on the road in Atlanta last Sunday night.
We wonder if Browns coach Todd Monken, former Ravens offensive coordinator who knows this group well, will even mess around with establishing the run all the much and will just try to throw his way to the lead and attack a suspect secondary . Still, it’s very difficult to win games in the AFC North without being able to sustain a run game and we don’t fancy the Browns rank 30th in the NFL in EPA/designed run play (-0.22).
The Browns QB hasn’t thrown in the towel in the regular season – he certainly tried to do it in the preseason – and he’s been playing decent football. But his legs are not what they used to be, and when he holds the ball he becomes a double agent.
Watson is being sacked on 11.4% of his dropbacks , this Browns offensive line has big issues all around and this guy will turn the ball over. He is also a notoriously slow starter and if the Ravens can run their way to the lead in the first half they should have success taking the air out of the ball in the second half. Watson is in the bottom third in the NFL in air yards per attempt, pushing the ball downfield is not a forte for either QB in this game, but Huntley has the benefit of what should be a robust run game to put him in down and distances to succeed.

title: Five Storylines For Ravens' Divisional Matchup vs. Browns
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will be on the road again in Week 5 for their first game against an AFC North opponent when they take on the Cleveland Browns on Sunday afternoon.
Coming off a thrilling victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5 in primetime , in which they had to pull off a late rally and force overtime to extend their winning streak, the Ravens are currently holding the best record in the division at 4-1, while the other three teams are tied for second at 3-2.
There are several intriguing storylines surrounding this divisional matchup between these two rival teams. Here are the top four.
With two-time league MVP Lamar Jackson officially being ruled out after missing the entire week of practice for the second week in a row since suffering an ankle sprain midway through the Ravens' Week 3 victory over the Tennessee Titans, his Pro Bowl backup will be making a second straight start this upcoming Sunday. Huntley performed exceptionally well in last week's overtime thriller over the Atlanta Falcons after getting all of the reps with the first-team offense leading up to the game.
The seventh-year veteran went 24-of-32 for 201 passing yards and a pair of touchdowns and scored the game-winning touchdown on a quarterback sneak. He is now 3-0 in his last three starts in place of Jackson since rejoining the team last year, two of which came in primetime and all were against NFC opponents.
As the next man up again, this will mark his first start against a division rival since Week 18 of the 2023 season, when the Ravens had the division crown and the AFC's top seed, and decided to rest several key starters against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Unlike that game, this one has much higher stakes and they'll need Huntley to be on his 'A' game with first place on the line.
"[Huntley]'s a really good player, and he's got a great demeanor," head coach Jesse Minter. "He's got great poise. He has great respect amongst his teammates. He's just [an] infectious personality. Infectious can be different, [but] he's just cool, calm, collected, confident — that to me, that's infectious. When he's in there, that's kind of how the guys feel, and it's really no different with Lamar."
While the Ravens' home record has been abysmal, dating back to last season's franchise-worst six losses, they've been far more successful away from the confines of M&T Bank Stadium. In addition to being perfect 3-0 on the road through the first five weeks of this season, their 21-7 record playing outside of Baltimore since 2023 is the best in the league, as is their point differential, turnover differential and offense with an average of nearly 400 total yards.
Their running game has traveled especially well, averaging over 180 yards on the ground per road game since 2023, with an NFL-record streak of 36 consecutive road games of rushing for at least 100 yards. The Ravens are 4-4 in Cleveland during the Jackson era dating back to 2018, and this Sunday will mark Huntley's second career start against them during that span, with his first coming in Week 15 of the 2022 season.
Through the first four weeks, the Ravens were among the most penalized teams in the league, having been flagged 10-plus times for over 100 yards twice in that span, including season-highs with 13 flags for 131 yards in Week 4. They managed to finally buck that trend in primetime against the Falcons with a season-low five penalties for 40 yards against the Falcons. The bulk of their flags were attributed to the offense, as they were not only still getting acclimated to running the Declan Doyle offense in live action, but they also had shuffling pieces on the offensive line and at the skill positions due to players going down and even being lost for the season due to injuries.
It might've been the fact that they were playing with a small margin of error, with a backup quarterback under a national spotlight for the first time this season, that made them dial in even more last week. Nonetheless, they find themselves in a similar situation heading into this matchup and will need to do their best to repeat the feat or do even better.
Overall, the Ravens rank in the middle of the pack when it comes to passing yards allowed per game with 223.6, and for the past four weeks, nearly half and sometimes more than half of that production has come from the connection between the opposing quarterback and his top wideout. They've allowed a 100-plus-yard receiver in three straight games during their win streak. Even though Chris Olave fell just shy of reaching the century mark in Week 2, he was unguardable when the New Orleans Saints needed him most as they spoiled the Ravens' home opener in an upset.
This trend wouldn't be especially puzzling if the Ravens didn't have one of the league's most talented defensive backfields, which they've invested four first-round picks and free-agent resources in over the years. They've had their top two cornerbacks, Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey, make big plays in key moments against these upper-echelon wideouts, but haven't been able to fully put the clamps on for a full or even most of the game. The Browns' leading receiver through five weeks is second-round rookie Denzel Boston with 330 receiving yards, three touchdowns and a league-leading 20.6 yards per catch.
"Every team has a good one. I feel fortunate that we have good corners," defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said. "We don't really have to necessarily travel to people. I think we do in certain spots just because of specific skill sets of our guys, but we feel confident in all the DBs that we do have. In terms of the guys that we've faced thus far, we've had our good days and bad days. But I think, just collectively as a whole, that group is starting to gain confidence."
Before becoming Cleveland's head coach this offseason, replacing Kevin Stefanski, a two-time AP Coach of the Year, Todd Monken spent the previous three seasons from 2023-25 orchestrating the most prolific offense in franchise history, including what should've been back-to-back MVP-winning seasons for Jackson in his first two at the helm. Even without their star dual-threat signal caller, Monken is just as familiar with the strengths and weaknesses of several returning players on offense and defense.
"I'm not playing defense. I just know that he's going to try to give us [his] best shot, especially starting the game," Huntley said. "We have to be ready for all the different little gimmicks that he has for our game plan, and we [will] just go from there."
The Ravens have a lot of new pieces on both sides of the ball that Monken is not familiar with, a whole new scheme on offense and a slightly different scheme on defense. It's not like Jon Gruden facing the former Oakland Raiders in the Super Bowl, as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' head coach in 2002, when he knew his former team's entire playbook. Still, he has some insight into how a Huntley-led offense and overall team will approach this game because he successfully pulled it off twice last year in impressive fashion.
"[Monken] has a great game plan, and he's a great coach," Huntley said "We have to be ready to put our thinking caps on and be ready to go follow our keys and win us a game."

title: The 3 Matchups That Could Decide Ravens At Browns In Week 6
full_text:
The Ravens are probably not going to blow out the Browns.
Baltimore is just 4-4 in the last eight trips to Cleveland, and these have been almost always one-score games . With backup quarterback Snoop Huntley in for Lamar Jackson and the Ravens dealing with a looong injury list , the margins get even more slim. Divisional games tend to be tricky and this is the first one for Ravens rookie head coach Jesse Minter, while Browns coach Todd Monken, the Ravens former offensive coordinator, has already upset the Steelers.
There will be handful of plays that determine this game. The Ravens quite likely are going to need to navigate a fourth quarter in a manner that has been difficult for them going back six years. These are some matchups I will be paying very close attention to:
The Ravens are doing the right thing here and not getting cute trying to force new center Cam Jurgens into the center spot after making an utterly-desperate trade to land him while in the concussion protocol. Ioane has been better than anyone could have hoped for thrust into the center spot against elite competition and I will say it again – he is quite likely the best center on this team, already.
Mason Graham was selected in the top 10 for a reason, and he has his moments as a rookie but he is blowing people up in Year 2. He is a game wrecker, and he was dominating up until he picked up a knee injury very early in the win over the Steelers. He is listed as questionable for this game. If he plays, I expect him to be a handful. And if Ioane can handle this pass protection assignment the way he did Dexter Lawrence in his first start at center, and he helps the run game crank at the second level like it did against the Falcons the Ravens are going to win this game barring a turnover nightmare.
Graham has four sacks in four games and is tied for the lead among NFL defensive tackles. Cleveland is 30th in run defense Expected Points Added. Road grading will go a long way to winning this game.
The Ravens secondary has been a mess , there are no two ways about it, and coverage for the corners and free safeties has been bad and it’s been particularly awful in the slot where QBs are completing 74% of their passes for a 121.8 pass rating. Yuck.
Concepcion is in the slot 60% of the time he has a skillset that is in the vein of Ravens dervish Zay Flowers and Monken will have big plans for him. He can kill you with YAC and the first-round pick can win downfield, too, and with a well-balanced passing attack I’m not sure the Ravens want top corner Nate Wiggins traveling inside to the slot with him, but maybe they do.
My suspicion is that when rookie slot corner Chandler Rivers is on the field Deshaun Watson is going after him. Watson isn’t pushing it deep, his OL is not good so he will deliver it quickly and he knows how Concepcion can turn it into a big play after the catch.
Rivers has allowed nine catches on 11 targets in the last three games for 120 yards and a touchdown. Marlon Humphrey on Concepcion in the slot would be tricky unless he is jamming and beating him up at the line, but this secondary has issues. Period.
Very interested to see how Minter plays this. Fannin can be a handful and the Ravens have not been targeted much by tight ends in general this season. Do we see some Trenton Simpson here? I have issues with free safety Malaki Starks in coverage and given the volume in the Browns passing game and the quality of options he can’t focus on a one-man funnel like some of the previous offenses they faced.
Hamilton is reading the ball well underneath as are all the LBs, who have accounted for all three interceptions this season. Fannin needs to get particular attention on first down. They like taking shots with him – he isn’t a big air yards guy in general but on first down he averages 11.2 yards per catch and nearly 10 air yards per target and he is a tone setter to get drives going.

title: Breaking Down How The Ravens Should Attack The Browns With Snoop Huntley At QB
full_text:
Hopefully, two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson is back for the Ravens next week to continue his pursuit of a third such award and his first Lombardi Trophy. In the meantime, its up to veteran backup Snoop Huntley to try to manage the team to another win, this time at Cleveland.
The assignment isn’t all that different from a week ago. The Browns, like the Falcons, are getting elite pressure rates without blitzing but Cleveland has superior cover corners and more individual talent overall on defense. And unlike the Falcons, the Browns can’t stop the run at all, and even though Atlanta entered last week leading the NFL in that regard the Ravens still rolled up 200 yards on the ground against them .
Thankfully, the Ravens are not overcomplicating things by trying to force recent trade acquisition Cam Jurgens – a desperate trade by a desperate general manager – into this game as he comes back from a concussion and Huntley gets to work with the same center as a week ago. That would be surging rookie Vega Ioane ( one of their five best players thus far ) and the same offensive line, likely, for that matter, pending final decisions on the injury report regarding guard Andrew Vorhees (might as well stick with Emery Jones).
The Ravens are just 4-4 in their last eight trips to Cleveland and weird things tend to happen there and new Browns coach Todd Monken is the Ravens former offensive coordinator and will have them fired up for this game . It won’t be easy but rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, who might be on a head coach fast track if he keeps this up, had a great approach to managing Huntley through the road assignment last week and much of that will apply here, too.
No surprise the first play of the game last week was an end around for Zay Flowers, and the Ravens will hunt explosives with YAC horizontally again with Huntley wise not to break with who he is and try to force the ball downfield against these corners. He is best when the ball comes out quickly and the Browns have a legit rush – top four in pressure rate and only 20th in blitz rate.
The ball needs to come out quickly and thee could be more tackle eligible plays with the Ravens further compromised at tight end this week. Exploiting the flats and designing a few more screens for Derrick Henry, like his TD scamper last week, are in order as he is second on the team in YAC.
If Huntley starts patting the ball and holding the ball, problems will rise. Here are his career splits when under duress; he has a 27% sack rate when pressured and Jared Verse and Mason Graham (questionable) will wreck him. We could see reserve RB Justice Hill seeing his highest target rate of the season and catching 3-5 passes.
Huntley when Pressured: 48% comp, 4.9 yds/att, 62.7 rtg
Huntley When Not Pressured: 74% comp, 6.3/att, 91.6 rtg
Henry has already run 113 times – more than any age 32 running back through five weeks since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger. At some point they will need to dial it back (he is on pace for an outrageous number of carries). But not this week.
The Browns are holding teams below 60% completions and tamping down the pass game but are 30th in Expected Points Added and Success Rate vs the run. And they have had their share of injuries to the front seven and missed practices. Now’s not to the time to get too cute. Multiplicity in the run game was everything last week and should be again Sunday.
Henry is averaging 22.6 rushes/game and we suspect he touches the ball upwards of 25 times.
The Browns are playing man coverage 44.4% of the time, far and away most in the NFL. The Bears are second at 31.5% and the league average is 18%. Perhaps they change their spots but they have multiple man corners they love. Problem is, they are a blow average team in QB rating and completion percentage when in man, and Huntley has incredibly tilted splits in this regard for his career.
Huntley vs. Man : 63% comp, 8 TD – 2 INT, 8.3 Air Yd/att, 97.1 rtg
Huntley vs Zone : 70% comp, 3 TD – 8 INT, 7.1 AY/att, 79.1 rtg
Playing all that man means defenders have their back to the play quite a bit and that helps quarterbacks get extra yards on the ground. Huntley can still move pretty well, we expect his legs to be a bigger part of the plan here and the Browns are 24th in EPA vs QB runs and haven’t been tested much. We think that’s about to change. Huntley for a run of 15 yards or more and over 30 rushing yards feels about right to us.
