title: Ravens Make Determination On Lamar Jackson's Status For Sunday
full_text:
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson remained unable to take the practice field at all this week leading to him being ruled out for Week 6 with an ankle injury, while new center Cam Jurgens (concussion) and rookie tight end Matthew Hibner (hand) are also out, head coach Jesse Minter said.
Minter has continued to refer to Jackson’s ankle injury, which caused him to watch the second half of Week 4’s win over the Titans, as a “day-to-day” situation though we reported shortly after the MRI that Jackson was highly likely to miss at least two weeks . There was never any chance of him playing last week, as we heard at the time, and the odds this week were never strong and once he did not take the field at all Wednesday the Ravens began shifting them game plan for back-up Snoop Huntley, who was great in the clutch in an overtime win at Atlanta Sunday night.
The decision to take this course of action was in Jackson’s “best interest” as Minter reiterated after practice on Friday, and while he has not committed to a timetable next week, barring a setback, expect to see Jackson back on the practice field at least in some capacity Wednesday to face the Bengals in another big AFC North game.
Huntley, who spent time with the Browns last season, doesn’t get rattled, though he will be facing an elite pass rush, and the game plan is likely to be very much like last week, with a heavy emphasis on screens and horizontal passes and the perimeter run game and look for Derrick Henry, doing things no age 32 running back has ever done before to carry a heady load against Cleveland’s struggling run defense (30th in Expected Points Added vs the run)
Jurgens was in concussion protocol when Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta made a panic move to trade a second-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027, for him. Jurgens is still learning this offense, he has not even had a full practice to begin snapping regularly with the quarterbacks and he was ruled our for Cleveland with the sense Week 7 is good for him. Rookie guard Vega Ioane is set to start his third straight game at center and he has been nothing short of a revelation for this football team Hon a shaky offensive line.
Hibner was in line for a bigger role with the Ravens losing “Joker” tight end Durham Smythe for the season and with veteran tight end Mark Andrews taking 16 points off the board against the Falcons and unable to win downfield anymore . However, the hand injury he suffered last week took him off the practice field this week. Minter said the team is not considering an IR stint for the promising player and believes it is more a matter of a week or two.
Trey Hendrickson, the team’s big offseason signing , is set to return after missing two games with a procedure on his finger. He said he knew in Week 1 he would require surgery at some point after suffering the injury, and he and Nnamdi Madubuike have a chance to supercharge a sagging pass defense with more pressure after playing just 32 snaps together thus far and not with either in top form.

title: The Ravens Top 5 Players Through The First 5 Weeks
full_text:
The Ravens could easily be unbeaten after five games and the offense has performed well enough to win every game.
Of all their offseason moves, the one that looks the most sage, right now, is hiring 30-year-old Declan Doyle to be a first-time offensive coordinator and play caller. If he doesn’t have straight A’s, it’s close to it. We haven’t seen what we thought we were going to get from a defense that seemed primed to start strong Week 1 and it’s especially surprising on the back end, where rookie head coach Jesse Minter is a particular savant and with a roster that was supposed to be loaded in the secondary.
Instead, we have seen more Derrick Henry through five weeks of a season than ever before – and more carries at this point in the season by an age 32 running back since the 1970 merger – in part to help a makeshift offensive line really struggling in pass protection and in part because two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson has been out with an ankle injury – and also in large part because the defense needs a ball-control offense to help it out, struggling mightily as usual on third down and in the fourth quarter.
With all of that said, there are the Ravens top five players to this point in the season. We are weighing heavily the gravitational force of the player and an ability to impact multiple positions and do things that simply no one else on this roster can pretend to do. We are talking about players who have proved to be irreplaceable thus far and who have in some cases done things they haven’t ever done before to allow the offense or defense to function.
The rookie guard has been thrust into incredibly -challenging situations and met them all and saved the Ravens backside in the process. When they journeyman and already-injured options at center couldn’t hold up, he moves to the position mid-game in Brazil when the A gap was getting obliterated and a terrible Cowboys run defense was shutting Baltimore down.
He holds down the critical position, then shuts down All-World defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons in his first start at center the following week and holds him off the stat sheet for the second time since the start of the 2025 season. Then he triggers the return of the run game by getting to the second level and mauling people even out on the perimeter against a Falcons defense that was No. 1 vs the run entering that game. Ravens are undefeated since he took over there and he gets better every week and no way would I play Cam Jurgens there Sunday having not practiced fully with the team, but maybe they know better.
No one on the defensive line has played more snaps than him since his return from over a year out with a serious neck injury. And it’s not even that close. Him carrying a heavy load means Calais Campbell can really stay on a pitch count and Travis Jones doesn’t have to do too much.
Top edge rusher Trey Hendrickson hasn’t been healthy and/or hasn’t played at all since halftime of Week 1, and Madubuike coming in and leading the team in pressures in his first three games back at a time the overall defense was suspect and the pass rush particularly iffy, is vital. He is getting back to being himself and is as important as any player on the roster not names Lamar Jackson in the second half of the season.
We knew Minter had big plans for him, and we saw what Minter did with hybrid defender Derwin James in LA. Keeping him around the line of scrimmage has been critical; he leads the team with two interceptions and was in a linebacker role on both of them, with the ball not traveling 10 yards downfield in the air when he picked off Tua Tagovailoa to end Sunday’s game (linebackers have all three Ravens picks).
His ability to man so many different spots from play to play has allowed Minter to experiment and try to hide other flaws in this unit, especially in coverage. Hamilton’s pressure rate hasn’t been great but he also hasn’t had the chance to blitz opposite Hendrickson much yet. He is a glue guy and connective tissue on a defense that would be lost without him. Ravens getting picked apart in the slot when he’s not there.
Imagine what the offense would look like is he wasn’t limited to less than 100 routes run on the season so far? In a brand new offense predicated on hunting explosive plays, he remains the only guy really delivering downfield with even a modicum of consistency and he’s doing it like never before. That pre-season contract extension looks pretty brilliant right now .
Doyle is putting him in motion more than ever before and putting him the slot 50% more than ever before and he’s already shown up more in the redzone than ever before. His chemistry with Jackson is uncanny and he seems primed for the best receiver campaign in franchise history if he can remain remotely healthy.
Looks well on his way to a another MVP-worthy campaign and could it be he wins an MVP in his first full season with an offensive coordinator for the third straight time? As awesome as Doyle’s stuff looks, try executing it without the best player in the NFL and especially when you are winging it at center from week to week.
Every reason to believe he is back in Week 7 from the ankle injury – as we told you all along – and picks up where he left off.
Jackson is leading the NFL with 10.1 yards per attempt, he is leading the NFL in play-action, passer rating (155.8, perfection!), and he is tops in the NFL with a 119.6 passer rating overall. That’s without having anyone really winning downfield except Flowers and despite a hit-or-miss run game and despite the OL issues and despite his legs even really entering the equation as much as they will.

title: The 1 Development For The Ravens Defense That Could Change Everything
full_text:
Baltimore Ravens defensive players have combined to play 3410 total reps over 310 plays.
Care to guess how many have included their two most accomplished pass rushers on the field at the same time?
Precisely 32, totally nondescript snaps in which $30M edge rusher Trey Hendrickson, the team’s primary offseason acquisition , was on the field with $20M former All-Pro defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike, who missed the first few games of the year coming back from a serious neck injury suffered last September. Since Madubuike started getting his legs back, Hendrickson required surgery on a painful finger injury, and Sunday could be their first extended run together.
Hendrickson shouldn’t need an extended pitch count only missing a few weeks and Madubuike is far and away Baltimore’s leader in snaps played at the LOS over the last three games since he’s returned. It stands to reason that Sunday in Cleveland marks the first time we see both at close to full strength (pending how Hendrickson performs if still in a cast or apparatus of some sort). And they are facing a Browns offensive line that has had major issues and quarterback Deshaun Watson is being sacked on nearly 12% of his dropbacks, second-worst in the NFL.
Seems like the perfect time for Madubuike to register his first sack since his neck surgery, does it not?
“Every game, every practice, I'll say I feel better and better,” Madubuike said this week. “Getting better. I really feel the same, honestly. I am just thankful to be back playing football and with the guys and making plays. There are things we can clean up and we are going to continue to emphasize that and get better at that, but no, I feel good."
He is already doing some impactful things, and Madubuike leads the team in pressures since returning to action and he has allowed other players to fall into a deep rotation and take on heavy responsibilities, drawing double teams and showing that he can still collapse a pocket. At a time when the Ravens cornerbacks and free safeties are most definitely struggling no matter how they might want to couch it in Owings Mills. Getting Madubuike and Hendrickson going and working some stunts and games up front could go a long way to adding bite to a defense suffering greatly on third down.
Hendrickson was a beast in Week 1, with Madubuike still watching, but suffered the finger injury during that game and was not as dynamic or impactful off the edge before the decision was made to have his finger operated on prior to Week 4. This is someone who routinely posted elite pressure and sack rates with the Bengals, and is expected to be a difference-maker week in and out and be that late game “closer” rookie head coach is desperate for inheriting a defense notorious for fourth-quarter collapses (and they stink in the fourth quarter this season thus far).
"I needed it Week 1,” Hendrickson said of the surgery. “I've had two healthy quarters here. It's not what I planned for the offseason, but God has a plan. It's one of the things that is very humbling, but [I was] pushing through it through Week 2 and Week 3, but the best decision for everybody was getting it fixed for [the] long-term and short-term."
Hendrickson said that he is in significantly less pain after the surgery but was less specific about whether he will need to have his hand clubbed up for some period of time moving forward.
“That's obviously an ongoing process, so we're just working it out," he said.
Just getting these two on the field for regular work at the line of scrimmage will be a big deal.
The Ravens are currently 20th in the NFL in pressure rate and 21st in sack rate. Tavius Robinson has been their most consistent sacker of the quarterback. All of that should start to change soon enough.

title: All Signs Point To This QB Starting For Ravens In Week 6
full_text:
Ravens two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson has yet to practice in any capacity since injuring his ankle at the end of the first half in a win over the Titans in Week 4, making it increasingly clear who is starting against the Browns Sunday no matter how the team has chosen to couch it.
Talking about the possibility of Jackson playing after not practicing is one thing; doing it is another and rookie head coach Jesse Minter has been decidedly conservative with medical decisions to this point – to his credit – and it would be fairly stunning if Jackson is not ruled out on Friday as he was last week. If the Ravens chose to list him as questionable, given it’s a division game and they want to crate some disbelief in the Browns, they can do that as well, but we would be astonished if Jackson suits up for this game no matter how his ankle feels over the weekend.
From the moment he was first injured we strongly suggested he would be back Week 7 against the Bengals, and nothing that has occurred to alter that conclusion, despite what Minter has hinted and what those ever willing to get used for quasi-stories are willing to “report” (I mean parrot). A player of this magnitude playing the position the way Jackson does, and doing so this early in the season with an injury that is easily aggravated never made sense on any level, and the fact he hasn’t even been limited in real practices – Wednesday and Thursday – tells you all you really need to know.
The situation is further complicated by the fact that new center Cam Jurgens – who general manager Eric DeCosta panicked in acquiring - has never even snapped with Jackson off to the side. And Jurgens has only practiced limited as he gets cleared from concussion protocol and Minter has repeatedly talked about the veteran playing Sunday, though personally I would let rookie Vega Ioane man the position and actually field the same starting offensive line two weeks in a row for the first time all season.
“I think it probably is a much bigger challenge than people understand, because the general public might not know all the things that go into that job,” offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said of trying to bleed Jurgens in under duress. “One, it's a new guy in the building, so he has to get integrated with his teammates. He has to learn the playbook and the new terminology.
“Football is football, but communication's such an important part of that. He has to learn our language and how to speak our language so that he can get the other five guys up front going in the right direction.“
Yeah, I’d punt on that until next week when Jackson is back to practice fully and so if Jurgens. But that’s only the start of the injury riddle. So Snoop Huntley starting at QB appears painfully obvious, but the Ravens and their medical team have plenty to still sort through.
As to who will catch the football, rookie tight end Matthew Hibner, an ascending player who would ideally begin to phase out fading veteran Mark Andrews , has not practiced all week with a hand injury he suffered in Atlanta. Premier blocking tight end Durham Smythe has already been lost for the season. Minter talked down Rashod Bateman’s shoulder situation earlier in the week, but he went from limited participant to doing nothing on Thursday, never a good sign.
Top receiver Zay Flowers, absolutely joining the elite in the NFL this season , went from finally not showing up on the injury report with his hamstring issue to be listed as limited with a toe injury Thursday.
On defense, pass rusher Mike Green was added to the report as limited with a hamstring and breakout linebacker Trenton Simpson is limited with a hamstring as well and defensive tackle Broderick Washington went from limited to not practicing at all with an ankle.
On the bright side, $30M edge rusher Trey Hendrickson should be removed from the report tomorrow as he has practiced fully all week returning from a procedure on his finger.

title: Ravens Least Experienced Corner Could Be Most Vital Sunday vs Browns. Here's Why
full_text:
If the Ravens were facing Zay Flowers in some parallel universe, and he was lining up in the slot, which of Baltimore’s defensive backs do you think would draw the coverage responsibility?
Who would share enough commonality in terms of build and twitch and leverage to be able to hang with a jitterbug like that, or attempt try to hang with a jitterbug like that, where he has a two-way go and the entire middle of the field to work? Most likely, that would be rookie nickel corner Chandler Rivers. And while Cleveland’s rookie wideout KC Concepcion is not at the level of Flowers, Browns head coach Todd Monken, former Ravens offensive coordinator , is using him inn] a very similar way and Cleveland’s diverse passing attack is stacked in ways that present Baltimore’s sagging secondary potentially serious problems.
Monken will come at Baltimore with vigor – the Ravens are bracing for as much – and they will be throwing the ball quite a bit and there will likely be multiple match-ups that decide this game on this side of the ball. But it stands to reason that Rivers, a fifth-round pick, and Concepcion, who was selected 24th overall, will see quite a bit of one another and while Rivers has done some very nice things as a rookie and has great instincts reading screens and wrapping up when the play is in front of, like the rest of this allegedly-elite secondary, he has been picked up in coverage in recent weeks and it’s a major issue for this team across the board .
The Ravens tackling in the secondary has suffered and the Browns defense is heavily reliant on yards after the catch (8th in the NFL in YAC/reception) and Concepcion is someone with the athletic skillset to burn you just that way.
“You have to take great angles,” Ravens coach Jesse Minter said of the challenge. “You have to be super detailed when you're tackling these guys in the open field — attacking the right hip with the right leverage, knowing where your help is.
“You're never out there by yourself, and so it's knowing, if he does cut back or you miss it, where's your help, and where are those things at? It's a detail game in open-field tackling. They do a great job with the ball after the catch … Good group of skill players that can make plays, and a challenge we're excited about."
The Ravens corners have been bad in coverage against mostly marginal quarterbacks to this point, as we have been documenting. Ravens corners and free safeties in coverage:
Opposing QBs: 70/100 (70%), 836 yards (11.9/comp), 5 TDs – 0 INTs, 111.9 rating
13 passes 20+, 41 1st downs, 3 DPI, 4 pass breakups
Yeah, that sucks. But it gets even worse when you drill down on what happens in coverage on targets who come from the slot:
Opposing QBs : 37/50 (74%, 24th in NFL), 9.1 yds/att (23rd), 3 TD – 0 INT, 121.8 rating (25th).
Concepcion is in the slot on 60% of his snaps, far and away most on the Browns.
He does the most damage from the slot. And overall, he sees 20% of the team’s targets, tied with fellow rookie Denzel Boston, with elite move tight Harold Fannin at 18% (running back Quinshon Judkins is next at 14%). The Ravens don’t usually move corners around with someone, but could bring top outside corner Nate Wiggins into the slot for Concepcion. However, that might create bigger problems on the outside, and Minter has been very reticent to use veteran Chidobe Awuzie out there and probably for good reason.
“We don’t necessarily have to travel to people,” defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver noted on Thursday in discussing this difficult match-up for his secondary.
Rivers is playing quite a bit, he is a quintessential slot guy, and in the last three weeks he’s allowed nine catches on 11 targets for 120 yards and touchdown. Gulp.
The Ravens also have struggled to defend No. 1 wide receivers all season and when they did face one team that had two real wideouts who could win – Dallas – both got off on this defense. The return of top pass rusher Trey Hendrickson from a finger injury should add juice to the pass rush, but the Ravens are going to keep hearing questions about receivers getting over on them until they do something about it.
“We’ve had our good days and our bad days,” Weaver suggested, which is whimsical and all but not quite true. And Monken is uniquely qualified to spot their underbelly and knows most of these players quite well and we suspect Rivers will be in his sights.
Since Week 2, here is what quality receivers have done to this defense:
Drake London (ATL): 7/11, 118 yards, 7 1st D
Carnell Tate (TEN) : 9/12, 145 yds, 6 1st D
CeeDee Lamb (DAL): 7/8, 112 yds 5 1st D
George Pickens (DAL): 7/11, 82 yds, 4 1st D
Chris Olave (NO): 8/10, 86 yds, TD, 6 1st D
The Browns are very aware. Monken knows .
“They have some guys that can stretch the field and do some things in short areas,” corner Marlon Humphrey said of the Browns. “They have a lot of talent over there, and it will be all -hands-on-deck to try to kind of contain the offense."

title: Bills Would be Wise to Claim Rookie Linebacker Released by Texans
full_text:
Linebacker has been one of the weakest positions for the Buffalo Bills this season. They have been leaning on Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams, but rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr has been proving himself worthy of more snaps lately as well .
As for their starters, Bernard and Williams have each had issues adapting to Jim Leonhard's defense. That's why Bills On SI's Ralph Ventre gave the position group as a whole a C- after the first quarter of the season. Ventre says that "Bernard has looked slow while Williams appears confused at times," and believes the Bills should consider bringing up Shaq Thompson from the practice squad or giving Joe Andreessen more snaps.
Buffalo could also look for more depth, and an intriguing name just became available. On Saturday, Jordan Schultz reported that the Houston Texans would be releasing rookie Aiden Fisher, who will be available to claim on Waivers. The Bills aren't high on the priority list, but they should put in a claim and attempt to bring him in.
Sources: The #Texans are releasing rookie LB Aiden Fisher. The 7th-round pick was an All-American last season en route to helping Indiana win a national championship. He will be on waivers. pic.twitter.com/3f9YR4GCI0
Fisher was a seventh-round pick out of Indiana and has appeared in three games this season. He has 38 snaps, all on special teams, and has recorded just one tackle.
He began his collegiate career at James Madison before transferring to Indiana in 2024. He was vital to their title run in 2025 and finished his two years with the Hoosier with 215 tackles, 16 tackles for loss, six sacks, and two interceptions.
What should stand out with Fisher for the Bills is his high football IQ. During the pre-draft process, NFL.com scout Lance Zierlein praised Fisher for being a coordinator on the field , saying he can run a defense.
"Fisher is a Mike linebacker who can run the defense as an extension of his coordinator. He’s well-built with leadership and football character that are praised by teammates and coaches. Fisher has the instincts and feel of an NFL player but lacks the needed quickness and athletic ability," Zierlein wrote. "He reads play designs and gets to the action at a high rate, but a lack of range, cover talent and plus open-field tackling will make the NFL jump challenging."
The lack of range and coverage skills are what led to Fisher sliding into the final round, and could be a reason for the Bills to be concerned. That said, his intelligence and leadership make him worth taking a flier, especially as Leonhard is looking for players who fit his vision.

title: Bills OLB Bradley Chubb Fined Following Altercation With Alaric Jackson
full_text:
There was some drama on the field following the Buffalo Bills thrilling overtime win over the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5. As players were shaking hands after the game, there was an altercation between Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson and Buffalo outside linebacker Bradley Chubb.
Jackson was initially suspended two games for throwing a punch, but that was reduced to one game. Chubb was not suspended for his part, but the league still decided to punish him.
According to Mike Garafolo, the NFL fined Chubb $14,329 for taunting Jackson.
Also, the #Bills ’ Bradley Chubb was fined $14,329 for taunting in his postgame exchange with the #Rams ’ Alaric Jackson that led to Jackson striking Chubb. https://t.co/vHFBzKJkQP
Chubb admitted to starting the conversation with Jackson, who was doing a jersey swap with Deone Walker. Chubb accused Jackson of "front-running," which is to say he began to talk trash when it appeared the Rams were going to win.
Once Buffalo fought back and stole the victory, Chubb felt the need to say something to Jackson and told reporters exactly what he said to the Los Angeles offensive lineman.
"I'll tell you exactly what I said," Chubb told reporters Wednesday, according to Nick Suss of ESPN . "I've heard I was talking about his mom. That's not true at all. I said, 'We're gonna see y'all's ass again. And when we see you again, all that chipping ain't gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.' He said, 'What'd you say?' I said, 'That chip's not gonna save you. The guard's not gonna save you.' And then boom."
Chubb was a prized free-agent signing for the Bills, agreeing to a three-year, $43.5 million contract during the offseason. The former Denver Broncos first-round, who also spent time with the Miami Dolphins, has appeared in all five games this season. Chubb has 17 tackles and 1.5 sacks for the Bills.
Considering his salary, the Bills expected more from Chubb. The veteran outside linebacker currently has a PFF grade of 56.5 , which is 81st out of 106 qualifying EDGE rushers.
Of course, Buffalo has been able to lean on Greg Rousseau , who is in the midst of a breakout season. Rousseau, who blocked the field goal that allowed the Bills to defeat the Rams, has 20 tackles and six sacks through five games. If Buffalo can get Chubb rolling alongside Rousseau, it would go a long way toward fixing their defensive woes.

title: Four Defensive Changes Bills Must Make to Floundering Unit in Week 6
full_text:
The numbers aren't pretty.
The Buffalo Bills ranks 30th overall amongst their NFL peers in total defense (388.6). They are permitting 28.3 points per game, and their pass defense (280.4) is next to last on the circuit.
First-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard knows the results must change sooner than later .
"It's a simple game if you really cut it down to it, of execute, play with your leverage, play with your technique," said Leonhard this week. "Once you handle your responsibility, you haul ass to the football. Like it can be that simple and I think we got to get back to the fundamentals of that."
With the Bills visiting the Las Vegas Raiders for a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff on October 18 in Week 6, here are four adjustments that could improve the defense's production.
While Buffalo's pass rush has been adequate, the back end has been victimized for 13 touchdown passes while making only two interceptions over five games.
There are plenty of instances where the Bills' defensive backs and linebackers are allowing excessive separation to opposing receivers. Some of the problem appears to stem from giving too much cushion at the snap while there are other times when Buffalo defenders are too easily beaten.
“We have to get more production on the ball. There's no question about it," said Leonhard. "We got to find ways to get more production on the football, and I have to help them get closer to routes, and understanding how we're trying to get attacked, get these guys a little bit closer to receivers."
Starting outside cornerback Maxwell Hairston, a 2025 first-round draft pick, has appeared most vulnerable in one-on-one coverage, and he's shown a tendency to play too far off opposing receivers.
After a nightmarish performance in the Week 4 loss to the New England Patriots, Hairston was not in the Week 5 starting lineup despite head coach Joe Brady claiming there's been no change on the depth chart.
On Monday Night Football, second-round rookie Davison Igbinosun started in Hairston's spot , seeing 84 percent of snaps. He's more of a physical presence than Hairston, and the Ohio State product plays with a contagious confidence.
"IGB has the right mindset. He's a fighter. I've talked about it a bunch. He's not perfect. He's a young guy growing," said Leonhard.
It's time to let Igbinosun grow on the job.
In a contract year , starting inside linebacker Dorian Williams has underwhelmed, particularly when dropping back in pass coverage.
Opponents have caught two touchdowns against Williams while passers are completing 83.3 percent of targets thrown his way.
We made the case for the Bills to sign practice squad linebacker Shaq Thompson to the active roster, and plug the veteran into the starting lineup. More likely, however, may be an increase in snaps for fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr .
Although Brady wouldn't admonish the team's linebacker performance thus far, he mentioned the possibility of more Elarms-Orr in the coming weeks.
"I like where the linebackers are at right now. They're continuing to get better. I'd love for Kaleb to play a little more than he played the other day," said Brady.
The Bills' defense, which is running a new 3-4 scheme under Leonhard, has admitted to difficulty communicating, especially pre-snap.
Slot cornerback Dee Alford even went as far as blaming home crowd noise as a factor.
"Sometimes, the game can be loud and super loud to the point where we not able to get the play that fast [when] we need it," said Alford after the 29-26 loss to the Patriots in Week 4.
Whether it's at home or on the road, the Bills need to clean up the communication to minimize missed assignments moving forward.
"I mean, we, as a football team, we got to continue to improve. Our communication isn't where it needs to be right now," said Brady.

title: Bills RB James Cook Hit With Fine Despite Avoiding Penalty During Rams Game
full_text:
While the Buffalo Bills are completely focused on their Week 6 showdown with the Las Vegas Raiders , the NFL is looking back at their Week 5 win over the Los Angeles Rams .
The Monday Night Football showdown went to overtime and the Bills escaped with a narrow win. James Cook III was a hot topic during the win, mainly because of his two fumbles . One of those was lost, and happened to come in overtime, nearly costing the team the game.
That wasn't the focus for the NFL, however, as the league was worried about a play during the first quarter when Cook lowered his helmet while initiating contact. He wasn't penalized during the game for the play, but according to Mike Garafolo, the league office fined him $21,167 for using his helmet. Cook's fine was one of six in the NFL for using the helmet.
#Bills RB James Cook was fined $21,167 for use of the helmet on this play. No flag. In all, six fines across the league for use of the helmet in Week 5. pic.twitter.com/NPQoJEwnqU
Cook might have had problems holding onto the ball, but he was still able to put up impressive numbers. He finished the night with 111 yards and two touchdowns on 25 rushing attempts. On the season, he now has 532 yards and five touchdowns while averaging 5.6 yards per attempt.
As dangerous as Cook has been with the ball in his hands, he's also had more than his fair share of struggles with ball security. His two fumbles on Monday brought his season total to four, which is highly concerning after he had six in 2025.
Head coach Joe Brady touched on the problem following the win. He stated that he had faith in Cook, even giving him the ball again after his late fumble. He did add that something needs to change, because they can't stay patient forever.
"I have all the confidence in him, that's why I put him right back out there," he said of Cook . "But, obviously, at some point there has to be consequences to when we're putting negative stuff out there."
"That can't happen and at some point it's going to cost us football games, and it almost cost us one. And so, it's got to improve or the carries are going to decrease."
It's easy to overlook the fumble thanks to the win, but had it not been for a blocked field goal by Greg Rousseau, the tone surrounding Cook might be vastly different entering Week 6.

title: One Bills' Reporter Casts Serious Doubt on DJ Moore and Ed Oliver's Statuses For Week 6
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills once again have two key players uncertain to suit up in Week 6 in wide receiver DJ Moore and defensive tackle Ed Oliver.
Moore has been dealing with a sprained AC joint since Week 2 and he did not play last week after re-aggravating the injury in Week 4. Meanwhile, Oliver has been bothered by a knee injury that forced him to miss Week 5, also.
In Week 6, both players are questionable ahead of Sunday after they only logged a single limited practice during the week.
While the questionable tag gives both a chance to play, WGR 550's Sal Capaccio believes neither one will suit up for Buffalo because the team will opt to rest them this week, which will allow for yet another week of rest and rehab with the bye coming up the following week.
"My feeling is no. Not playing, that's my feeling, that he wouldn't play," Capaccio said of Moore . "He wants to play. We know that, right? He wants to play, that's just in his nature.
"But, guys, I mean, they went to L.A. and won a game without him, still scored 37 points... And then, they have a bye next week. It doesn't seem like it's smart to put him on the field unless he's actually truly healthy enough."
Capaccio then said he thinks Oliver is in the "same boat" as Moore in regard to the Bills wanting to get him the extra rest.
When asked about the statuses of Oliver and Moore on Friday, head coach Joe Brady made it clear the team is taking a wait-and-see approach and wouldn't commit to either one playing.
"They've been doing a lot on the side. They've been doing all the walkthroughs and everything. It was good to get them out here today, and just being able to move around," Brady said . "We'll see how they field coming off the field. Look at it on tape. See what it looked like and have discussions. I say it every week, if they're ready to go, they're gonna play."
This make sense on both accounts. The Bills are sitting at 4-1 and have the luxury of taking the long-term approach and sitting two of their best players to make sure they're healthy the rest of the way and avoid more serious issues.
It's especially important the Bills take this approach with Moore, who may not be fully healthy the rest of the season based on a report last week from NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe .
"Bills WR DJ Moore is inactive tonight vs. Rams after aggravating AC sprain in his left shoulder," Wolfe reported on Moore after he was officially inactive in Week 5. "Hope is more rest will help him with shoulder throughout the season."
Adding to all that, the Bills are fully capable of beating a struggling Las Vegas Raiders team without Moore and Oliver on the field.

title: New Bills 2027 Mock Draft Lands Vertical Playmaker at WR
full_text:
Wide receiver has been a position of need for the Buffalo Bills ever since they moved on from Stefon Diggs ahead of the 2024 season. They did land DJ Moore in a trade with the Chicago Bears this offseason, but as his recent shoulder injury has reminded us, the depth behind him is still concerning.
That's why wideout is still a popular position for Buffalo in many 2027 NFL mock drafts. That's where they go in Round 1 of a recent mock from Pro Football Sports Network's Alec Elijah.
At No. 28 overall, Elijah has the Bills selecting Cam Coleman out of Texas , a wideout who has become one of the best in the nation after transferring from Auburn.
Buffalo likes what they've seen from Moore, but injuries have kept him sidelined. Khalil Shakir has continued to shine, but he's a slot receiver and not someone who stretches the field. Coleman, however, can do that, and was called a vertical playmaker by Elijah.
"The Buffalo Bills found a legitimate No. 1 option for Josh Allen when they brought in DJ Moore, but beyond Moore and Khalil Shakir, the receiver room still lacks a true difference-maker, especially after the Keon Coleman experiment has failed to pan out. Cam Coleman is the No. 3 receiver on PFN’s big board with an 89.1 prospect grade, and landing a talent of his caliber this late in the first round is a coup for Buffalo," Elijah wrote.
"Coleman has been efficient in a Texas offense that spreads the ball around, catching four touchdowns while earning an 88.2 PFN WR Impact Score against one of the toughest schedules in the country. At 6-foot-3 and 200 pounds, he is a vertical playmaker with the speed to get behind defenses and the body control to win in contested situations, and he would give Allen a dangerous boundary weapon to pair with Moore for years to come."
Throughout the first five games of the year for Texas, Coleman has 318 yards and five touchdowns on 17 receptions. He's averaging an impressive 18.7 yards per catch , which is the exact type of threat the Buffalo offense needs to take its next step.
Adding Coleman along with Moore and Shakir would give the Bills a trio of wideouts capable of hurting defenses, and gives them the depth they will need to navigate through any injuries in future years.

title: Three Areas of Concern for Bills in Week 6 Road Matchup vs. Raiders
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have had an interesting week in the National Football League.
After narrowly escaping with a nailbiting victory against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on Monday Night Football to end Week 5, which included a feisty postgame altercation between Bills’ outside linebacker Bradley Chubb and Rams’ left tackle Alaric Jackson , the team had little time to celebrate.
Immediately after the overtime thriller, Buffalo’s coaches and players quickly jetted down to the UC Irvine campus in Orange County to prepare for their next matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders slated for Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET at Allegiant Stadium.
The Bills head into the game currently holding the best record in the AFC East following their most recent win.
For the Raiders, though, it's a sticky situation that they find themselves in after two straight AFC losses against the Kansas City Chiefs and Patriots, which comes on the heels of a surprising 3-0 start.
Undoubtedly, first-year head coach Klint Kubiak’s group will be motivated to avoid a three-game skid, and it’ll take a full 60-minute effort—if not even more— from Bills’ quarterback Josh Allen and Co. to come away victorious on the road once again.
Here are three areas of concern for Buffalo regarding the team’s ability to accomplish that very goal before its Week 7 bye.
So far this season, the Bills have struggled with turnovers , particularly over the past three weeks against the Los Angeles Chargers, New England Patriots, and Los Angeles Rams.
Surprisingly, or maybe not so much for those paying close attention, quarterback Josh Allen and running back James Cook III have been the main culprits for the miscues on offense , particularly during this past three-game stretch where Buffalo is losing the turnover battle by a ratio of 1:3, meaning the offense is turning the ball over three times as much as the defense is forcing any turnovers of its own.
For perspective, the Bills have turned the ball over nine times in their last three matchups while forcing just three of their own . . . which makes the turnover ratio seem even more worrisome given the glaring number of offensive mishaps recently.
The team will need to shore things up in that department moving forward, but it’ll be a tough task to do so in Week 6 against Las Vegas, a squad that currently ranks 11th in the league with a turnover differential of +3.
Meanwhile, Buffalo is ranked 24th in that specific statistic with a turnover differential of -4 through five weeks.
And, given that the team seemingly isn’t moving in a positive direction with its turnover struggles, it’s definitely an area that the Raiders could wind up taking advantage of on Sunday afternoon out West.
Holding on to the ball will be key for the Bills.
So far this fall, outside of a few bright spots , Buffalo’s defense has been horrendous. And, new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard isn’t shying away from the criticism.
In fact, Bills ON SI recently highlighted Leonhard’s comments regarding his unit’s pitiful display on the field to start the season, and Leonhard certainly didn’t mince his words: changes appear to be on the way .
But, even with that said, those significant shifts might not occur until after the upcoming bye given the short week Buffalo currently finds itself in following a much-needed victory on Monday.
So, the defense could still be pretty shaky on Sunday against Las Vegas, and a major area of concern will be how the AFC West squad chooses to attack the Bills with their top two tight ends.
Entering Week 6, Brock Bowers (24 receptions, 312 yards, 3 TDs), who is second in the NFL for receiving yards at his position, and Michael Mayer (21 receptions, 171 yards, 1 TDs) have combined to make 45 receptions for 483 yards and four touchdowns thus far.
Furthermore, third-string tight end Ian Thomas has even registered four receptions for 52 yards and one touchdown.
It’ll be up to safeties Cole Bishop and C.J. Gardner-Johnson, as well as Buffalo’s linebacking corps , to keep both players in check. So far, though, that hasn’t been the case.
The Bills, as a whole, have allowed 28 receptions for 300 yards and one touchdown to opposing tight ends in 2026.
Although Buffalo’s offensive line hasn’t been terrible by any stretch of the imagination this season, the unit has been a bit more productive in terms of run blocking versus pass blocking, which has seemingly always been the case since Josh Allen has been the franchise quarterback in Western New York.
So far this season, Buffalo’s offensive front has given up 10 sacks through five games, which is currently tied for the 12th worst in the NFL for sacks surrendered.
On the opposite side, Las Vegas’ defense ranks 10th in the league with a total of 13 sacks, and that’s with superstar edge rusher Maxx Crosby accounting for just two quarterback takedowns right now. Crosby does, however, possess a pass-rush win rate of 27% according to ESPN 's database, which ranks eighth in the NFL right now.
In addition to that scary fact, his teammate Malcolm Koonce—an alum of the University at Buffalo who happens to lead the Raiders with three sacks—also posseses a pass-rush win rate of 24%, which currently ranks 19th in the NFL. For comparison, despite leading the league in total pressures according to Pro Football Focus , as well as being second in the NFL in sacks with six, Bills' veteran outside linebacker Gregory Rousseau isn't even in the top-20 for pass-rush win rate.
Needless to say, the Raiders will be looking to get after Allen behind the line of scrimmage on Sunday, and it will be prudent that the Bills’ offensive line keeps him upright.

title: Bills, Chargers Viewed as Possible Trade Match With Buffalo's Need at Cornerback
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have some question marks at the cornerback position in 2026 and the Los Angeles Chargers might be a team capable of helping them out with that issue.
Buffalo's cornerback play has not been inspiring this season, as Maxwell Hairston, Davison Igbinosun and Dee Alford have all experienced struggles.
Making matters worse, the group has had Injury issues and that's another stark reminder that Buffalo could use more depth at the position.
As a result of all that, the Bills are sporting the second-worst pass defense in the NFL, which simply isn't sustainable, for a team with Super Bowl aspirations. That's why general manager Brandon Beane should explore the trade market for help.
CBS Sports' Jared Dubin listed one trade deadline proposal for all eight of the top Super Bowl candidates this season and he matched Buffalo with the Los Angels Chargers and their cornerback, Tarheeb Still.
"The Bills definitely need help in the defensive backfield, and the slot is the most obvious place for an upgrade," Dubin said. "They're playing Dee Alford there, for the most part, and according to Pro Football Focus, he's allowed opponents to complete 12 of 17 passes for 197 yards when throwing his way lined up inside."
"Still has lined up both outside and in the slot for the Chargers and played well in both roles, but especially when kicked inside," Dubin adds. "Opponents are just 7 of 12 for 53 scoreless yards targeting him there. With the Chargers struggling, maybe they're willing to part with him for a draft pick."
The Chargers are sitting at 0-5 and unless they make NFL history, they aren't going to the playoffs in 2026.
With Los Angeles heading toward a disappointing season, they may hold a fire sale in order to garner some draft capital as the team potentially looks to retool in 2026.
With Still having one more year on his contract and playing well this season, he could fetch a good enough return that Los Angeles considers moving him.
Thanks to his inside/outside versatility, the Bills can deploy Still in whichever spot they deem the biggest problem, whether that be on the boundary or in the slot.
Still, who has played 88 snaps in the slot and 144 out wide in 2026, is giving up a completion rate of 52.9% and a passer rating of 84.4 when targeted, according to Pro Football Focus , and he sports a coverage grade of 77.5, ranking ninth among qualified corners.
All of those numbers are superior to the ones Hairston, Igbinosun and Alford are putting up, so he could very well amount to an upgrade for defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's defense. Acquiring Still would also beef up the Bills' depth.
If the price is right (we figure Still will garner a fourth-round pick, at most), the Bills absolutely should pull the trigger on a trade for Still, who could be a multi-year solution for Buffalo.

title: Bills' Final Week 6 Injury Report: DJ Moore, Four Others Questionable to Face Raiders
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have ruled five players as questionable to face the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6.
After wrapping up practice at UC Irvine on Friday, the Bills issued their final injury report prior to the October 18 road game.
Wide receivers DJ Moore and Josh Palmer, defensive linemen Ed Oliver and TJ Sanders along with slot cornerback Dee Alford are all uncertain to dress on Sunday. The other 10 players listed are all cleared to face the Raiders for the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.
One of the 10 without a game designation is starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who left the Week 5 win , and did not return, after 16 snaps due to a back flare-up.
Brown practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday before improving to full participation on Thursday and Friday. With a  minor "muscle freak out" now in the rearview, the starting right tackle is ready for his 79th regular season appearance in a Bills' uniform.
"Just tweaked it. Nothing major. Disc looks fine. Had an MRI. Looks better than it did last year. Long-term wise that's good to hear," said Brown after Wednesday's practice at UC Irvine.
In another positive development, running back Ty Johnson, who was limited by a hamstring at the first two practices, participated in full on Friday, and he's been cleared for the Sunday game.
Moore and Oliver both sat out the October 12 win over the Los Angeles Rams after injury incidents knocked them out of the October 4 loss to the New England Patriots.
Neither player participated at practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but both returned to the field in a limited capacity on Friday, providing a glimmer of hope that they'll be available for kickoff.
"They've been doing a lot on the side. They've been doing all the walkthroughs and everything. It was good to get them out here today, and just being able to move around," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady . "We'll see how they field coming off the field. Look at it on tape. See what it looked like and have discussions. I say it every week, if they're ready to go, they're gonna play."
Moore sprained his AC joint when hitting the ground during the Week 2 win over the Detroit Lions. He was active in Weeks 3 and 4, but reaggravated the injury against the Patriots. Missing his first game since December 2020, it's likely Moore is itching to play in some capacity on Sunday.
Oliver took a hit to the knee area at the end of a play near the sideline in Week 4. Although it appears to be only a minor injury, the Bills may exercise caution by sitting him again with a Week 7 bye waiting on the other side.
After being scratched in Week 5, Alford and Palmer logged limited participation all three days this week. The former is nursing a minor ankle issue that emerged against the Patriots. The latter is fighting through a shoulder injury from an October 9 practice.
Both Alford and Palmer showed positive signs throughout the week, looking ready to return to game action, by multiple accounts, during media-viewing portions of practice.
Sanders, who has already dealt with a knee issue and a subsequent bout with appendicitis, made his season debut on October 12. He performed well over 51 defensive snaps, but apparently came out of the overtime win bothered by a shoulder. He progressed to full participation at Friday's practice, but remains questionable to play.

title: Five Key Things to Know About Bills vs. Raiders in Week 6
full_text:
When last we saw the Buffalo Bills, it took more than four quarters for Joe Brady’s club to outlast the Los Angeles Rams, 37-34, at SoFi Stadium this past Monday night.
From a long evening to a long afternoon. Last Sunday, the Las Vegas Raiders were in Foxborough to battle the defending AFC champions. The New England Patriots scored early and often and Klint Kubiak’s squad was on the wrong end of a 45-17 blowout.
The Raiders have dropped consecutive games to the Chiefs and Patriots after a 3-0 start. Meanwhile, Josh Allen and company look to maintain their one-game lead in the AFC East with their third road victory in six weeks.
This is another one of those original AFL series that dates back to 1960. And when you include the team’s postseason victories in the 1990 AFC title game (51-3) and the ’93 divisional round (29-23), the Bills own a 22-21 lead in the overall standings.
Dating back to 2017, Buffalo has won three consecutive meetings by a combined 102-47 score. The Bills have scored at least 30 points in each of those victories. The clubs’ last meeting took place in 2023, with the Bills coming away with a 38-10 triumph. Meanwhile, the Raiders took it on the chinstrap, 30-23, six years ago the last time they hosted this series.
The team has a new defensive coordinator this season in Jim Leonhard. However, this year’s unit is off to a very shaky start. Brady’s club has already surrendered 141 points (31-plus in 3 games) and 18 offensive touchdowns. During last season’s 4-1 start, Buffalo allowed 113 points and gave up just 13 offensive TDs.
A season ago, the Raiders ranked a respectable 14th in the league in total defense and pass defense in terms of yards allowed. The club gave up 45 offensive TDs while coming up with just 16 takeaways. In five games this season, Las Vegas has already forced 10 turnovers—nine in three wins and one in two losses.
A season ago, Buffalo’s James Cook became the Bills’ first player since Hall of Famer O.J. Simpson in 1976 to lead the NFL in rushing yards. This season, he’s averaging 106.4 yards per game on the ground. But he’s put the ball on the ground four times in five games (2 lost)— much to the chagrin of the team’s head coach.
While Ashton Jeanty has reached the end zone just twice in 2026, both touchdowns via the air, the sixth overall pick in the NFL draft entered Week 6 ranked 10th in the league in total yards from scrimmage (506). Jeanty leads the Raiders in rushing yards (291) and is also second on the club with 22 receptions.

title: Panthers Have a Chance to Answer One Huge Question Against the Eagles
full_text:
Beating the Detroit Lions before the bye felt like a big moment for the Carolina Panthers. They didn't just sneak out with a win, either. Carolina put 32 points on the board, Bryce Young and the offense made plays, and the Panthers went into the bye at 2-2 with some momentum.
Now comes the part that might tell us even more about this team. We've seen Carolina have good moments before, but turning those moments into something that lasts has been the problem. That's what makes Sunday's trip to Philadelphia so interesting.
The Panthers are coming off their best win of the season, had an extra week to get healthier, and now face an Eagles team that has lost three straight. Jalen Hurts is out, Tanner McKee will start in his place,  and Saquon Barkley missed multiple practices with a hamstring injury.
None of that means Carolina can just show up and expect to win. Philadelphia still has plenty of talent on both sides of the ball, and McKee has been in that offense long enough to know what he's doing. But there's also no reason to pretend this isn't a pretty good opportunity for the Panthers.
Carolina is getting healthier in some important spots, too. Jalen Coker was a full participant Thursday after missing the Detroit game, while Young also practiced fully despite being listed with a knee injury. Taylor Moton practiced in full as he continues working toward his return.
The Panthers don't need another moral victory here. If this team really is starting to turn the corner, going on the road and taking advantage of a struggling Philadelphia team is the kind of game it needs to win.
That's really what Sunday is about for me. Beating Detroit was impressive, but one good game doesn't tell us much if Carolina turns around and gives it right back two weeks later. The Panthers have a chance to show that what happened before the bye was something they can actually build on.
Carolina doesn't need to do anything crazy against McKee. Get pressure on him, don't give Philadelphia cheap opportunities, and make a quarterback with only two NFL starts beat you for four quarters. McKee has played well when he's gotten opportunities, so the Panthers can't treat Hurts being out like an automatic win.
That's where I think this game is a little different than Detroit. Nobody expected Carolina to have an easy time in that one. This week, the Panthers are facing a struggling team without its starting quarterback, and there's going to be an expectation that they take advantage of it.
That wouldn't suddenly mean Carolina has everything figured out. At 2-2, we're still talking about a team with plenty left to prove, and four games isn't enough to erase everything we've seen over the last few years. But stacking another good performance on top of what we saw against Detroit would be another sign that maybe things really are starting to change.
The Panthers looked like a good football team against Detroit. Going into Philadelphia and backing it up would show us a little more.
For me, that's what Sunday is really about.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: The Panthers Can't Just Beat the Eagles — They Need to Show Us These 4 Things
full_text:
Let's get the obvious part out of the way. If the Panthers win 10-9 on a last-second field goal Sunday, nobody is going to care how ugly it looked.
A win is a win, especially on the road.
But coming out of the bye, I do want to see a few things from Carolina. The Panthers looked good in the 32-26 win over Detroit, and now they're getting an Eagles team that has lost three straight and won't have Jalen Hurts.
I'm not expecting Carolina to go into Philadelphia and dominate. I just want to see some of the things we saw against Detroit carry over. Here are four things besides a win that I'll be watching for Sunday.
This one is pretty simple. Don't let McKee come out, complete six or seven easy passes, and suddenly start looking like a guy who's been starting all season.
McKee has played well when he's gotten opportunities, so I'm definitely not saying he's some quarterback Carolina can ignore. But there's a big difference between getting a few chances here and there and having Derrick Brown and this Panthers defense coming after you for an entire game.
I'd like to see Carolina get after him early. Make him move around, speed up some throws, and don't give him a bunch of easy completions to get going.
If McKee gets comfortable early, I could see this turning into a much tougher afternoon than it needs to be.
Jalen Carter is the guy up front who worries me the most. He already has three sacks through five games and is coming off a two-sack game against Jacksonville, so Carolina knows exactly what it's dealing with.
A lot of that responsibility is going to fall on the middle of the Panthers' offensive line. Damien Lewis and Robert Hunt could both get Carter, depending on where Philadelphia lines him up, and Luke Fortner is going to have to help when needed.
And that's the problem with Carter. Philadelphia can move him around and look for the matchup it likes. Carolina can't just point at one offensive lineman and say, "He's your problem all afternoon."
Lewis being limited Thursday with an elbow injury is worth keeping an eye on, too. I'm not expecting Carolina to keep Carter out of the backfield all day because that's probably not happening.
Just don't let him take over the game.
Give Young some time and see if he can pick up where he left off against Detroit.
I'm not saying Carolina needs to come out and run the ball 15 straight times. But if the Panthers are picking up four, five, or six yards per carry early, please don't suddenly decide it's time to throw it all over the place.
That makes things easier on Young and, just as importantly, keeps Carolina out of third-and-forever with Carter and the rest of that Eagles front knowing exactly what's coming. Nobody wants to see Young dropping back on third-and-11 all afternoon.
The Panthers had an extra week to figure out how they want to attack Philadelphia. If they find something that works on the ground, stick with it until the Eagles give them a reason not to.
Sometimes it really doesn't need to be more complicated than that.
This might be the biggest one for me. How many times over the last few years have we gone into a Panthers game just hoping they'd hang around long enough to have a chance late?
Carolina just beat Detroit, Philadelphia has lost three straight, and Hurts isn't playing. I'm not saying the Panthers should walk into Lincoln Financial Field thinking this is going to be easy, because that's probably how you end up getting beat.
But they shouldn't walk in there hoping to steal one, either.
Take care of the football. Don't kill drives with dumb penalties. And if you get a chance to put Philadelphia in a hole early, do it instead of letting the Eagles hang around all afternoon.
There are going to be mistakes Sunday, especially on the road. That's football. But Carolina shouldn't need everything to go perfectly to win this game.
Detroit was fun, and the Panthers deserved a lot of credit for that one. Now we get to see if they can come out of the bye and give us another one.

title: Panthers-Eagles Suddenly Means Something — These 3 Matchups Could Decide It
full_text:
This isn't exactly where most people expected the Carolina Panthers to be heading into Week 6.
Carolina is 2-2, coming off a bye and heading to Philadelphia with a chance to put itself right in the middle of the early NFC playoff conversation. The Eagles are only 2-3 and have lost three straight, so this game looks a whole lot different than it did when the schedule came out.
Then Thursday changed things even more.
Jalen Hurts was ruled out with a superficial blood clot, meaning Tanner McKee will get the start for Philadelphia. That obviously helps Carolina, but I'm not ready to act like this suddenly becomes an easy road win.
The Eagles still have plenty of talent, and Carolina hasn't exactly reached the point where we should expect them to walk into Philadelphia and win. If the Panthers are going to come home 3-2, these are the three matchups I think will have the biggest say in whether it happens.
Let's start with Young because, at this point, how could we not?
He's playing the best football of his career, throwing for 1,268 yards and nine touchdowns through four games. He hasn't thrown for fewer than 287 yards in a game this season, and Carolina is averaging more than 30 points per game.
I've spent the last few weeks trying to figure out what's really changed for Young this season . Whatever the answer is, he looks more comfortable in this offense than he has at any point since Carolina drafted him.
Philadelphia should give us another pretty good idea of where Young is right now. According to the Panthers' preview of the Eagles , Philadelphia has allowed 222 passing yards per game. The Eagles don't blitz a ton, but they've still been able to generate pressure with four rushers on 32% of their opponents' dropbacks.
That's the part I'll be watching.
Young has looked comfortable in this offense and has done a much better job of taking care of the football. But if Philadelphia can get pressure without having to send extra guys, things could get a little tougher.
If Young gets time, though, I like Carolina's chances of moving the football. Tetairoa McMillan is coming off a 192-yard game, Jalen Coker is back, and Darren Waller can't be overlooked.
That's a lot more for a defense to worry about than Carolina had around Young earlier in his career.
If there's one guy on Philadelphia's defense who worries me, it's Jalen Carter.
Carter already has three sacks through five games, matching his total from all of last season. He also had two strip-sacks against Jacksonville last week, and he's one of those guys who can completely screw up what an offense wants to do if you let him get going.
Carolina can't let that happen.
That's easier said than done when Young has already been pressured on nearly half of his dropbacks this season. He's handled it better than anyone could've expected, but asking him to keep surviving that kind of pressure every week probably isn't the best plan.
There is some good news up front. Taylor Moton was a full participant in Thursday's practice as he works his way back, although rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling remained out with a knee injury.
Carter is still going to put plenty of pressure on the middle of Carolina's offensive line. This is where Robert Hunt and the rest of that group have to make sure Young isn't spending the afternoon with Carter in his face.
It matters for Chuba Hubbard, too.
Hubbard finally got going against Detroit with 122 yards and two touchdowns. If Carolina can keep Carter out of the backfield, it gives Hubbard a chance to build on that game and keeps the Panthers from putting everything on Young.
Nobody is going to completely erase Carter for four quarters. Carolina just can't let him take over the game.
This matchup became a whole lot more interesting Thursday afternoon.
The Panthers spent most of the week preparing for Hurts before learning that McKee will start Sunday . He hasn't played this season, but this isn't his first time on an NFL field. McKee has appeared in six games with two starts, throwing for 597 yards, five touchdowns and only one interception.
So no, I'm not looking at this like Carolina automatically gets a win because Hurts isn't playing.
What the Panthers need to do is make McKee beat them. Saquon Barkley has been dealing with a hamstring injury and missed practice Wednesday and Thursday. If he plays, Carolina can't let Philadelphia lean on him all afternoon and make life easy on its backup quarterback.
I'd much rather see McKee staring at third-and-8 than third-and-2.
That's where Derrick Brown and Carolina's defensive front come into this. Philadelphia has gone through plenty of changes up front, and the Panthers have a chance to make McKee uncomfortable if they can slow down the running game and put the Eagles in obvious passing situations.
Carolina's defense has been hard to figure out all season. I recently wrote about how this defense somehow makes absolutely no sense , but we've also seen this group come up with stops when it absolutely had to.
McKee might play well. He's done enough in limited opportunities that Carolina has to respect him, but there's a difference between respecting a backup quarterback and letting him settle into the game.
Make him uncomfortable and see what happens.
I'm not calling a Week 6 game a must-win because that's going way too far. But let's not pretend this isn't a pretty big opportunity for the Panthers.
Before the bye, I wondered whether Carolina's 2-2 record might be lying to us . Philadelphia was the game I wanted to see before deciding just how seriously we should take this team, and I still feel that way.
The Panthers are coming off a bye, Philadelphia has lost three straight and the Eagles will be without their starting quarterback. Carolina has spent the first month of the season making people look at this team a little differently, and going into Philadelphia and winning would only add to that.
It probably comes down to the same things most games do. Protect Young, don't let Philadelphia's best players wreck the afternoon and make the backup quarterback uncomfortable.
Do those three things, and 3-2 would look pretty good heading back to Carolina.

title: Panthers-Eagles Betting Outlook: A Wild Line Swing & 3 Props That Stand Out
full_text:
What a difference a few days can make for the Carolina Panthers. They started the week as underdogs heading into Philadelphia, but then Jalen Hurts was ruled out with a superficial blood clot, and the betting market quickly shifted toward Carolina. Suddenly, the Panthers are getting a level of respect we haven't seen much of lately.
Reuters reported Thursday that Hurts will miss Sunday's game and Tanner McKee is expected to start in his place. I'll admit, watching what happened to the line after that news made me do a double take. But once you get past the initial shock, some of these numbers aren't as crazy as they might look.
Bryce Young has been dealing, Tetairoa McMillan just went off for 192 yards, and Chuba Hubbard finally got rolling against Detroit. So I went through the numbers at DraftKings Sportsbook , and a few immediately caught my attention.
Philadelphia opened as a 1.5-point favorite at DraftKings Sportsbook, but that didn't last. After the Hurts news broke, Sports Illustrated's betting team reported that the line swung five points, moving Carolina all the way to a 3.5-point favorite. The number has continued moving since then, which shows just how much uncertainty Hurts' absence has created around this game.
Do I completely trust Carolina as a road favorite yet? I'm not there, because this is still a 2-2 Panthers team, and Philadelphia still has plenty of talent even without Hurts. The Eagles have dropped three straight, though, while Carolina went into its bye after beating Detroit 32-26.
There's another reason I don't think we can chalk the entire shift up to Hurts being out. Carolina has scored 121 points through four games, the most the franchise has ever scored over the first four games of a season. The Panthers have actually done something to earn some of this respect, and let's be real, we haven't been able to say that very often lately.
Young's passing-yard total is hovering around 240 yards at DraftKings Sportsbook , and this was probably the number that surprised me the most. According to the Panthers' official statistics , he's thrown for 1,268 yards through four games, which comes out to 317 per game. That's a pretty big gap between what Young has actually been producing and the number we're seeing for Sunday.
It gets even more interesting when you look at his game-by-game totals. Young has thrown for 361, 287, 291, and 329 yards, meaning his lowest output of the season is still well above Sunday's number. Four games isn't a huge sample, but he's been remarkably consistent throwing the football so far.
There is something that gives me pause, and that's how this game could unfold with McKee starting instead of Hurts. If Carolina gets ahead early, Dave Canales may not need Young throwing it 35 or 40 times. Still, we've spent years wondering whether Young could consistently push the football downfield, and now we're looking at a number around 240 yards and wondering why it isn't higher.
Hubbard finally looked like Hubbard against Detroit, carrying the ball 20 times for a season-high 122 yards and two touchdowns while averaging 6.1 yards per carry. The Panthers' official stats have him at 306 yards on 61 attempts this season, an even 5.0 yards per carry. His rushing-yard total was listed at 71.5 at DraftKings Sportsbook in Thursday's published odds.
My first reaction was that 72 yards doesn't seem like much after what we just watched against Detroit. Then I went back and looked at Hubbard's first three games, and he didn't reach 70 yards in any of them. That's why this number isn't nearly as simple as it first appears.
I'm not ready to assume one big afternoon suddenly means Carolina's running game is fixed. At the same time, if the Panthers are playing from ahead Sunday, this could turn into exactly the kind of game where Canales keeps feeding Hubbard and tries to shorten things in the second half. Of all the numbers I looked at, this is probably the one I could talk myself into either direction on the easiest.
Good luck figuring out what to expect from McMillan after what he just did to Detroit. He caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns, and the Panthers noted in their Inside the Numbers breakdown that he became the first player in franchise history with at least 10 catches, 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns in the same game.
He enters Sunday with 26 catches for 385 yards through four games and is averaging 14.8 yards per reception.
His receiving-yard total was listed at 66.5 at DraftKings Sportsbook in Thursday's published odds. Nobody should expect another 192-yard afternoon every week because that's ridiculous, but 66.5 is a completely different conversation. Young clearly isn't afraid to look his way, and McMillan has already shown he can turn a handful of opportunities into a big afternoon.
What I like about McMillan right now is that Carolina doesn't have to force everything his way. Jalen Coker is back, Darren Waller has become another option for Young, and suddenly defenses have several guys they have to account for. If Carolina continues spreading the ball around, McMillan might actually get some better opportunities instead of seeing his production disappear.
After watching him put up 192 yards, I'm not trying to guess what he's going to do for an encore. I'm more interested in seeing how Philadelphia decides to defend him and whether Young keeps looking his way when the Eagles start adjusting.
That's the question I kept coming back to while looking through all of this. The Panthers went from underdogs to favorites on the road against the Eagles, Young has a passing-yard number that somehow feels low, Hubbard is coming off 122 yards, and we're already wondering what McMillan can possibly do for an encore.
Think about where this franchise was not that long ago, and those are some pretty wild conversations to be having.
I'm not ready to say Carolina has arrived because four games isn't enough for that. Philadelphia also isn't suddenly a pushover because Hurts isn't playing, and McKee has played well enough in limited opportunities that Carolina can't just show up and expect to win. There are still plenty of reasons to be cautious about this matchup.
But there does seem to be something different about this Panthers offense. Maybe it's Young taking another step, maybe it's finally having legitimate weapons around him, or maybe it's simply what happens when a young team starts believing it can score with anybody. Whatever it is, the betting market has noticed too, and now Carolina gets another chance Sunday to show whether that respect is deserved.

title: Bryce Young Isn't the Panthers' Biggest Question Anymore
full_text:
For almost three years, every conversation about the Carolina Panthers eventually came back to the same question: Is Bryce Young good enough?
I've asked it plenty of times myself. After what we watched during his first couple of seasons, I don't think it was an unfair question. Carolina took Young No. 1 overall, and at some point, you needed to start seeing something that made you feel better about that decision.
Four games into this season, I'm starting to wonder if we've been asking the wrong question. Young has thrown for 1,268 yards, nine touchdowns, and only two interceptions. He's thrown for at least 287 yards in every game, Carolina is putting points on the board, and we're no longer spending every Monday trying to figure out what's wrong with the quarterback.
That's a pretty big change from where we were not that long ago. Young has spent most of his career trying to prove he's good enough for the Panthers. Maybe now it's time for the Panthers to show they're good enough to do something with him.
I'm not going to pretend four good games erase everything that happened before this season. They don't, and there's still a lot of football left. But Young is playing really good football right now, and I don't know how else to put it.
We wanted him to push the ball downfield more, and he's doing it. We wanted him to take better care of the football, and he's doing that, too. More than anything, we wanted to see an offense that didn't look like it was scared to put the game in his hands, and we're finally getting that.
It's not like everything around him suddenly became perfect, either. Young has been pressured on nearly half of his dropbacks , and he's still putting up the best numbers of his career. That's probably what has impressed me the most.
For the longest time, I wondered what Young would look like if Carolina just gave him some help. Now Tetairoa McMillan looks like a legitimate No. 1 receiver, Chuba Hubbard is coming off a 122-yard game, Jalen Coker is back, and Darren Waller has been sneakily good. Carolina finally gave Young some guys to work with, and he's making it count.
He just looks more comfortable out there, too. Young talked recently about how much input offensive coordinator Brad Idzik gives him during the week, and I wrote about how different things seem for Young in this offense . Maybe it's the weapons, maybe it's another year in the offense, or maybe Young is simply getting better. It's probably a little bit of all of it.
Whatever the reason, it's working. For most of his career, it felt like Carolina was trying to figure out whether it could win with Young. Now he's becoming one of the biggest reasons they're winning.
That's what makes Sunday in Philadelphia so interesting to me. I'm not saying beating the Eagles suddenly makes Carolina a Super Bowl contender. We're four games into the season, and nobody needs to get carried away yet.
But if you want people to start taking you seriously, these are the games you eventually have to win. Philadelphia has lost three straight, Jalen Hurts is out, and Tanner McKee will start in his place. Carolina is coming off a bye after beating Detroit 32-26, so you couldn't ask for a much better opportunity.
That's really what I want to see from Carolina now. We've spent years talking about patience, development, rebuilding, and waiting to see what Young becomes. Well, we're starting to get our answer, and now the Panthers have to do something with it.
Protect him better. Keep putting weapons around him. Give him a defense that doesn't make him feel like he has to score every time he touches the ball. When you get a chance to go on the road against a struggling team playing without its starting quarterback, take advantage of it.
That's why Sunday feels like a little more than just a chance to get to 3-2. I don't need Young to throw for 350 yards and four touchdowns to convince me he's playing well. He's already spent the first month of the season answering most of the questions I had about him.
Now I want to see what Carolina does with it.
If this version of Young is what we're going to keep seeing, the conversation around the Panthers has to change with him. For years, we kept asking whether Bryce Young was good enough for Carolina.
Maybe it's finally time to find out if Carolina is good enough for Bryce Young.
