title: Final Panthers Injury Report: Latest Updates on Jaelan Phillips, Bryce Young & More
full_text:
Ahead of the Carolina Panthers ' Week 6 matchup vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , Carolina's roster has key pieces returning, while others may not be able to suit up.
The biggest positive of this week has been the confirmation that WR Jalen Coker will return . Coker was forced to leave the Panthers' Week 3 game against the Cleveland Browns in the second half. The injury kept Coker off the field for Carolina's Week 4 victory against the Detroit Lions.
Aside from that news, the status of major players such as EDGE Jaelan Phillips, RT Monroe Freeling, and others remains up in the air. Here's the latest on who could be in and out of the lineup on Sunday afternoon.
Freeling suffered a knee injury during Carolina's Week 4 victory over the Lions. The injury sidelined Freeling for the rest of the game, and he left the medical tent wearing a brace. Freeling was a limited participant in practice, according to the latest injury report.
Carolina's offensive line is already thin, and with Freeling trending towards missing Sunday's matchup, sixth year veteran Stone Forsythe will take on the starting right tackle spot.
Another Week 4 exit. Phillips left the game against Detroit in the fourth quarter and was checked for a concussion and a hamstring injury.
Head coach Dave Canales said he was "hopeful" that Phillips would be ready for Sunday during the bye week. Hamstring injuries are notoriously tricky and can linger, making them very easy to re-aggravate.
Still remaining "questionable" on Friday isn't a great sign. It seems like Phillips' status won't be solidified till closer to the game.
AJ Dillon's ankle injury came up during the Week 5 bye. It's clearly something that is semi-serious, as Dillon didn't participate in any of this week's practices leading up to Sunday afternoon.
With Dillon out, RB Tre Tyus has been elevated from the practice squad to the 53-man roster for Week 6. Tyus's debut is also due to RB Trevor Ettienne being listed as questionable after being activated from IR this week.
Bryce Young has been listed on the injury report with a knee injury throughout this week. However, he fully participated in Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday's practices.
QB1 no longer has an injury designation and is ready to keep his hot start to the season going.
Damien Lewis suffered a UCL tear in his elbow during the first half of Carolina's Week 3 loss. After missing Week 4, Lewis has trended in the right direction during the bye and throughout this week.
In Friday's report, Lewis was listed as a full participant in practice. This is a great sign that he could return to protect Bryce Young and bring back starting-level talent and experience back to the offensive line.
Anything other than "OUT" is a welcome sign for Moton and the Panthers, as he hasn't played a down of football this season due to multiple blood clots in his right lung.
Blood clots are terrifying, not just when it comes to playing football. It's a serious health issue that can be lethal if not taken care of properly. Moton's 21-day practice window was opened this week, as he's off IR and seems to be ramping up towards a season debut.
It wouldn't be shocking if Carolina still waited this week out and kept Moton on ice.

title: Bryce Young Is Making His Doubters Look Silly & Even PFF Is Buying the Hype
full_text:
It wasn't that long ago that it seemed like everybody had something to say about Bryce Young, and most of it wasn't good.
He was too small. He couldn't push the ball downfield. The Panthers made a mistake taking him No. 1 overall. We heard all of it, and to be fair, there were times during his first couple of seasons when it was hard to argue back.
Now here we are four games into the season, and things around Young feel a whole lot different. He's playing the best football of his career, Carolina's offense is putting up points, and even Pro Football Focus is starting to buy into what we're seeing.
In its latest NFL quarterback rankings , PFF has Young at No. 9 in the league.
Seeing Young inside the top 10 caught my attention, but his actual PFF grade might be even more impressive. Young has an 88.6 overall grade, which trails only Lamar Jackson among quarterbacks through the first five weeks.
And really, it's hard to argue with what we've watched so far.
According to the Panthers' official statistics , Young has completed 101 of 162 passes for 1,268 yards, nine touchdowns, and only two interceptions. He's averaging 317 yards per game and has a 100.0 passer rating.
PFF has also given him an 85.2 passing grade, which ranks fourth among qualified quarterbacks. He's been credited with eight big-time throws and only one turnover-worthy play through 176 dropbacks.
That last number might be the one that stands out the most to me. Young is making plays down the field without putting the football in danger very often, and that's something we haven't always been able to say about this offense.
What makes the PFF ranking even more interesting is where the conversation was before the season. Back in August, PFF's Panthers season preview called this a pivotal season for Young. There were still questions about just how good he could be and whether Carolina had seen enough to eventually make a long-term commitment to him.
Those were fair questions at the time, but four games into the season, Young is starting to answer some of them. He's not just showing flashes anymore. He's putting together good games week after week, and Carolina finally looks like it has an offense that can make teams pay through the air.
We've spent most of Young's career talking about what he couldn't do. So far this season, he's giving everybody a lot more to talk about when it comes to what he can do.
That's probably the biggest thing I've noticed about Young so far. There hasn't been one ridiculous game carrying his numbers.
He threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns against Chicago, then followed that with 287 yards and three more touchdowns against Atlanta. Young threw for 291 yards against Cleveland before putting up another 329 yards and two touchdowns in Carolina's 32-26 win over Detroit.
His lowest passing total through four games is 287 yards, but the consistency is what stands out to me. We've seen Young have good stretches before. What we haven't seen enough of is him coming back the next week and doing it again.
It also doesn't hurt that Carolina finally has some weapons around him. Tetairoa McMillan already has 385 receiving yards, Jalen Coker has 222, and Darren Waller has given Young another option in the passing game.
That's a big difference from some of the offenses Young had around him earlier in his career. Defenses have more than one guy to worry about now, and Young is taking advantage of it.
I'll admit I've been pretty cautious with Young. Every time he had a big game, it was easy to say, "OK, let's see him do it again." Then he'd have another one, and we'd basically say the same thing the following week.
At some point, you have to give the guy his credit.
I'm not saying four games suddenly answer every question about Young. There's a lot of football left, and eventually he's going to have a bad game. Every quarterback does.
But I also don't think we can keep brushing this off as just a nice little stretch.
PFF has Young ranked ninth among NFL quarterbacks. His 88.6 overall grade trails only Lamar Jackson, and he's thrown nine touchdowns against two interceptions while averaging 317 yards per game.
That's not just hype anymore. Young is playing really good football, and through four games, he's given Panthers fans plenty of reasons to believe this might be more than just a hot start.
Now we get to see if he can keep it going.

title: Panthers Trade Deadline Big Board: Realistic Targets Ranked by Fit and Cost
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have what a lot of Super Bowl-level teams have: an elite offense . After four games, it's fair to say that. Things are clicking in an unforeseen and unprecedented way for this team.
They are not, however, without weaknesses. They need more out wide with rampant injuries, and the offensive line has been depleted and the remaining players have almost all been bad.
The defense has some major question marks, too. The cornerback situation is borderline untenable. The pass rush still lacks firepower. The run defense is improving, but it has been gashed before.
But knowing the talent on defense and the production of the offense, the Panthers have a real chance to make some noise. So, it wouldn't be a shock if they traded for someone to boost their NFC South and eventual playoff chances.
Xavier Legette is on IR, and Jalen Coker has either missed or come away hurt in every single game this season. We can't keep asking Bryce Young to throw to John Metchie in crucial situations. So unless Legette's return is imminent and Coker's going to suddenly stay healthy, the Panthers could use a wide receiver.
Jerry Jeudy is expendable from the Cleveland Browns, who drafted two top wide receivers this year. A projected conditional fifth-round pick is not too high a price for this need, even if Panthers legend Steve Smith hates Jeudy.
The Philadelphia Eagles are tearing it down up front after sending Cam Jurgens to Baltimore and seeing Lane Johnson retire. Many believe Howie Roseman isn't done, and that Landon Dickerson could be on the move, too.
The Panthers make so much sense. He'd cost a lot, but the Panthers' line has been awful, and Damien Lewis is hurt. Robert Hunt has been surprisingly bad. Adding an interior lineman would be a great way to bolster this ailing unit.
Josh Sweat has seemingly been on the trade block forever. We've discussed him as a possible target for the Panthers for a long time, and as the deadline inches closer, he remains a possibility. He won't be the cheapest addition, though.
The Panthers, despite signing Jaelan Phillips and getting a good year out of Princely Umanmielen, do not have a reliable pass rush. They're middle of the pack, but the rush goes silent at bad times. They also have just eight sacks, the fourth-fewest in the NFL.
Plus, Phillips is banged up, Patrick Jones has been in and out, and Umanmielen is a one-note defensive player. Sweat would be a nice addition.
All of the above applies here to Josh Uche, the Miami Dolphins' edge rusher. The Panthers could use some help, but maybe they don't need a star, per se. Uche would be much cheaper since he's a vested veteran on a bad team. He's also much more likely to be moved.
Speaking of the Dolphins, linebacker Willie Gay Jr. is also a vested veteran. Now, the Panthers have Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke, both of whom have enjoyed stellar starts to the 2026 NFL season. But depth is a concern.
When Lloyd was out, the defense struggled against a bad Cleveland Browns offense. The depth is simply not there, especially after losing Claudin Cherilus. Gay could be a nice, cheap addition to bolster a thin spot on defense.
Analysts like Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report have noted that Donte Jackson makes a lot of sense for the Panthers. They're not wrong. The former Panthers cornerback would be an immense help while Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn are out.
The Chargers are bad , and Jackson likely isn't in future plans (also a vested veteran), and while he hasn't played with the Panthers in a while, he has one season under Ejiro Evero, so there's some history that means this could work.

title: Ranking Panthers Players Most Likely to be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is approaching , and it's unclear what route the Carolina Panthers will take. Will they go for it and buy as they try to defend their NFC South crown ? Will they stand pat like last year? Could they offload some assets?
Teams are often not specifically buyers or sellers, often working as both. The Panthers feel like a team that could move some players and bring others in. If they do, these five have to be considered as trade options.
Rasheed Walker will probably not be traded. It's like a 99.9% probability. But, there is a world where it happens. Walker has not been great in pass protection on the left side. If Taylor Moton comes back, Monroe Freeling loses his spot.
It's a tough sell to start and then bench your prized draft pick, especially when he was meant to be on the other side of the line. Walker's cheap, so a team in desperate need of a tackle might trade for him, allowing the Panthers to keep developing Freeling where he's meant to play.
Despite our cries, Luke Fortner remains the starting center . But, that could (and should) change very soon. Sam Hecht deserves a spot. And while depleting the center depth would be unwise, the Panthers could use Brady Christensen as the backup.
This is essentially moving on from Fortner because he's been unplayably bad so far, but centers don't grow on trees, and some team might be willing to part with a late-round draft pick for the added depth up front.
When pressed into action, John Metchie III has been remarkably solid. Could that be a good reason to move on? He's on a one-year deal, and he's ordinarily the WR5. He doesn't play special teams, and WR-needy teams might pounce.
This all depends on the health of Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette. If Coker comes back fine and Legette returns from IR as soon as possible, then Metchie becomes more expendable. If not, he's going to have to stick around.
At some point, the Panthers are going to get Jonathon Brooks back. This week, Trevor Etienne could be back. The space for AJ Dillon is dwindling. He has proven to be a solid player still, so he could have some value.
We're mostly thinking that if Dillon gets traded, it'll be to the RB-needy Green Bay Packers, his former team. If not, then he'll probably be cut and moved to the practice squad, but there may be a team or two willing to fork over a future seventh-round pick.
Ja'Tavion Sanders is still young with some upside, but he has no future with the Panthers. They keep scratching him despite being totally health. Tight end is crowded, and he doesn't bring anything to the table.
A young player who won't cost much is always a good candidate to be traded, so even if the Panthers do buy at the deadline, Sanders will probably be sent packing.

title: Chargers Could Have Answer to Panthers' Defensive Woes with Familiar Face
full_text:
There are three winless teams in the National Football League, all in the AFC, and two of them are certainly no surprise. The Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans both come off losing campaigns in 2025, the latter tied for the worst record in the league.
Then there are the Los Angeles Chargers, who dropped to 0-5 last Sunday with their third home loss in five weeks. A 23-17 setback to the Denver Broncos means that Jim Harbaugh’s club is the lone member of the AFC West with a losing record. Hence there’s been plenty of speculation on whether the tea, a playoff participant the previous two season, is ready to blow things up in the coming weeks?
Two such speculators are C arter Bahns of CBS Sports and Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report . Among the numerous players mentioned by both writers is a veteran cornerback who could certainly help Dave Canales’s first-place team.
Donte Jackson was a second-round pick by the Carolina Panthers back in 2018. After six seasons in Charlotte, he was traded to the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2024. He came up with a total of six takeaways, including a career-best five interceptions, in his lone season with the Black and Gold.
In 2025, he signed a two-year deal with the Los Angeles Chargers. He played in all 17 games, totaled four picks and a dozen passes defensed. Knox feels that both the first-place Panthers, who are currently shortahnded at cornerback, and the Buffalo Bills are possible landing places for the nine-year pro.
“Teams may not be eager to make a move for Jackson until he's clearly healthy (hamstring),” stated Knox, “but he's a player worth targeting before November 10. The Los Angeles Chargers appear to be going nowhere this season after a 0-5 start and numerous injuries across the roster. Jackson, meanwhile, plays an in-demand position and is set to be a free agent in 2027—trading him would save L.A. $6 million in 2026 cap space.”
“Jackson started 15 games for the Chargers last season,” added Knox,” and allowed an opposing passer rating of only 56.8 in coverage.”
This season, he has been limited to just 113 defensive snaps in four games, and sat out last week’s clash with the Broncos. He’s totaled eight tackles, two passes defensed and one forced fumble this season.
Of course, the Panthers are dealing with the losses of starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, both players currently on injured reserve. Knox projects that Jackson could be had for a fifth-round draft choice in 2027.
Then again, all of this is contingent on the Chargers bailing on the current season. The team is off to its worst start since 2003. Meanwhile, the Panthers off to their best start since 2021, and look to hold down the fort until Horn and Jackson can get back on the field.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Trip Attempt by Bears Kicker Against Packers Draws No NFL Fine
full_text:
Bears kicker Cairo Santos made an obvious attempt to trip Packers return man Matthew Golden on the sidelines Sunday but apparently this legwork wasn't as impactful as his field goal kicking normally can be.
Santos drew no fine from the NFL for the attempt in the Bears' 31-7 loss to Green Bay .
Trips can draw a basic first-offense fine of $8,190, but Santos didn't technically make the trip, as Golden avoided it.
Santos earned more than his share of Packer fan criticism on social media for the attempt to stick a foot out and get Golden.  Bears-Packers games normally produce their share of chippy play but that one was both comical and unncessary.
#Bears kicker Cairo Santos with a dirty play trying to trip #Packers WR Matthew Golden after the play pic.twitter.com/5ORYKVwZ1K
Neither player seemed to concerned about the situation and Santos even made comments during the week at Halas Hall to this effect.
However, Santos didn't seem the only player worthy of being fined on the play. Golden took the punt and ran out of bounds, then unnecessarily ran about 25 yards on the Bears sidelines. Players have been fined in the past in the NFL for unnecessarily running through the opponent's bench, or penalized for taunting. Golden then carelessly ran into a Bears assistant coach, knocking him to the ground. This was when Santos stuck his leg out in an attempt at the trip.
Despite what seemed an obvious taunting attempt and the needless crash with a coach, Golden was not fined, either. Taunting fines can draw $11,941 fines for a first offense.
In the overall scheme of things, the fine and conduct by Santos probably did nothing more than generate a few chuckles at Halas Hall, or maybe even some pats on the back, considering the high level of rhetoric being exchanged between the teams both before and after the game. Ben Johnson's provocative comments last year about wanting to beat Packers coach Matt LaFleur twice no doubt added to that atmosphere.
Another look at the sideline incident that led to a penalty on Jameson Williams and now a fine for Tyrique Stevenson. pic.twitter.com/JvC7cXRsSN https://t.co/qnthvMymef
The Bears have been involved in other sideline exchanges in the past that resulted in either a penalty or a fine or both. Tyrique Stevenson was fined over $19,000 for a trip on Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams along the sidelines in 2024, a play in which Williams drew a taunting flag.
The Bears have not managed to avoid fines completely this season.
Notice how he celebrated on the sideline without assaulting any coaches like @MatthewGolden_ Pure class https://t.co/OhawYkZKRL
Tyrique Stevenson was fined $22,342 in Week 2 against the Vikings for unsportsmanlike conduct/using his helmet in a tackle. The other Bears fine for game conduct was $5,620 for unsportsmanlike conduct in Week 1.
In addition, cornerback Jaylon Johnson received $5,971 fine from the NFL against the Eagles for a uniform policy violation, involving wearing an unapproved streamer towel.
The Bears escaped a fine of any type for linebacker D'Marco Jackson when he put a hit on Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts at the sidelines just as he stepped out of bounds in Week 3.
Packers WR Matthew Golden appeared to intentionally knock over a Bears coach on the sideline and Bears K Cairo Santos tried to trip him out of retaliation. (🎥: NFL on FOX) pic.twitter.com/wK4DqcuGs1
Gene Chamberlain has covered the Chicago Bears full time as a beat writer since 1994 and prior to this on a part-time basis for 10 years. He also has worked a prep sports writer for Tribune Newspapers and Sun-Times newspapers.

title: Bears' Caleb Williams Makes Official Return from Injury in Week 6 vs Falcons
full_text:
For the first time since Week 2, the Chicago Bears will finally have their starting quarterback under center. According to NFL insider Mike Garafolo , Caleb Williams has passed all the tests for his injured hamstring and is good to go for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.
Though Bears fans widely expected Williams to be back after a full week of practice, and especially after he reposted an electric hype video on social media, it has to feel good to get this official confirmation. The Bears went 2-1 in Williams' absence, a good record for any team to hit without their starting quarterback, but a disastrous Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers reminded everyone just how badly Williams is missed.
While he's always played with something of a chip on his shoulder, one has to believe that Williams is coming into tomorrow's game with a vengeance. His hamstring injury created memes and jokes across all social media, most of which were unfair and wildly ignorant. Critics and podcasters created a bizarre narrative that Williams, who had started and finished 35 consecutive regular season games before his injury, was soft and not built for the NFL.
While that is quite literally adding insult to injury, it didn't stop there. Backup quarterbacks Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent both led the Bears to one win apiece in Williams' absence, which fueled wild theories about whether the Bears even needed Williams. It was as if the central role he played in the Bears' 59-point Week 1 thriller against the Carolina Panthers had never happened.
But, as aforementioned, the Bears' 31-7 shellacking at the hands of the Packers should have served as a bucket of cold water over the heads of anyone who still entertained such ridiculous notions. The Bears' offense is severely limited without No. 18 under center, and no one is more eager than Williams himself to prove that on the field.
Williams' return in Week 6 felt like a sure-thing ever since he landed on last Friday's injury report as 'Questionable', but now it's confirmed. The former No. 1 overall pick from the 2024 NFL draft is back and ready for action, and not a moment too soon. The Bears sit at 3-2 currently, leaving them in a three-way tie with the Packers and Detroit Lions for second place in the NFC North. They need to start stacking wins before their next divisional matchup in Week 12.
Unfortunately, Williams won't likely get much help from his defense. With Montez Sweat suspended for the next two games Sign Up For the Bears Daily Digest - OnSI’s Free Chicago Bears Newsletter and Dayo Odeyingbo headed to IR , a defense that was already struggling is now severely short-handed. That means the Bears are likely going to need another tsunami of touchdowns from Williams in order to beat the Falcons.
Between Williams wanting to remind the NFL world of who he is and sheer necessity, I would hate to be the Falcons' defense tomorrow.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: What History Says About Caleb Williams and Bears Trying to Bounce Back
full_text:
How Caleb Williams bounces back from his first extended period away due to injury is every bit the theme for Sunday's Bears game at Atlanta as how the team performs coming off its worst performance since losing 52-21 to Detroit in Ben Johnson's second game as coach.
Uncertainty rules in either situation based on the past because there hasn't been any history of absence for Williams and not much of one for adversity with Johnson's team.
However, there have been some . Here is what they suggest.
The problem with trying to forecast how Caleb Williams will play following three missed games due to a hamstring injury is he has never been injured in the past. However, there are instances when he had plenty of time off or even an extra day or so before taking the field again.
For the offseason, I’m posting one random Bears play every day. Here’s number 15. Caleb Williams finds Cole Kmet for the 2 point conversion against the Lions. pic.twitter.com/NQ4Wf9UNUH
In lieu of rebounding from past injuries, this at least indicates how he handles periods off or away beyond a normal work week.
The first instance of this occurred when the Bears played Washington in the Hail Mary game in 2024. They went into it after two weeks away due to their bye week, following a blowout win overseas in London against Jacksonville. Williams wasn't very good on that day, at 10 of 24 for 131 yards. But he did scramble for 47 big yards in what would have been a win, except for Tyrique Stevenson playing out of control on one final Jayden Daniels heave.
Look at Caleb Williams reaction to the Jayden Daniels Hail Mary lmaoooo pic.twitter.com/Ab0Cp5YmTh
In terms of won-loss records, Williams is only 3-6 when he has had more than a week for his next game. This doesn't include his first game ever because he hadn't been in the NFL prior to that one.
Williams hasn't necessarily played poorly in these nine games, though. He had a 94.8 passer rating for the nine games with 183 of 293 (62.4%) for 2,000 yards (222 yards a game) and 12 touchdowns. The interesting part is how few interceptions he had. He threw only one interception total in those nine games when he had extra time to prepare since his NFL debut.
He also had his biggest rushing days after longer periods off. In the 2025 opener, he had six carries for 58 yards in a loss against Minnesota and made 10 carries for 65 yards in this year's opener with Carolina after a full offseason away. In the Hail Mary game, when he'd had two weeks away, he rushed for 47 yards on nine carries. All three represent his top three rushing attempts in games after a break and top three yards gained rushing.
Combine that tendency to run it more with his lack of interceptions and it looks like Williams will be extra cautious with the football and run it himself more. Critics might say he was rusty, uncertain and needed to run it more after holding it too long. Either way, it indicates he's not going to put the ball in harm's way and will take off on his own if need be.
Caleb Williams best plays vs. Dallas pic.twitter.com/jDtdJKDvLh
Of course, the fact he's coming off a hamstring injury suggests he might try to run less anyway but he would have none of that talk when asked about it.
“No. I'll take off," he said.
Maybe his best overall game with extra time was the one at San Francisco last year when the Bears lost 42-38. He only had one extra day then, though. Williams went 25-of-42 for 330 yards with two touchdowns and ran for 18 yards. Second best was the 17-of-29 performance for 252 yards and a touchdown in last year's dramatic comeback win over Washington, when they had a full 15 days before the next game.
D'ANDRE SWIFT FUMBLES ON THE 1-YARD LINE pic.twitter.com/2GuaudF8n9
Johnson's ability to bring a team back after a loss is even more encouraging than Williams' record of performance following breaks or longer prep time.  He saw evidence in practice focus of how they didn't enjoy losing the game to their biggest rivals.
“It's a prideful group," Johnson said.
The Bears are 6-2 in games after a loss when Johnson is coach. This includes their playoff win over Green Bay. It includes their opener this year with Carolina after they had a playoff loss last year to the Rams.
DJ Moore trolled the Packers by wearing a cheese grater hat in the locker room after the game pic.twitter.com/Poh9fJdmrD
The other game this season Johnson coached after a defeat was following the blown game against Minnesota at home when Williams suffered his hamstring injury, D'Andre Swift fumbled at the 1-yard line and Cairo Santos had a tying field goal blocked late in the fourth quarter from only 23 yards out when Sam Roushar whiffed while blocking the player who knocked down the kick.
In 2025, Johnson's biggest comeback win was 31-14 over Dallas after their most embarrassing defeat besides last week's with Green Bay. They had lost 52-21 to Johnson's mentor, Detroit coach Dan Campbell.
The only team to beat the Bears when Johnson is coach following a defeat is Johnson's former team. Besides beating the Bears badly after the 2025 season opener, they also won last year over the Bears at Soldier Field 19-16 to close the regular season in what turned out to be a meaningless game one week after San Francisco had beaten the Bears 42-38. No one else has beaten Johnson coming off a loss.
. @danwiederer : "Caleb Williams can threaten every blade of grass on the football field, and when you have that, you can do things offensively that really strain an opposing defense and make them be accountable to everything you're trying to do against them." pic.twitter.com/RuE3cNI5iV
Their list of wins after defeats includes the 27-7 win over the Eagles with Case Keenum at quarterback, the easy 31-14 win over Dallas at home last season, the wild 47-42 comeback win over Cincinnati last year one week after losing at Baltimore, the 31-3 rout of Cleveland at home a week after losing 28-21 at Green Bay, and their big comeback playoff win at Soldier Field one week after losing to the Lions in the regular-season finale.
There is nothing to suggest the Bears would have a problem following up on their most disappointing defeat of this season or that Williams will have problems shaking off rust and winning a game at Atlanta after inactivity, but each game is a new situation in and of itself in the NFL.
Johnson has said this often himself.
Caleb Williams to Colston Loveland is his best throw of the year Post/wheel concept with 49ers in a Bear front (5 on LOS) to stop the run. Coverage shows quarters pre snap but the safeties rotate just before the snap to cov 3 match. Caleb sees it & knows the wheel will be open pic.twitter.com/j2LRBjvUOZ

title: Two Unheralded Bears LBs Will be Vital to Team's Success Against Falcons
full_text:
Only the Chicago Bears have more rushing yards (866) than the Atlanta Falcons do (834 yards) on the season.
Both teams average more than 166 rushing yards per game, and Atlanta's Robinson duo (Bijan and Brian) has quickly become one of the league's best (alongside D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, when they're both healthy ). They're the only pair with four rushing scores through the first five games.
Bijan, specifically, is a special talent who has firmly established himself as one of the league's best backs. He's a threat to score whenever he has the ball in his hands, and Chicago will need all 11 defenders on the field to commit to slowing him down.
That task will be much harder with three key starters, T.J. Edwards, Montez Sweat, and Dayo Odeyingbo, sidelined. They might go heavier on the defensive line (Neville Gallimore and/or James Lynch might see some time at DE alongside Shemar Turner) more often than not this week, but it's really anyone's guess how they'll divvy up the snaps there.
Meanwhile, the linebacker unit is much more clear. This is a rare instance where it's arguably just as important to get quality play from that unit.
It's no secret how Atlanta's bread is buttered on offense. I've already mentioned that they have the second-best rushing attack. Meanwhile, their passing game lags far behind (their 195 yards per game rank 21st). They've gotten a bit of a boost after Michael Penix Jr. returned to the lineup, but he's probably less than 100% after exiting last week's matchup against Baltimore with a rib injury.
Based on the Falcons' rushing and passing success, it's safe to assume Chicago will deploy their base defense (featuring four defensive linemen and three linebackers) more often this week.
Devin Bush is the Bears' best linebacker, but he's much better in coverage than when he's coming down near the line of scrimmage. His size (5'11", 234 lbs.) limits his ability in that department.
With Edwards out of the lineup, they'll probably be counting on D'Marco Jackson to wear the green dot and relay plays to the rest of the defense this week. That's a role that he took over ( and passed with flying colors ) after a bomb went off in Chicago's linebacker room last year. He'll be an every-down player on Sunday.
Who will be Chicago's third linebacker? Based on last week, it'll be Noah Sewell. He played 22 snaps in his season debut against Green Bay after returning from the Injured Reserve list. That was 36% of the team's defensive snaps , and he'll probably see 50% or more this week.
Sewell enjoyed a mini-breakout last season after largely being limited to special teams duties over his first two years. He started nine games and finished the campaign with 59 tackles (including 3 for loss) and one forced fumble before tearing his Achilles in their Week 17 matchup against San Francisco.
If the Bears allow the Robinson duo to take over the game , they'd be hard-pressed to come out with a victory in Atlanta. Both Sewell and Jackson have shown flashes , but have largely been overshadowed throughout their career. They'll need to bring their A-game to slow the Falcons down.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Bears Activate Gordon, Place Dayo on IR, Cut Safety Among 6 Roster Moves Before Week 6 Game
full_text:
The Chicago Bears made a slew of roster moves on Saturday that included the activation of Kyler Gordon.
Gordon, who had been on the PUP list since the offseason due to a calf injury, is now ready to play for the Bears on Sunday after his activation on Saturday .
It remains to be seen how many snaps Gordon will play, but he is expected to return to his job in the slot, which should push Malik Muhammad to the boundary opposite Jaylon Johnson. If that's the case, Tyrique Stevenson will head to the bench.
In addition to activating Gordon, the Bears made a surprising cut, with the team waiving veteran safety Xavier Woods, who was signed during the offseason amid injuries in the secondary.
That almost certainly means that Cam Lewis will be starting at the safety position next to Dillon Thieneman.
The Bears also placed Dayo Odeyingbo on injured reserve thanks to his quadriceps injury he suffered in Week 5.
This means Odeyingbo will miss at least the next four games, which is a devastating blow to the pass-rush, as Odeyingbo had the team lead in pressures and was second in sacks. Chicago is going to be very short-handed for the next two games because Montez Sweat is also out because of a suspension .
Chicago made three moves involving the practice squad. Nick McCloud has been promoted to the active roster and both linebacker Buddy Johnson and running back Zavier Scott garnered an elevation for Week 6.
The elevation of McCloud could be an indication that the Bears don't expect Stevenson to play. The veteran cornerback is on the injury report with a hamstring injury and is questionable to play .
Johnson's elevation is in response to the Bears missing both T.J. Edwards and rookie Keyshaun Elliott. Edwards and Elliott were ruled out on Friday with hamstring and quadriceps injuries, respectively.
Scott will give the Bears a third running back with Kyle Monangai ruled out for a second straight game . Monangai is dealing with a turf toe injury, but he is expected to avoid injured reserve, which puts him in play to return next week or the week after.
The issue with a possible return in Week 7 for Monangai is the fact that the Bears will be playing on a short week. Nevertheless, head coach Ben Johnson said Monangai is "trending in the right direction," so he's making progress.
One move we were hoping to see was the removal of Caleb Williams from the injury report. However, that did not happen and instead his status remains up in the air with the questionable tag.
The Bears will release their list of inactives at 11:30 a.m. ET on Sunday, so we'll know for sure if Williams is playing by then.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Bears Reporter Responds to Criticism Over Tense Caleb Williams Interaction
full_text:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams met with the media for the first time since his injury on Thursday and had a tense interaction with a Bears reporter.
That Bears reporter was The Athletic's Dan Wiederer, who pushed Williams for an answer on his exact injury diagnosis. However, the Bears quarterback was not interested in giving an answer , as he was clearly frustrated with the reporting on the subject.
"Yeah, we got a grade, but I wouldn't say it's deserved to be put out there after all the false ones," Williams said . "Next question."
"Just not deserving. Next question," Williams responded when Wiederer pressed him further for a direct answer on his injury. "Next question. Thank you. Next question."
Williams' frustration is understandable after it was initially reported that he had a minor hamstring injury, which led to ridicule over how he reacted on the field, and then later reports revealed he had suffered a more serious Grade 2 hamstring strain.
Wiederer received no shortage of backlash from Bears fans who thought he should not have prodded once it was clear Williams wasn't going to answer.
Wiederer was a guest on "Spiegel & Holmes" on 104.3 The Score on Friday and downplayed the significance of the interaction with Williams and said he has "the utmost respect" for the quarterback.
"This is just one small exchange over 30 months of my time covering Caleb," Wiederer said. "I’ve got the utmost respect for him and the way he goes about his craft. It’s just a moment. I think the livestream nature of our world today blows everything up into something way bigger than it needs to be."
We understand the desire for information, as reporters are often criticized if they don't get as much information as possible. But once it was clear Williams wasn't going to answer, Wiederer should've backed off.
Williams is listed as questionable to play and he did not commit to suiting up, but all signs continue to point to him returning.
Williams logged three full practices this week and head coach Ben Johnson said on more than one occasion that he's on track. But he also noted that the Bears would have to see how Williams emerges from a full week of practice.
"I'm hopeful we'll have more clarity at the end of the day today," he said on Friday . "(Williams) looked good yesterday for one practice, but we got to be able to stack a few back-to-back.
"He got some good work in on Wednesday, it's part of the plan and he's on track right now."
On Friday evening, Williams reposted a hype video on TikTok, which strongly suggests he's going to play.
We could get confirmation on Saturday, but if not we'll know no later than Sunday morning if Williams will suit up.
When it comes to who will start if Williams doesn't play, Johnson is keeping that close to the vest, which is a departure from last week when he named Tyson Bagent the starter over Case Keenum early in the week before Bagent imploded on Sunday.
Given Johnson's lack of an announcement for which backup would start, it's safe to assume he either expects Williams to play or plans on rolling with Keenum, who had the best performance of the two backups when he started in Week 3.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Bears Injury Crisis: 4 Players Who Must Stop Bijan Without Dayo, Sweat, and Edwards
full_text:
The Chicago Bears enter Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons as slight favorites on the road at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday, despite dealing with a full-on injury crisis.
Falcons running back Bijan Robinson makes Atlanta an intriguing underdog in this one, though. Robinson is coming off three straight games of averaging at least five yards per carry with at least 17 touches out of the backfield.
Chicago is coming off a brutal 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers and lost three key Bears defenders in edge-rushers Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo, and linebacker T.J. Edwards over the past week.
Sweat was suspended two games for violating the league's performance-enhancing substances policy. Edwards injured his hamstring during the brutal loss at Lambeau Field. Meanwhile, Odeyingbo injured his quadriceps.
While none are renowned run-stoppers, all of them are key pieces of Dennis Allen's defensive ecosystem.
Being without Sweat's edge-setting and Edwards' green dot communication could provide unique challenges for the defense that Robinson could exploit. Odeyingbo's gravity, which often draws double-teams on early downs, will also be missed.
These four Bears need to step up on Sunday to slow down the NFL's most feared running back:
Austin Booker had his biggest game of the season against Green Bay, amassing two sacks, three TFLs, and a forced fumble.
After vouching for a bigger role before Week 4 against the New York Jets , he received it and delivered.
Now, he needs to follow that up by setting the edge against Robinson, who prefers bouncing to the outside more than playing between the tackles. Booker might be the most important player for Allen and Co. until the injuries subside.
Daniel Hardy is one of the primary candidates to see extended snaps against the Falcons in Sweat and Odeyingbo's absence.
Hardy specializes in special teams play, but he'll need to prove his value on the line after receiving a multi-year extension in the offseason.
Hardy hasn't proved himself as a pass-rusher, but covering the edge well against Robinson could earn him more defensive snaps.
Defensive tackle James Lynch has the opposite problem as Hardy. Lynch is a strong run-stopper but isn't disruptive rushing the passer.
Lynch could make a name for himself in extended snaps this Sunday during his debut season in Chicago and give Allen another reliable big body in the middle.
Now in his second stint with the Bears, Jamree Kromah could finally get his first regular-season snap this Sunday.
Kromah had three sacks, four TFLs, and forced a fumble in the preseason. There's definitely intrigue about what Kromah could do after spending two seasons bouncing around practice squads.
Andrew Hughes is a freelance journalist based in Austin, Texas, who has bylines across ON SI and The Sporting News. His work has been featured in The Miami Herald, Bleacher Report, and Yahoo Sports. Andrew graduated from Brooklyn College with a degree in journalism in 2017 and has been a sports fan since 1993.

title: Chicago Bears Projected to Be Major Players at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
It has been tough to fully gauge exactly where the 3-2 Chicago Bears stand when it comes to the team being a true contender when it comes to a Super Bowl.
Through five games, the Bears have started three different signal-callers thanks to the injury to Caleb Williams. Hopefully, that won't happen again this season after Williams gets back, which could happen as soon as Week 6 .
On the other side of the ball, the Bears have three really good performances sandwiched in between two really bad ones, leaving the jury still out on the defense overall.
But if the Bears can show they are legit between now and the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10, they could be very aggressive — and Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox agrees with that.
Knox listed the Bears as a team he predicts will be among the biggest players at the NFL trade deadline next month. Knox is pointing to the defense as the side of the ball where Chicago could look to make at least one addition.
The Chicago Bears are sitting at 3-2 and chasing the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in the NFC North," Knox said. "While Caleb Williams' hamstring injury played a role in both losses, a suspect defense hasn't helped."
"The Bears' defense has looked respectable at times, but it ranks 22nd in yards per carry allowed and 30th in net yards per pass attempt allowed," Knox added. "Don't be surprised if general manager Ryan Poles looks to bolster the defensive front and the pass rush in the coming weeks."
The defensive line has two positions that could use more help.
On the edge, Chicago's pass-rush has been OK but not great, even when fully healthy. Now, Chicago is missing Montez Sweat due to suspension and Dayo Odeyingbo because of injury .
With those two out, Chicago is relying on incredibly shaky depth behind Austin Booker, with guys like James Lynch, Daniel Hardy, Jamree Kromah and Shemar Turner set to try and fill the voids. Those three players have 3.5 career sacks combined and the veteran Lynch has all of them.
The Bears need more pass-rush juice on the interior, as their D-tackles have just one sack, which belongs to Kentavius Street.
Chicago's run defense could use a bolstering, also, with the Bears posting a run stop win rate of 27% that ranks 29th, per ESPN , and a yards allowed per carry average of 4.4, which is tied for 11th-highest in the NFL.
Another sneaky position that could use more help is cornerback.
Granted, the Bears are on the cusp of being at 100% at the position as Kyler Gordon prepares to come back , but we know his past with injury issues and both Tyrique Stevenson and Jaylon Johnson have been awful in 2026.
Of course, there's no telling where injuries will hit between now and the trade deadline, so a position we aren't currently considering could become a need down the road, also.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons: Who Wins and Why for Week 6
full_text:
The Bears have made bouncing back their theme for the week. It's all you can do after being embarrassed by your biggest rival.
“That story has yet to be written," coach Ben Johnson said. "We get a chance to do that ourselves. I feel strongly about our locker room. I think we have a lot of high-quality, character guys. A lot of prideful individuals.
"So far this week they've handled it. It's all been back to business as usual."
They're in last place in the NFC North based on divisional records but at 3-2 there are only three teams in the entire NFC with better overall records.
"There's no moping around or woe is me," Johnson said. "They understand it's a long season. Everything is still out in front of us. We still have a winning record. That's a good thing.
“This game sets up beautifully for Ben Johnson.” @danorlovsky7 and @Hawk preview the Bears-Falcons matchup in Atlanta 💪 pic.twitter.com/4MCfmwzLiq
"We have a lot to play for here going forward. This next stretch before the bye week is a big part."
It starts with trying to stop the NFL's top rusher, Bijan Robinson, and with Caleb Williams making big plays downfield in his expected return to the field.
In fact, this could be an entirely different group than went to Green Bay and seemed to quit by the fourth quarter, but that's not entirely a good thing. It could include slot cornerback Kyler Gordon and tackle Ozzy Trapilo besides Williams, but not starting defensive ends Montez Sweat, Dayo Odeyingbo or linebacker T.J. Edwards.
It's the Bears and Falcons in Atlanta with the roof closed at noon Sunday. Here's who wins and why.
. @MattSpiegs didn't mince his words in reacting to the NFL failing to award the Bears a pair of compensatory draft picks for Ian Cunningham leaving for the Falcons. "This is absolute trash," Spiegel says. "And I'm angry about it. I'm bothered by it." pic.twitter.com/famEYz9XSJ
Without the power punch of Kyle Monangai, the Bears' running game looked less impactful last week. They're not going to have him this week. At least D'Andre Swift is a week removed from a hip injury that had been bothering him. Atlanta's defense gave up rushing yardage in chunks last week for the first time when up against Derrick Henry and Baltimore, but have given up only 3.8 yards per rush and former Bear Gervon Dexter has actually been fairly effective at stopping the run after he struggled doing it in Chicago. No edge
It's hard to see how Williams would be able to play without rust and also show the kind of movement he normally flashes after he has had a hamstring injury that kept him out 3 1/2 weeks. The Bears will need plenty of support for Williams in the ground game and from his receivers. Fortunately for the Bears, Atlanta's biggest weakness has been pass defense and starting cornerbacks C.J. Henderson and A.J. Terrell Jr. are both out injured. They're 27th at stopping the pass. The last time the Bears faced a pass defense so challenged they scored 59 points. Edge to Bears
Derrick Henry bulldozes his way for another first down 😤 @BALvsATL on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/rHZW07dVYP
The numbers say the Bears are better at stopping the run than last year but they're still getting moved off the line too far at times. Grady Jarrett has been a force inside, but losing T.J. Edwards and both starting defensive ends can't help when Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. are bringing it in Atlanta's running game. Bijan is averaging 5.7 yards an attempt and his 580 yards is No. 1 in the NFL. Grady Jarrett's homecoming game is going to need to include penetration and breaking up the wide zone schemes Atlanta loves to run with the Robinsons. Edge to Falcons
Losing stinks, but Falcons running back Bijan Robinson tells @archerqb16Atlanta will learn from the way Baltimore put 10 defensive players in the box. 📹 @fox5sports pic.twitter.com/sCehlv31uU
Last week was the first time since the opener that the Bears had massive breakdowns in the back end and if they get Kyler Gordon back they could have an effective group, although it's going to be difficult for the entire defense to focus on stopping the pass when Atlanta has run it the second most times, trailing only the Bears. Trying to get a pass rush going with backups will be difficult but the Bears could turn loose Austin Booker after Michael Penix. Facing a left-handed quarterback can be a change that causes problems for the Bears defense but they've got enough problems stopping WR Drake London besides that. They'd have even bigger problems if tight end Kyle Pitts started making catches but with only 10 receptions he's been less of a threat even than the Bears' Colston Loveland (13 catches). No Edge
As a reminder, the Chicago Bears have already traded for a CB in Clark Phillips from the Falcons in the Gervon Dexter deal. Why isn’t he seeing playing time? #DaBears
Cairo Santos last week used his leg better at tripping Packers on the sidelines after they knocked over Bears coaches than he did for kicking the ball. His missed 43-yarder can't happen. Santos isn't going to help as a long-range kicker so accuracy has to be his thing. However, even after that miss he's a better kicker than 41-year-old Falcons kicker Nick Folk. Zavion Thomas got a taste of a breakaway return last week and next time needs to avoid being caught from behind. Atlanta has used former Bear Olamide Zaccheaus, RB Brian Robinson Jr. and Zachariah Branch to return kicks but they're averaging less (24.6) than the Bears have had from Thomas (25.9). No Edge
🔥I love Dillon #Thieneman ; he has been very solid as a rookie. He is a versatile safety with good range, a knack for being around the ball, and physicality. @DillonThieneman #DaBears pic.twitter.com/FiR1eCHXzq
Ben Johnson hasn't had too many opportunities to show his team can bounce back but last year they lost consecutive games twice and that suggests it's not always easy for the coaching staff to reverse negative trends. All of the injuries the Bears have had on defense might have a positive overall effect. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen was at his best last year when he was given less talent due to injuries. Atlanta's Kevin Stefanski and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees aren't known as the most dynamic offensive coaches but they do have outstanding offensive line veteran coach Bill Callahan supporting them. No Edge
The Caleb Williams ruckus, a loss to the Packers and numerous injuries combine with a road game against a talented opponent to leave the Bears staring at a dangerous threat. Atlanta's defense just faced Baltimore and former Bears offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. The Ravens had the upper hand, but is it really an advantage for the Bears if Atlanta is familiar now with this style of offense after seeing it two straight weeks? Edge to Falcons
If Michael Penix was a good NFL quarterback, he completes this pass and the Falcons win the game. pic.twitter.com/bsPqh0VeyD

Key to Bears win: Big gains in the passing game against a Falcons secondary teetering much of the year. A lead via the pass can go a long way toward forcing Atlanta to get away from the run and using Bijan Robinson.

title: Ben Johnson Is Keeping the Falcons Guessing on Caleb Williams Until the Last Possible Moment
full_text:
Here's how this is going to work with the Bears and Caleb Williams ' return as they creep closer to game day in Atlanta amid the secrecy and pretense involved with Ben Johnson's injury report .
Williams has run the plays and this week, went through physical testing of his hamstring after doing rehab for four weeks but the Bears stopped short of labeling him their starter on Friday. Johnson essentially  wants the uncertainty for the Falcons' defense to ponder. There can be no other reason for this after four weeks.
Caleb Williams moving well at #Bears practice today. He was a full participant. pic.twitter.com/ZLE7gS8psT
“I'm hopeful we'll have more clarity at the end of the day today," Johnson said Friday. "He looked good yesterday (Thursday) for one practice, but, we've got to be able to stack a few back-to-back. He got some good work in on Wednesday, even though we walked-through, he went through his own throwing session beforehand. So, it's part of the plan and he's on track right now.”
Asked what on track meant, Johnson provided nothing.
Bears QB Caleb Williams’ workout concluded at 9:27 am here at Lambeau Field. He did a variety of different throws, including his “Superman.” pic.twitter.com/fcT8tL7Ieg
“He's on track to get all those check marks," Johnson said.
And finally, Johnson was asked if it meant Williams would play Sunday once he cleared all of their "check marks."
“Potentially," Johnson said.
The Bears put Williams through all sorts of testing and Williams himself estimated five or six hours of rehab a day recently. They say they are just trying to be sure he's ready by getting him past these mile markers of sorts.
🚨YIKES: Caleb Williams still looked bothered by his hamstring injury today at practice. After practice he referred to the injury as “serious” but would not provide further details. (🎥: @Zack_Pearson ) pic.twitter.com/F3rwcVLxvZ
“It probably is a little bit different intensity and yet that's what we're trying to work through here over the course of the week; is just getting him up to those high speeds and making sure that we don't have any effects that continue to linger on," Johnson said. "Once again, we're right on track with the plan and we'll see what it looks like, see how he feels. Confidence is a big part of it as well, but I know he wants to play.
"He's a competitor. It's been not fun for him the last few weeks watching from the sideline, just like any guy that loves football. It's been a tough deal for him. I know he's itching to get back out there and help us win ball games. If we feel really good as a front office, a coaching staff, and the player himself about playing, then we'll go ahead and go with it."
Caleb Williams appearing at the #Bears ' starting quarterback press conference might be a tell, but not the one you think it is. The underlying lesson of that awkward press conference moment was that Ben Johnson loves gamesmanship, so all bets are off: https://t.co/2QLJvIZMTO
So much of Williams' game revolves around his mobility, being able to escape the pocket and run or pass or even just move in the pocket and throw. His spins, the mad dashes and jump passing are integral parts of his game. Although healed enough to play, Williams said on Thursday the fear of re-injuring the hamstring isn't enough to prevent him from scrambling.
“No. I'll take off," Williams said.
None of this says for certain he'll play, but Williams was downright bored with his rehabbing status, so he might drive Johnson nuts if he's not allowed to play.
Is Caleb Williams justified to be cautious about speaking to the media regarding his injury? The crew weighs in ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/UzyC69T4bW
This doesn't clear anything up for the moment, but the Bears do have Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum in case he really can't play. Keenum won his only start, 27-7 over the Eagles. Bagent started last week's 31-7 loss at Green Bay and also the 23-12 win over the Jets.
So who would the backup be? Backup passes in drills were being handled by Bagent, but the media doesn't get to see actual plays being run and play reps.
"We've got two guys that are equally qualified," Johnson said.
At least they're consistent with how they treat the news of the day.
This feels like the beginning of the end of Caleb Williams & Chicago. This isn’t the response of a guy who trusts his PR department. He was certainly prepared for this. When things get outwardly combative, there are usually bubbling issues behind the scenes. Just speculating. https://t.co/BFLwca7dU4

title: Cincinnati Bengals Players Fined For Separate Plays Following Dolphins Win
full_text:
A pair of Bengals took on fines for separate plays in this past Sunday's win over Miami. Our Jay Morrison noted on Saturday that Erick All and Jordan Battle got infractions handed down from the league.
"Erick All Jr. fined $7,073 for an unnecessary roughness penalty against Miami. Jordan Battle fined $21,623 for illegal use of helmet," Morrison posted on X .
Cincinnati got physical in the win over one of the few winless teams remaining in the NFL. All and Battle were huge parts of those wins to help Cincinnati get to 3-2 on the season.
It was a hot, tightly contested game filled with tough hits like the ones that got those players penalized.
"Nothing really at this point in October gets you ready for this heat. Somebody told me it started as the hottest game here in October history, which I can attest to," Taylor said about the hot Miami weather after the 31-24 win. "I've coached here for four years, and this was, I mean, in pregame, I was worn out. Our players fought through that, and I made that statement to them because I know they're dead tired right now. I didn't want them to think that's just in their mind, like, what's wrong with me? It was a hot day, and they battled through it, and they found a way to win. I don't discount that at all."
Cincinnati has a couple more days off before returning to practice on Monday ahead of the most important game of the season so far.
An AFC North matchup against Baltimore awaits .
"You kind of like it more towards Thanksgiving," Taylor said about the bye week placement on Monday. "But I do think just where our team is right now, and the way that these last three games have gone down to the wire, and guys playing through some stuff right now, it is a good time to get a bye and get our legs back underneath us, get some guys healthy, and go full force when we come back for Baltimore."
Cincinnati takes on the Ravens next Sunday in Baltimore.

title: 3 Potential Trades the Bengals Could Make Prior to 2026 Deadline
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals rolled into the bye week 3-2.
Work needs to be done, but this team still has the pieces to make a long run in the postseason. It cannot be denied that fixing the issues needs to happen quickly.
What do those changes look like? The easy answer could be in the form of a trade. Here are three potential trades the Bengals could make if they plan on being all-in on a Super Bowl run this season.
The Bengals' linebacker play has not been on par for a team that is chasing a deep playoff run. That's where Tennessee Titans linebacker Cody Barton comes into play.
Not to bash on the Titans, but they are a team that is far away from being a competitor. If they have pieces that can bring back value, they could be a very active team at the deadline.
Barton is a piece that can bring them back some value while also giving a competitive team a nice addition to their defense.
Pro Football Focus currently has Barton graded as the 27th-best linebacker in the league. The cap hit for the 30-year-old linebacker is over $4 million for the 2026 season.  If it's an all-in situation, Barton would fit the bill.
If the Bengals are looking for secondary depth, Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Tariq Woolen could be an option.
The Eagles seem to be unsure what the future holds. The NFC East has looked like a train wreck, as the Eagles are 2-3 but still in second place.
Woolen's cap hit would only be $910,000 if a team were to make a trade. That could make this a high-upside situation for the Bengals.
A familiar name for Bengals fans, Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III would be a major move. After spending five seasons with the Bengals, including the 2021 season when the team went to the Super Bowl, Bates has spent the last four seasons in Atlanta.
It would be a heavy cap hit to bring Bates back in the fold. But would a $9 million hit to the cap be worth Bates' veteran presence in the secondary? Not to mention, this homecoming could have the fan base buzzing.

title: Ravens Star Quarterback Lamar Jackson Carrying Injury Into Bengals Game Week
full_text:
The Bengals may not be facing Lamar Jackson next week.
The Ravens star quarterback injured his ankle in the team's Week 4 win over Tennessee, and he has not practiced in any session since then, with the Bengals up next in Week 7. He is not playing in Week 6 when the Ravens suit up in a couple of days.
“It’s Wednesday. There’s a lot of time between now and Sunday,” Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said last week. “To Lamar’s credit, he’s getting a lot of treatment and doing things. There’ll be a point later in the week where we’ll kinda figure out where it’s at ... When he’s ready to play, he’ll be ready to play.”
It would be a massive loss for Baltimore, which has dominated Cincinnati in Jackson starts. The team is 11-3 against Cincinnati when Jackson is on the field.
He's been lights out, with 7.9 yards per attempt, 24 passing touchdowns, six interceptions, and a 101.9 passer rating in those games. Whether it's Jackson or Tyler Huntley out there next week, Cincinnati is aiming to be ready.
Zac Taylor is hoping to have as many healthy players as possible after Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins gutted through injury in Miami.
"Hats off to them. They wanted to play, and Ja'Marr had to clear protocol on Saturday," Taylor said about the duo. "His mindset all along was, 'I'm playing." Now I hadn't seen him on the field enough to know. I appreciate him saying that, but I need to see him do it in practice, and he did. For those guys to go out there and make plays that they did for us is a big time. I don't ever question that.
"Those guys have been here seven years, six years, and they show up for us every chance they get. We have leaders and great players like that on our team. It sets the tone for everybody else when those guys are playing through injuries and doing everything they can to come down here and play in Miami before bye week. They could easily say, give me a week off, we'll get the bye week, and we'll come back for the divisional game, but they didn't want to do that."
Cincinnati battles the Ravens at 1 p.m. ET next Sunday.

title: Bengals Bye Week Self-Scout Reveals What's Working and What Must Change
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are off to a solid start after five games with a 3-2 record and normally we would dissect the opponent and dive into the data to get a feel for how they're performing this season, but with the bye week already here, it's time for some self-scouting and dissecting where the Bengals stand after five games.
Let's start on offense where they avoided the dreaded slow start and rank 10th in EPA per play and PFF has them as the 5th highest graded offense.
Joe Burrow is again PFF’s highest graded passer on plays without play-action. He has been ranked number one in 2021, 2022, 2024, 2025 and now holds that top spot in 2026.
Does it feel like Burrow and this offense hasn't been explosive this year? I'm sure they want to create more big plays, but Burrow leads the league in 20+ yard touchdown passes with five. He's also one of four quarterbacks without a “turnover worthy throw” on deep passes. His 137.9 passer rating on deep balls leads the entire NFL.
But it's really the Intermediate area where Burrow is doing his damage to opposing defenses.
22.8% of his total passes are targeted between 10-19 yards this season and his 95.7 PFF grade leads all quarterbacks.
He's completing 74.4% of his passes in this range and that also tops all QBs. And the Bengals are getting big plays out of it as Burrow averages 12.0 yards per attempt in this area.
It probably helps that he's getting protected up front with the best offensive line of his career. This Cincinnati line ranks 6th in PFF’s Pass Block Efficiency.
Their 4.5% sack rate - 5th Best in NFL and they were 10th last year and 19th in 2024. Looks like steady progress for a QB and offensive line that has been heavily criticized for allowing too much pressure and taking too many sacks.
Look no further than right tackle Amarius Mims and his 98.8% pass block efficiency which is second amongst all offensive tackles.
Dalton Risner at right guard is the 5th highest graded pass blocking guard in True Pass Sets from PFF and he's enjoying a career year as a run blocker as well.
Despite allowing pressure on just 36.3% of all dropbacks this season, which ranks 7th best, the Bengals are allowing pressure on 3rd downs at a higher rate than I'd like. On 51.9% of their 3rd down passes, Burrow is facing pressure and yes, they're  converting 50% of third downs this season, that's tied for second-best.
The issue is that they're seeing the 11th most 3rd downs in the NFL. You don't want to put your QB under that much pressure on critical down and the other two top teams in 3rd down conversions, Buffalo and San Francisco, are seeing 3rd downs at the lowest rate in the league.
The run game has been a big topic the last few weeks as they've struggled to get Chase Brown going despite some decent blocking overall.
Brown is currently outside the top 35 backs in average yards AFTER contact at 2.1 and his Elusive Rating from PFF ranks him 22nd amongst the 32 starters in the league.
Last season, Brown averaged 3.4 yards after contact per carry.
It's not all Brown either, as a whole the Bengals sit at 2.03 Average Rush Yards After Contact - 31st in the NFL
The Bengals running scheme should be helping him here: They've only been “Stuffed” on 13.2% of rushing plays - 8th best in the league – They led the NFL last season at a 10% stuffed rate.
But, they're not converting that into explosives or successful runs.
Their 39.5% Rushing Success Rate ranks 20th after being 11th-best last season at 42.8%
Where are the issues with the blocking? Amarius Mims is the 4th lowest graded offensive tackle in Run Blocking from PFF.
Drew Sample ranks 37th and Erick All 44th of 51 total right ends in PFF run blocking.
With the lack of success running the ball, the offseason plan of getting under center and running the ball and exploiting defenses with play-action has been thrown out. The Bengals have the 2nd lowest rate of play-action in NFL this season.
So it's back to the Bengals offense of old. Even if they figure out the run game, I expect this shotgun offense to lead the way and that's not a bad thing.
The offense usually fires up at this point in the season. Since 2021, the Bengals are the very best offense in the league (EPA per play) in weeks 6 through 12.
That's 5 years of sustained elite offensive success and that includes 10 games started by the combo of Jake Browning and Joe Flacco.
Is it the same old Bengals on defense?
Cincinnati owns the 12th ranked defense based on EPA per play. We would take that all season long.
They're 5th in passing EPA, but rank 26th on defense for PFF and they're dragged down by the 28th ranked Coverage grade and 26th ranked Tackling grade.
They're currently the 7th best defense in terms of EPA per play when in their base 3-4 defense. That ranking drops to 22nd when they're in Nickel defense.
A run defense that boasts a league-leading 30% Run Stuff Rate, but 21 runs of 10+ yards allowed leads the NFL also.
They're very home run or strikeout in run defense.
The Bengals are doing this all with a Light Box (less defenders near the line). They lead the league in light box rate at 59.6% of their total defensive snaps and that would explain some of the long runs that have gashed this defense.
You can play with less defenders in the box when Dexter Lawrence accounts for two people. He's been everything we could've hoped for as he enjoys a bounce back season on the stat sheet. Lawrence is on pace for 65 pressures and 10 sacks this season and currently owns PFF’s second highest grade for defensive tackles.
As a whole, the Bengals defense is generating pressure on 41.6% of pass plays and that ranks 12th best in the league.
Much of that is thanks to free agent prize Boye Mafe and his 25 pressures through five games. That's a pace of 85 pressures for a full season. Only three players had more last season and 83 is the most Trey Hendrickson ever had with the Bengals (2024).
And they're doing with the frustratingly low Blitz Rate of 17.3% – lowest in the NFL.
So what are they doing on defense? They play the 10th-most single-high safety coverages with  the 9th-most Man Coverage calls.
They're also not disguising their coverages. They rotate safety coverage at the snap on 29% of plays and that's 9th least in the NFL.
But coverage has been tight. DJ Turner looks just as good in coverage as he did last season, but quarterbacks are avoiding throwing in his direction.
And why would they throw at him or Dax Hill when the linebackers and safeties offer easier completions?
The trio of Demetrius Knight, Barrett Carter and Jordan Battle have allowed 46 passes to be caught out of 58 targets. That's a completion percentage of 79.3% when you target those guys in coverage.
The coverage hasn't been all bad as 15.9% of all throws have been contested by the Bengals defense - 7th best rate in the NFL.
But when you play as much Man coverage as you do, you leave yourself open up the middle and they've allowed 145 QB scramble yards and that's 3rd most in the NFL. They'll have to figure that out before seeing Lamar Jackson this season.
Finally, they're currently averaging 8 penalties per game which is 19th worst and up from their 5 penalties per game last season. This is an area under Zac Taylor where they've always been exceptional and because it's always been good during his run as head coach, I expect it'll be smoothed out, but it is something to watch as it has affected their games to start the season.
Overall, they've got things to clean up and figure out as every team does. Zac Taylor teams do a good job at figuring those things out as they do and they tend to play their best as the season progresses. Since 2021, Zac Taylor and Joe Burrow together have won 75% of all games after the bye week. With 12 games to go, that's another 9 wins.
I'll take 12-5, even if it feels harder than it should.

title: Erick All Jr. Explains Why Bengals Would Much Rather Be Playing During Week 6 Bye
full_text:
Erick All would much rather be working this week.
The Bengals tight end appeared on First Word With James Rapien Wednesday morning and said he and many of his teammates wanted to keep the games rolling instead of taking their early bye-week break.
The roster won in Miami 31-24 this past Sunday, but it left a bad taste in their mouths.
"I felt like that wasn't our best game, and I feel like I'm just not the only one that feels like this, and a lot of guys are ready to go out there and put some explosive plays on film," All said on the show.
All was Cincinnati's second-leading receiver in the game behind Ja'Marr Chase. He caught all three of his targets for 25 yards, but did have a fumble that Cincinnati ended up recovering. That's weighed on the young pass catcher, and he gets a chance to keep responding next Sunday against the Ravens.
He's coming off a season-high 33 snaps as well, showing how well he rehabbed from major knee surgeries over the past few years.
"I had a lot of support, man. I had a lot of support, obviously my family and with the Bengals ," All said about working back to full health. "One thing that I love about being here, man, is the training staff is top-notch. Like those guys really helped me out a lot mentally. Well, pretty much 100% physically because they were getting me back healthy. But those guys are really, really good at what they do.
"Matt Summers, the head trainer, does a great job with making sure you're on top of things. When you're recovering for that long you can kind of get lenient on things, but he makes sure that you're locked in and you're keeping your eye on the main prize, and that's really all you can ask for."

title: Bengals Defense Ranks Top Five Among NFL Teams in Key 2026 Metric
full_text:
The Bengals defense has shown solid improvement in several areas to start the season, but one stat shows it's one of the league's most opportunistic units. Over five weeks, the Bengals defense ranks fourth in creating havoc for opposing offenses, a statistic that measures the percentage of times a defense gets pressure, a tackle for loss, a pass breakup, or a turnover.
The individual defensive stats back this up as they are twelfth in pressure rate at 32.5%, tied for the third-most sacks in the league with 17. They also rank eighth with 28 TFL's, eleventh in PBU's with 25, and seventh in takeaways with 8.
It is clear that the offseason additions have improved the Bengals' defense more than the team could have imagined. The most drastic improvement, however, comes from the defensive line.
Boye Mafe, Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, and Cashius Howell have all had tremendous impacts on the pass rush and are the reason for Cincinnati's dominance in the trenches this year.
Mafe, in particular, has emerged as the Bengals' most capable pass rusher so far, leading the team with 25 pressures and tying Lawrence and Allen with three sacks. Lawrence and Allen also both have at least 16 pressures each five weeks into the season.
Following the Bengals' recent win over the Dolphins, Mafe suggested the defense could reach another level.
“It definitely felt like it was more connected, but there still are more things that we can do, and more that we can do to keep going," Mafe said. "There's another level, and that's the thing that I feel like today we realize is that there is another level that we can take it to."
Should the defense reach a higher level, we could see it eclipse 60 sacks this season, as it is on pace for 58 through 17 games. That would break the current franchise record of 51, set in 2012. That should, in turn, lead to the defense creating even more havoc than it is now.

title: Bengals Must Avoid This Tempting Trade Deadline Mistake
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are 3-2 as they hit the early Week 6 bye week. The win over the Miami Dolphins this past Sunday was massive, but the team left a lot of meat on the bone during that performance.
The passing game has been exactly what everyone expected. Joe Burrow and his merry band of weapons are one of the most dangerous passing offenses in the league. Then you have a revamped defensive line that is causing terror, alongside an offensive line that is a night-and-day difference from the past few seasons. But there's a reason this team is just 3-2.
One of the biggest weaknesses on this team has been the running game. The Bengals are 26th in rushing yards this season at 414. Chase Brown leads the team in rushing with 246 yards, but it hasn't been enough. While there have been issues with the unit, a tempting trade at the deadline would be a bad move.
Trying to upgrade at the trade deadline in this league has to feel like an impossible task. Very few teams would be willing to give up a running back that the Bengals would arguably be their number one option.
So, let's look at a name that could come up before the deadline. Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard may seem like a great trade candidate and one the Bengals may want to look into.
Pollard's numbers are very similar to Browns. The Titans' running back has rushed for 273 yards and one touchdown this season. But what needs to be added to that equation is that the veteran running back is running behind an abysmal offensive line.
Then there's the financial side to a potential trade. If the Bengals were to make a move for Pollard, the cap hit would be a little over $5 million.
Does it really make sense for the Bengals to take that hit for a talent that is putting up the same numbers as the starting running back they already have?
Sure, more backs may hit the trade rumor mill before the deadline approaches. But at the moment, it feels like the talent that could potentially be traded at the deadline in the backfield is scarce.
This could be a case where the Bengals want to make a move, but the talent that can be added isn't going to be enough to move the needle. The Bengals really need to think hard about any potential move at running back.
