title: Joe Burrow Ranked Outside Top-Five NFL Quarterbacks as Bye Week Rolls on
full_text:
Sports Illustrated's Matt Verdarame dropped the site's latest 1-32 NFL quarterback rankings, and Bengals passer Joe Burrow fell outside the top five names in the update.
He started the season ranked fifth overall and is down to sixth on the board with Cincinnati sitting at 3-2 overall entering its bye week.
"When Burrow has been healthy, he’s been an elite quarterback throughout his seven-year NFL career," Verdarame wrote . "In 2026, Burrow has started all five games for the Bengals and looked like a superstar, ranking sixth with 1,361 passing yards while tossing 11 touchdowns against three interceptions.  Analytically, Burrow also ranks fourth in CPOE (6.0) and 13th in EPA per play (0.179) while checking in eighth in success rate (51.2%). With Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on the outside, Cincinnati remains one of the more dangerous offenses in football, led by a quarterback whose only true challenge is remaining on the field for 17 games."
Names like Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, Brock Purdy, Lamar Jackson and Jared Goff got slotted above Burrow in that order from 1-5.
Once you get to the top-eight quarterbacks this season, it's hard to really slice one apart from the other. The QB play at the top has been fantastic. If Burrow had 1-2 turnovers instead of four, he'd likely be in that top five, and Cincinnati could be 4-1 or 5-0.
Alas, he faces the easiest remaining strength of schedule on ESPN's NFL FPI. The veteran passer can light things up the rest of the way and cement himself as a top-five hurler by the end of the season.
"We got to be smarter. We got to be smarter. Two fumbles in the red zone. A couple of personal fouls that hurt us, hurt our field position, gave them points on the board. We got to be smarter," Burrow said about the offensive operation on Sunday before touching on his bye week plans. "We'll see. I don't know. It's so early. I want to maintain my conditioning, my strength and conditioning, and certainly want to keep throwing. I'll try to find a plan. This is uncharted territory for me, having a bye this early, so we'll see."

title: Bengals Could Reshape Backfield With Star SEC Running Back in 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
The bye week is here for Cincinnati, prompting a little looking ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft. Pro Football Focus released a fresh mock draft projecting the first round this week, and Cincinnati added an offensive playmaker in the exercise.
The Bengals rolled with Florida running back Jadan Baugh with the 15th pick in the draft.
"The Bengals have fixed their offensive line and have a passing attack that opposing defenses are forced to respect," Gordon McGuinness wrote . "That's the ideal offensive environment in which to add a dynamic running back, and they would be well justified in using a first-round pick on Baugh. The Florida standout has averaged 3.72 yards after contact per attempt and forced 36 missed tackles this season."
Baugh could be a dynamic way to replace Chae Brown as he works his way through the final season on his Bengals contract.
The Florida bruiser has a nation-leading 12 touchdowns this season and is averaging 6.1 yards per attempt.
McGuinness framed his pick slotting to open the article. Cincinnati is right in the middle of the pack even with a winning record at 3-2. There are 11 teams at either 3-1-1 or 3-2 as of this writing.
"With the 2026 NFL season now past the quarter mark, it’s time to take a far-too-early look at how the NFL draft could shake out if the current draft order holds," McGuinness wrote. "This draft class has generated plenty of excitement over the past two offseasons, and it still looks very strong on paper as we approach the halfway point of the college football season.
"The Tennessee Titans currently hold the No. 1 overall pick, giving them the option to select a new quarterback or add an elite receiving prospect to support their current starter, Cam Ward. One note for this mock draft: Arch Manning does not appear in the first round. Given reports that several scouts don't view him as a first-round pick, I'm taking the approach that he is more likely to return to Texas than enter the draft if that remains the case."
Cincinnati has a long way to go before thinking about picking Baugh, and the team is hoping to be picking way closer to No. 32 than 15th.

title: Erick All Opens Up On Discipline from Zac Taylor During Bengals Recent Win
full_text:
Many eyes turned to Erick All last Sunday after he committed an egregious penalty and fumbled his second catch. Fortunately, the Bengals tight end avoided losing the fumble when the Dolphins recovered it out of bounds. He still, however, received an earful from Zac Taylor on the sideline after his costly penalty where he headbutted a Dolphins defender after the play.
All revealed the experience on First Word , saying it was the first mental error he had made regarding a penalty and that no coach had ever yelled at him as Taylor did on Sunday. He said that he did not intend for the headbutt to be egregious.
"I've never been yelled at by the coach like that besides like missing a block," All revealed. "It was my first stupid penalty like that, I didn't intend for it to be egregious, but it was just one of those little quick walk by things that you didn't think nobody was looking at you and it looked bad and it was stupid."
All then explained that Taylor's discipline after the play is something he respects, given how badly he messed up. He also said that, in that moment, he hoped the coaching staff still trusted him and that, if he got back on the field, they knew he wouldn't make that mistake again.
"Whatever he has to say you just respect it because you just messed up," All said. "You wear it on the chin and hope that they still trust you and can put you out there on the field and know that you won't do anything like that again."
Taylor showed what some may see as another side of himself as a coach, one they hadn't seen before, that being his increased aggressiveness toward players on Sunday.
"I look at Zac as that type of coach that's very transparent, he'll tell you how he feels and it just kind of surprised me hearing 'I'm surprised he hasn't done that with people in the past,'" All said. "Zac's a great coach, if he sees something that he doesn't like or that he wants you to fix, he'll voice it to you whether in practice, game, cameras on, it doesn't matter, and that's what I love about him."
With Tanner Hudson's recent injury, All should see an expanded role in the Bengals' offense. He finished Week 5 with three catches for 25 yards, including a 14-yard catch-and-run that extended a drive in which the offense scored and increased its lead by two scores.
He should continue to ramp up on offense and build more chemistry with Joe Burrow as the season progresses.

title: Browns Still Without Mason Graham, Make Moves To Fill Void Ahead of Sunday
full_text:
For a second straight week, the Cleveland Browns will be without standout second-year defensive tackle Mason Graham.
On Saturday, Oct. 17, the Browns announced that Graham, due to a lower-body injury, was questionable for Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens . The 23-year-old suffered his injury in the Browns' Thursday Night Football showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers just a few weeks ago.
Along with Graham's absence, the Browns will be without defensive linemen Mike Hall Jr. and Kalia Davis.
Each has been slowly but surely recovering, but to be safe, the front office has made a few moves to fill their voids.
In the wake of Graham's "questionable" diagnosis and Hall Jr. and Davis being ruled out, the front office has elevated defensive tackles Chris Williams and Sam Kamara to the active roster.
This isn't the first time the Browns have had to use either, though.
Kamara waltzed out in front of a packed MetLife Stadium last weekend, recording three tackles and the first sack of his NFL career. Williams, on the other hand, didn't get in the stat sheet, but will continue to help the Browns' depth at the position.
While both weren't able to do enough to guide the Browns to a victory over the Jets last weekend, they did receive praise from head coach Todd Monken.
The first-year leader shared that they both provided the team with valuable time on the field.
“Those guys that got elevated really gave us some valuable minutes,” Monken said following the 27-20 loss.
The defensive line is now expected to see the likes of Williams, Kamara, Maliek Collins and Adin Huntington. On the outside, Jared Verse, Sam Williams and Isaiah McGuire will eat up a majority of the snaps.
The line is certainly banged up , more than it has been in quite a while in Cleveland, but that shouldn't stop the young, hungry group that is available from putting together a strong showing against the Ravens.
It is never good to see a player injured, especially one as talented as Lamar Jackson, but with the Browns' recent injury spell, being able to face a Ravens squad that will not have him available is a big break.
Jackson is recovering from an ankle injury he suffered against the Tennessee Titans back in Week 4. Since then, he hasn't practiced.
In his place, the Ravens will turn to Tyler Huntley to be the man under center, someone Cleveland is relatively familiar with. While he doesn't have the speed that Jackson does, he is pretty mobile, and the Browns' defensive line will have to be ready to track him down if he starts to roll towards the hashes.
With how Kamara stepped up last week, and the opportunity available in front of Williams, there should be little concern for how the Browns will look defensively.
As long as the rest of the squad does its job, they should be good to go.
The Browns and Ravens will clash from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Ranking the Browns Players Most Likely to be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is less than a month away, and the Cleveland Browns sit at 3-2 with four more games to decide if they should be buyers or sellers .
The deadline in the NFL is different from what it is across other sprots, as it does not have a flurry of players changing teams. However, should the Browns fall in the standings over the next four games, then these are the most likely players to be moved.
Delpit signed a contract extension in the offseason, but a team may be willing to give a haul for the veteran’s services. The Browns used a second-round pick on Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, and he has been getting more playing time as the season has progressed. Delpit is a terrific defender, especially around the line of scrimmage and a return would require several picks, including as high as the first round due to his contract length. The 2027 draft will be loaded and the Browns could go in with three first-round picks.
Possible fits: Detroit Lions, Dallas Cowboys, Carolina Panthers
McNeil-Warren has been playing free safety, which is Hickman’s position. Hickman is also a free agent and the Browns spent big money on Delpit, so he may be too expensive for an extension next season. While Hickman will not get the same return as Delpit would, he can still  get some good picks. He was an undrafted free agent and the return for him would be a big win for the Browns.
Possible fits: Detroit Lions, Dallas Cowboys, Carolina Panthers
The defensive line would not be as productive without Collins. He has been a monster since signing with Cleveland, but he is on an expiring contract and can really bolster a contender’s defense. Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. will return from injury to fill in for Collins and if he does not resign with the team in the offseason, then it is best to get a return for him should the Browns find themselves down in the standings. The return could be two middle-round picks, which the Browns have plenty of to be able to package and move higher in the draft.
Possible fits: Cincinnati Bengals, Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos
Jenkins is currently out with a back injury and rookie Austin Barber has usurped him in the depth chart. He is a free agent at the end of the year, and playoff teams get desperate for offensive line depth to make it through the end of the season. Jenkins will not garner much in terms of a return, but he can be packaged with a late-round pick to move up one round.
Possible fits: Seattle Seahawks, New Orleans Saints, Los Angeles Rams
The inconsistent wide receiver could be intriguing for a contender. The Arizona Cardinals got a second-round pick for the disappointing Marvin Harrison Jr. , but Jeudy is older and would not be reuniting with his college quarterback. The wide receiver room got full with the emergence of Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, so Jeudy’s role has been limited. The Browns could get two middle- round picks in return for trading him.
Possible fits: Buffalo Bills, Philadelphia Eagles, Los Angeles Rams
Sanders hired an agent, which could mean that he wants to be traded out of Cleveland as Deshaun Watson has been the starting quarterback all season. Harrison Jr. also hired an agent to explore a trade prior to his transaction. Dillon Gabriel has to come off the injured list in the next couple of weeks, and he can move to the backup role. A return for Sanders is questionable as he was a fifth-round pick and did not play particularly well in his limited time last season.
Should losses pile up, then it may be wise to consider moving some pieces for future capital. The Browns have two-first round picks and three-fourth round picks for the draft. Andrew Berry has been stocking up and these players can bring in what Berry is seeking. For now the Browns have a winning record, but the NFL season moves fast and big decisions will have to be made.

title: How Andre Szmyt Has Evolved His Game to Earn a Big Contract Extension
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns haven't had the best luck in the past signing or drafting kickers.
Just a few years ago, the front office drafted kicker Cade York out of LSU in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft. At the time, it was a controversial decision. And years later, it still is, as York would end up going 24-for-32 in his first season before being waived.
Since Phil Dawson left the organization in 2013, 16 different players , including York, have served as placekickers.
Finally, though, the Browns may have ended such a cycle.
Ahead of the 2025 campaign, the front office signed undrafted free agent kicker Andre Szmyt, a standout at Syracuse University. While he was initially brought in to serve as extra depth for the organization during training camp and offseason work, he stole the spotlight from Dustin Hopkins and won the job.
Across the last two campaigns, Szmyt has been remarkable , making 34 of his 37 field goal attempts. He has also connected on 32 of 34 extra-point attempts.
One of the most impressive parts, though, is his consistency from deep.
He has knocked through seven field goals from 50 yards or further on eight attempts , with a long of 55 yards in 2025 and 56 yards in 2026.
ANDRE SZMYT FROM 56 YARDS FOR THE WIN! pic.twitter.com/64qGSekF7q
Not only does the 28-year-old have a pretty powerful leg, but a consistent one as well.
He is approaching franchise history, sitting with 24 consecutive field goals made, dating back to the 2025 season. Heading into a week six matchup against the Baltimore Ravens, that mark is the third-longest in Browns history.
If he can knock through a few more over the course of the next few weeks, he may be able to steal the No. 1 spot.
Currently, the top two spots are being held by Dawson, who recorded streaks of 27 and 29 consecutive made kicks.
🚨 UNDER THE RADAR: Browns kicker Andre Szmyt is quietly approaching franchise history. Szmyt has made TWENTY-FOUR consecutive field goals. That’s the THIRD-LONGEST streak in Cleveland Browns history. pic.twitter.com/YSYfAd8Hfo
But it is hard to imagine that a kicker with such a strong start to his NFL career is sitting in long-term limbo.
After putting together that strong rookie stint in 2025, he was a free agent this past offseason. Eventually, the Browns and Szmyt met on a one-year, $1,005,000 deal to bring him back to Cleveland for the 2026 season.
With how well he has started the year, though, and the historic record he is approaching, a contract extension has to be on the minds of both Szmyt and the front office.
Due to the immense struggles the organization has faced in the position over the last decade, locking down a leg like Szmyt's has to be a priority.
Most FG made without a miss this season Spencer Shrader          16 Will Reichard                 15 Andre Szmyt                  10 Chase McLaughlin       10 Evan McPherson          10 Jason Myers                   10 pic.twitter.com/YGELg0GDjy
Recent high-end kicker contracts have seen Chris Boswell of the Pittsburgh Steelers land a 4-year, $28 million deal, and Brandon Aubrey of the Dallas Cowboys sign a 4-year, $28 million deal with $20 million guaranteed.
While Szmyt is not at that level just yet, he could see a two-to-three-year deal worth roughly $4.5 million a season. That would give him a bigger picture of 3 years at $13.5 million.
For a kicker like Szmyt, who is still establishing himself in the NFL, a multi-year contract would provide the security and confidence to develop while protecting the Browns from making too significant of an investment in a relatively questionable position.
If he keeps this up, maintaining the consistency he has shown through the last 22 games, a piece of paper with a good chunk of change should end up on his desk in due time.

title: Browns Get Much-Needed Injury Boost Ahead of Ravens Showdown
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have a chance to top the AFC North again. Luckily for them, they just received big injury news.
The Browns lost to the New York Jets in Week 5 of the NFL season in a sloppy, rainy game. Cleveland emerged from the loss with additional injury concerns and opened Week 6 with 17 players on its injury report. Important players on that list included Carson Schewsinger, Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins, and Derek Barnett.
The Browns got some big names back at practice today: Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins and Derek Barnett. Not practicing: Mike Hall, Teven Jenkins, Kalia Davis. pic.twitter.com/FMTfDWDLkW
All four players returned to practice Friday, according to ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi. Their return raises the possibility that all four could play in the pivotal division matchup vs. the Baltimore Ravens.
The Browns' run game has been less than desirable early in the NFL season. However, those struggles could worsen Sunday if the Browns are without their lead back, Quinshon Judkins.
Without Judkins, Cleveland would likely lean on Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime, who joined the team from Minnesota’s practice squad this week. Dylan Sampson’s potential return could also affect the backfield. Judkins’ return to practice offers encouragement for a Browns rushing attack still searching for consistency.
Arguably, the three most important players to return to practice are Mason Graham, Carson Schwesinger, and Derek Barnett. Graham got hurt during the Browns' Thursday Night Football game vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers in a scary injury many thought would take him out for multiple weeks. Now, just two weeks later, the star defensive tackle has returned to practice.
Having Graham, Schwesinger, and Barnett available matters because the Browns need to stop the run against one of the league's best backs, Derrick Henry . The Ravens' starting quarterback, Lamar Jackson, hasn't practiced all week leading up to the Browns matchup.
Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is not present during media viewing portion of Friday’s practice, which indicates Tyler Huntley will likely start for the second straight week. Jackson missed every practice this week and hasn’t suited up since spraining his left ankle in a win over the…
Considering the Browns allowed 134 rushing yards just a week ago to a less talented Jets team, Henry will get his fair share of carries. Graham missed that matchup, and having him available alongside Schwesinger and Barnett would give Cleveland a better chance to contain Baltimore’s ground game.
The Browns now have several key players back at practice ahead of Sunday’s matchup with the Ravens. With Lamar Jackson, the Ravens' MVP quarterback, potentially unavailable Sunday, the Browns have a real chance to reclaim the AFC North.
The question now is whether the team will rise to the occasion as it did in Weeks 2 through 4 or fumble an opportunity as it did in Weeks 1 and 5.

title: 4 Burning Questions Facing the Browns This Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are set to host the Baltimore Ravens at home in week six.
After last week's loss to the New York Jets , the Browns have a couple of questions they need to answer.
So far this season, Quinshon Judkins has yet to get back to his rookie-season form.
Through 73 rushing attempts, Judkins has only 221 yards and one touchdown. That averages out to just over three yards per carry.
Last week against the Jets, Cleveland had their chance to finally find out who they were on the ground. New York ranked 25th in rushing defense, yet the Browns still couldn't run the ball.
Now, Cleveland faces a Baltimore defense that ranks 11th in run defense and always brings an extra juice against AFC North rivals.
WOW: #Browns defense guilty of THREE penalties on ONE play and lose Mason Graham #NFL #TNF pic.twitter.com/PzHiPklMOk
Last week, the Browns did a better job of not hurting themselves with penalties. Still, they committed six penatlies for 30 yards.
On the season, Cleveland has the most penalties in the NFL with 49.
It has even been so bad at times that somehow the Browns managed to draw three penalties on one play.
A big key to getting the win on Sunday is playing clean football.
Through the first four games, Todd Monken called easy plays where Deshaun Watson just had to get the ball out to his playmakers.
This allowed the Watson to find confidence, the Browns to score points, and ultimately was the recipe for that 3-1 start.
Then the Jets game happened. It seemed as if Todd Monken was not play-calling as usual. While the rain may have played a factor, Cleveland still has to stay true to what they can do well.
Time after time, Deshaun Watson has proved that he is not the best at pushing the ball downfield. Even if he had a good throw, receivers like Isaiah Bond weren't able to make the plays happen.
It is incredibly important that the Browns call simpler plays for Watson and the Offense, especially when navigating the Ravens' defense.
Again, once the Browns called bad plays, dropped passes, and got themselves in a hole they weren't able to bounce back.
Coach Monken needs to rally his troops and get their heads back in the game in times of poor performance. Let's be honest, there is almost guaranteed to be at least one of those moments every game.
Overall, they will need to have their heads in the full 60 minute game.
No matter what happens, neither team will give up. That's AFC North football.

title: Browns Rookie Receives Highest PFF Grade among 2026 Draft Class
full_text:
After five weeks of the 2026 NFL season, PFF put out their rookie rankings by overall grade.
While many believe Cleveland won the 2026 NFL Draft , the rookie who ranks atop all the others may not be the one you're thinking of from the Brown and Orange.
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is looking special pic.twitter.com/zcF1Nj0Bsb
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has the highest PFF grade of any rookie this season through the first few games.
Somehow, the prospect fell all the way to pick 58 overall in April.
McNeil-Warren currently has a PFF grade of 89.9.
This number not only ranks him as the best of all rookies, but also the best of all 96 NFL safeties.
As for the stat line, EMW has 22 total tackles with only 4 targets allowed over 109 total snaps. Additionally, his average passer rating allowed per game is only 27.6.
But it's not necessarily the numbers that are the reason why the rookie is so great.
If you showed a regular fan highlights of the Browns defense, they could never tell McNeil-Warren is only five games in to his pro career.
The reason? His instincts.
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is ready for primetime Watch how he closes QUICK on both of these balls intended for DK Metcalf to make two high quality pass breakups 👀 pic.twitter.com/brnADB0XoX
Just watching the young stud is incredible. He is already out there jumping passes, making reads, and ultimately playing like a seasoned veteran. The Browns truly have found a playmaker for their secondary
At this point, he is just having to split snaps with Ronnie Hickman. Ultimately, the Browns may decide at some point in the future to move on from Hickman as well, which would free up more snaps for EMW.
Something else we can't just overlook is the other rookie on this PFF top-graded list, who you may have thought sat at the top. Denzel Boston has simply been a beast for the Browns this season.
In five games, the second-round pick out of Washington has 16 catches, with three of those being touchdowns.
Not only does he lead all rookies in receiver yards with 330, but here are some elite NFL names who Boston has out gained:
Clearly, the Cleveland Browns knew what they were doing in the 2026 NFL Draft, especially in the second round.
Outside of Emmanuel McNeil-Warren and Denzel Boston, the Browns have had great success from KC Concepcion, Austin Barber, and Spencer Fano.

title: How Audric Estime Could Work His Way Into Legitimate Playing Time With Browns
full_text:
The running back room has been depleted with injuries and ineffectiveness . Backup Dylan Sampson landed on the injured reserve list during the first game of the season and his replacement Reheim Sanders joined him this week. The Browns signed Jaleel McLaughlin to replace Sampson. The next man up for Sanders is now Audric Estime.
Estime comes from the Minnesota Vikings practice squad and he will look to contribute to the Browns’ offense right away. Quinshon Judkins has struggled so far this season and the running attack has stalled as a whole. The running game could use a new look after five games to allow the offense to thrive.
The 5’11 227 pound back runs hard and never stops moving his legs. Estime has been in the NFL for two seasons and has amassed over 500 yards with a 4.2 average per carry. That average is greater than Judkins’ average per carry by over a whole yard. McLaughlin only has two carries all season and the Browns will have to give carries to all the backs to try and find any improvement.
When he played for the New Orleans Saints in 2025, he had rushing attempts out of the shotgun formation. The Browns’ offense mainly plays out of that formation, which has led to them struggling to run the ball. The running back needs terrific vision as he does not start with momentum before getting the ball and has to find cracks in the line. For the Saints, Estime showed that he has the patience to find an opening and a large frame that does not allow him to get tackled by the first defender.
Deshaun Watson got sacked eight times last week with pressure coming from everywhere. The running backs did not do a good job of stepping up to chip or block defenders. Estime has taken interior defensive linemen one on one to help protect the quarterback. The offense was exposed last week with all the blitzing and Estime can gain serious playing time if he can help buy Watson additional seconds to throw the ball.
Estime’s ability out of the shotgun formation will help him earn legitimate playing time for the Browns this season. Todd Monken insists that Watson and the offense operates best out of shotgun and Estime will bring experience and production to the position group.
He will be in on obvious passing downs to block an extra defender and with the injuries to the other running backs, he should get carries as well. While he will not be an every-down back, he can use his abilities to get legitimate playing time for an offense that needs any type of positive change running the football.

title: Is Shedeur Sanders’ Time in Cleveland in Jeopardy?
full_text:
So far in the 2026 season, Deshaun Watson has surprised pretty much everyone.
After being named the starter right before the season, many thought Watson would only last two games before being removed for Shedeur Sanders .
However, Watson continues to be the guy for the Browns. So far this season, Watson has led the Browns on three game-winning drives in just five games.
While the Browns organization has expressed that they do not want to move on from the second year quarterback, there may be a new development from Sanders' side of things.
Last week, Sanders signed with a new agent for representation.
While it may be a bit of a stretch, former Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. did the same thing and was traded just a week later.
Marvin Harrison Jr signed with an agent & was traded the same wk.. Shedeur Sanders now has an agent.. https://t.co/A2JGviWe6V
While there is still an unlikely chance the Browns deal Shedeur Sanders, getting an agent may sway his mind.
At the moment, Sanders has been content being the Browns backup. According to the media, he is taking the time to watch and learn from Deshaun Watson.
However, if the new agent comes in and pursuades him to push for a trade due to a starting job potentially somewhere else, you never know what may happen.
Regardless, Sanders has a ton of young and raw talent. It is most likely better for him to get this time to watch and develop, knowing he may take over the starting job for Cleveland soon.
Cleveland simply can't afford to lose Sanders.
The Browns finally have a somewhat stable quarterback room. For the past few seasons, its been the story of the starter going down or playing bad, and having to be replaced multiple times per season.
Now, with Deshaun Watson winning games and the young Shedeur Sanders developing on the bench, the Browns are actually looking alright for the future.
There have been many talks about when Sanders could see the field. It may be this season, it may not even be next year.
But let's look at the facts. If the Browns go on a slide and start losing games, let's say they fall out of playoff contention.
The moment that happens they should put Shedeur in to at least let him get in game starting reps when you know when your season will end.
Now let's say Deshaun Watson takes the Browns to the playoffs, and even gets resigned next year.
No matter how much they pay him and for how long, Deshaun Watson is still currently 31 years old and will be 32 by this time next year.
Clearly, the Browns will need another option in the near future. If Sanders can be patient and take more time to develop and learn, he can be ready to go the second the Browns call on number two.

title: Browns Receiver Criticized by Former Star After Disappointing Jets Defeat
full_text:
After the Cleveland Browns lost their week five matchup against the New York Jets, former Browns receiver Jarvis Landry had comments for Isaiah Bond .
In the game, Bond had to step in for the injured KC Concepcion.
By the end, Bond had been targeted seven times. Out of those targets, he had three catches for 74 yards.
However, the second-year man also had numerous plays where he had bad drops, including one that was late in the close game.
Jarvis Landry calls out Isaiah Bond for his costly dropped pass against the Jets, insisting the Browns receiver needs to adjust after the mistake and live up to Cleveland’s high standards for its wideouts. "Isaiah Bond, my dog, if you can't catch that s**t without gloves, you… pic.twitter.com/wZXYKe9Fem
Not only did Landry rip the young receiver for his mistakes, but he also continued to talk about how Bond wasn't "living up to Cleveland's high standards for its wideouts".
In the contest at MetLife Stadium, it did not stop raining throughout the entire contest.
With that being said, Bond was playing the game without gloves on. This was something Landry also made note on, even inserting himself in the situation.
"I'm catching that s**t. Period. Ain't no ifs, ands, or buts. If I drop one without gloves, best believe the next time I come on the field, I got gloves on or I got tape on my fingers or something." Landry said.
Coming into this offseason, Isaiah Bond was someone who flew under the radar for the Browns.
We knew he was going to have to come in and compete for a job on the team, especially after Cleveland drafted two receivers in the 2026 NFL Draft .
A lot of speculation the #Browns should trade Jerry Jeudy Im on board with anything that gets Isaiah Bond more targets Two weeks in: 1 target 1 catch- he’s way too talented to not get the ball pic.twitter.com/N0lwLzfKah
Throughout training camp, the former Texas Longhorn stood out. Day after day it seemed as if Isaiah Bond was the big name who was contantly making big plays and scoring touchdowns.
It almost seemed as if the Browns found another stud who was going to have a breakout season.
But then came game days. At the start of the season, Bond was barely being used. Through the first four games, he only had two catches on his only two targets for a total of 12 yards.
So how can the Browns use him more?
KC Concepcion's health is the main question at the moment for Bond's playing time. However, even when the rookie comes back, I think Bond deserves to get more reps over a guy like Jerry Jeudy.
Bond has showcased in both games and the offseason his breakaway speed. If the Browns utilize him as a deep threat, that will open up the field for KC Concepcion who had been getting great separation off the line of scirmmage.
Tough day for Isaiah Bond. I truly believe he’s better than what he put on tape, but man… Can’t help thinking about what could’ve been. Head up, 007. Still a long season ahead. #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/3iQtpwRgsg
Overall, if Bond wants to redeem himself, he will just have to do it on the field. Going forward, he needs to be able to catch wide open passes. If he can't, adjustments need to be made.
Who knows, maybe Jarvis Landry himself will help out the young pup with some pass catching drills.

title: Browns Should Consider Flipping Jerry Jeudy For This Overshadowed Wideout
full_text:
The current situation of the Cleveland Browns ' wide receiver room is headlined by the excellent play of both rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who have combined for 34 catches for 449 yards and three touchdowns through the first five games of the season. Cleveland’s next leading receiver is second-year guy Isaiah Bond with 86 receiving yards. Bond struggled with a couple of drops vs. New York, but has gotten just nine targets this season.
Past those three, the rest of the room seems to be up in the air, and the one guy who is the odd man out is popping up in more and more trade rumors. That would, of course, be Jerry Jeudy, who is currently sixth for Cleveland in receiving yards and receptions.
Jeudy’s cap hit of $10.3 million this season, as well as $13.4 million in 2027, does not seem worth the price at the moment or in the future. Cleveland will be looking to trade him ; that’s no secret, but could it be for another receiver who has also seemingly lost his place in the room?
That would be the Jags wideout Brian Thomas Jr.
Thomas is now in his third season with Jacksonville, and after an unbelievable rookie season that showed him producing 87 receptions for over 1,200 yards and 10 touchdowns, his play has slowed down. The Jaguars hired Liam Coen last season, and since then, it doesn’t seem like Thomas has been a focal point of the offense.
An ankle injury also caused Thomas to miss three games last year, but through five games this season, the Jags offense has pivoted towards Parker Washington, Brenton Strange, Jakobi Meyers, and even sixth-round pick Josh Cameron over Thomas.
Now, a trade involving Jeudy for Thomas would have to come with some sweetening on the end of Cleveland, as Thomas is three years younger than Jeudy, and Thomas is making just $4 million on the cap this year, and just $4.6 million next season.
The Browns would most likely have to give up at least a fourth- and fifth-rounder alone, but if the Jags don’t see much value in Jeudy, Cleveland would have to ramp it up to a third, possibly.
Cleveland and Jacksonville have a recent history of trading with each other, as we know from the Travis Hunter & Mason Graham trade, along with the trade that brought Tyson Campbell to Cleveland in exchange for Greg Newsome.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: Cowboys Make 2 Key Roster Moves To Help Depleted Secondary vs Packers in Week 6
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' secondary has been a sore spot for a second straight season, allowing 227 passing yards per game and 10 passing touchdowns through the first five weeks of the season.
Christian Parker was hired as defensive coordinator with the hope of an immediate improvement in the defensive backfield, which has been his specialty throughout his career, but there have been no results. To be fair to Parker, he's been dealt a difficult hand.
The Cowboys have been plagued by injuries at key positions, with starting safeties Malik Hooker and Jalen Thompson both missing extended time, along with key members of the secondary like starting cornerback Cobie Durant, P.J. Locke, Alijah Clark, and rookie Devin Moore.
It hasn't been pretty, and with the recently acquired Joey Porter Jr. officially listed as questionable entering the team's Week 6 clash against the Green Bay Packers in primetime, the unit is especially thin.
Luckily, the Cowboys decided to call in some reinforcements ahead of Sunday Night Football, elevating two players from the practice squad ahead of the crucial game.
In anticipation of this week's game, the Cowboys have elevated safety Juanyeh Thomas, who has become a fan favorite throughout his career in Dallas, and cornerback Derion Kendrick, who signed a one-year contract with the team in free agency.
Kendrick was part of the team's final roster cuts before he was re-signed to the practice squad. Thomas, meanwhile, left the Cowboys in free agency to sign with the Indianapolis Colts.
Thomas spent four years with the Cowboys before leaving in free agency, but he re-signed with the team at the end of September. Thomas, who was placed on the reserve/non-football illness list last season due to chronic migraine attacks that were affecting his vision, had said he always wanted to return home to Dallas.
Now, he will get an opportunity to rejoin the team on the game day roster and provide some much-needed depth to the Cowboys' wounded secondary. Let's see whether he is called on to play significant time and make an impact on Sunday night.
Total Defense : The Cowboys rank No. 31 in total defense entering Week 6, ranking ahead of only the Detroit Lions. Dallas' defense is allowing a whopping 395.4 yards per game, while allowing 16 total touchdowns.
Pass Defense : Dallas ranks No. 21 overall in pass defense, allowing 227 yards per game and 10 touchdowns. The Cowboys are one of just six teams in the league to allow double-digit passing touchdowns.
Run Defense : The Cowboys' run defense has been dreadful, ranking dead last in the league and allowing 168.4 rushing yards per game. Dallas allows 12 yards more per game than any other team in the league, which contributes to the unit's inability to get off the field on third downs.

title: Updated NFC East Odds See Cowboys Soar After Devastating Jalen Hurts News
full_text:
The NFC East has been wide open through the first five weeks of the 2026-27 NFL season, with the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles in a virtual dead heat at the top of the division.
However, that has now all changed.
On Saturday afternoon, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter dropped the stunning news that the Eagles have placed star quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve due to his "superficial blood clot." The team not planned on placing Hurts on IR, but further consultations with the doctors led to the decision.
Now, Hurts will be out indefinitely, and the Cowboys' odds to win the division have surged. According to DraftKings Sportsbook , the Cowboys are now favored to take home the NFC East. Following the team's embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last Thursday, the team was listed at +180 to win the division. Dallas is now listed at even money (+100).
Not only do the Eagles go from favorites to win the division, but because of the uncertainty surrounding Hurts and the length of his absence, the team's odds have plummeted from +170 to +385.
They are now the third most likely team to win the division behind the Cowboys and New York Giants (+270), according to the oddsmakers .
Some of the interesting fallout from the Hurts situation is the Eagles signing backup quarterback Joe Milton III off the Cowboys' practice squad. Because Milton was signed off the practice squad by another team, he immediately must stay on their 53-man roster for at least two weeks.
That means that the Cowboys could be facing off against a Joe Millton-led Eagles squad in primetime on Monday Night Football in Week 7. What a wild turn of events that would be.
But for now, and most importantly, we wish Hurts a full and speedy recovery. There is no timetable for his return, but we know he will at least miss a minimum of four weeks after his move to injured reserve. Whether he returns this season remains to be seen.

title: Dallas Cowboys Projected  to Be Major Suitors at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
With the Dallas Cowboys' defensive overhaul failing miserably over the first five games of the season, the expectation is that the team will be active at the trade deadline.
Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox agrees with that expectation, as he predicts the Cowboys are going to be among the most aggressive teams next month .
"The Cowboys made a splashy move for Williams at last year's deadline, and they've already traded for Porter and Rashan Gary since the start of the offseason. Unfortunately, Dallas' flurry of additions hasn't yielded a playoff-caliber defense," Knox wrote.
We don't really have to guess this will be the case because owner Jerry Jones has said on several occasions the team will continue to seek out deals to improve the defense.
And he has said so even after the recent trade for Joey Porter Jr. with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
"I think the door is always open to get better. I know that's almost a cliche, but I'm never shut down from trying to get something that would really advance the needle, especially one that could do it now and into the future," Jones said.
The Athletic's Jonathan Jones even reported that Jones is not messing around when he says the Cowboys are open to doing more .
"They are running out of tradable resources to confront today’s problems," Jones stated. "But I’m told that won’t prevent Jerry Jones from making some sort of move if he feels it necessary before the Nov. 10 deadline."
Edge rusher is far and away the position the Cowboys need to add to the most, although you can certainly make an argument for just about every position on the defense with how poorly the unit has performed this season.
Despite having 76 pressures over five games , according to Pro Football Focus, the Cowboys have only five sacks thanks to the inability to get home, which has only exposed a lackluster secondary even more.
Guys like Rashan Gary, Von Miller and Donovan Ezeiruk have been major disappointments, with Gary having one sack, Ezeiraku having 0.5 and Miller having none.
Rookie Malachi Lawrence just notched his first sack in Week 5, but we can't say we're totally surprised he is off to a quiet start because it was always assumed he'd need time to develop.
The Cowboys don't just need to add a body, either. They need a substantial addition at the position. The problem is top-notch edge rushers are rarely available, and if they are, they're costly.
But Jones has expressed a sense of urgency at his age and a willingness to mortgage the future for this year's team, so anything is possible for the Cowboys come November.

title: 3 Reasons Cowboys Fans Should Be Confident Dallas Will Beat Packers
full_text:
This weekend will be huge for the Dallas Cowboys. They enter Week 6 with a record of 2-3, and the hope surrounding their once promising 2026 campaign has been dwindling .
Even so, the door is still open for them in the NFC East , thanks to the struggles of all their rivals . Of course, the only way they can take advantage of that is to start winning games. Their next chance to do this is during a showdown on Sunday Night Football against the Green Bay Packers.
Green Bay enters the weekend 3-2 and might feel like a daunting matchup for Dallas. While they're more than capable of running away with this one, here's a look at three reasons Cowboys fans should have some confidence against the Packers.
Losing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5 was horrific for the Cowboys' confidence. If there was anything positive from it though, it would need to be that they played on Thursday night. That means they had a few extra days of rest, and considering how banged up they have been this is a good thing.
Dallas had plenty of time off to recover, and it's allowed the coaching staff more time to dissect exactly what went wrong. They've toyed with moving Christian Parker to the booth and have had Jaishawn Barham play on the edge. These are things that typically happen during bye weeks, but the Cowboys had enough time this week to make some much-needed changes.
Green Bay started this season slow, thanks in large part to injuries. Micah Parsons has yet to return and they won't have Edgerrin Cooper or Javon Hargrave in Week 6. The Packers also won't have Josh Jacobs, who is on the Commissioner's Exempt List until Week 7.
All those reasons will help Dallas, but perhaps not as much as the fact that Green Bay is coming off an emotional win in Week 5. The Packers knocked off the Chicago Bears, keeping them in the NFC North race. As Dallas fans know, this can sometimes have a negative impact on the focus the following week, especially for a team that's dealing with so many absences.
One factor that could really help this week for the Cowboys is the addition of Mike Pettine. The newly-signed senior defensive assistant is expected to help Christian Parker, who has seemed overmatched at times this season.
Pettine not only brings plenty of coaching experience, but he's no stranger to the NFC North. Not only was he previously a defensive coordinator for the Packers (2018-2020), but he spent the past four seasons as an assistant with the Minnesota Vikings where he was on the winning side in three of the past four meetings with Green Bay.
The Packers have been inconsistent on offense, thanks in large part to their struggles in the run game, which could play into the hands of Parker and Pettine as they look to get things corrected in Dallas.

title: Joey Porter Jr Injury Update Stirs Further Concern For Week 6 Availability vs Packers
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys secondary just can't catch a break. The defensive backfield has been plagued by injuries throughout the first five weeks of the season, with starters Malik Hooker, Jalen Thompson, and Cobie Durant all missing time.
Even when players are technically healthy, they have been last-minute scratches because of a stomach bug . Sorry, Joey Porter Jr.
Since joining the Cowboys in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Porter has played in just one game. He had a standout performance in that outing, allowing zero catches, but he missed last week's loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after he was sent home from the stadium for vomiting in the locker room.
This week, there was some optimism that Porter would be able to return to the field and suit up against the Green Bay Packers , but now even that is in question after he popped up on the official injury report with an ankle issue .
And with the latest update from NFL insider Ed Werder, it looks like there is real concern that Porter could miss the Week 6 primetime game at Lambeau Field.
According to Werder, Porter "rolled his ankle" in practice this week. While that in itself is not concerning, it's the phrasing from Werder that followed that raises concerns about the cornerback's availability.
"A source involved says Porter is hoping to play and that his game status has nothing to with his contract," Werder wrote on X.
A hope and a prayer, that is what Porter's status for Sunday will come down to. And throwing in that "contract" note doesn't make anyone feel any better. It's a reminder that Porter had a "back injury" that miraculously healed as soon as he was traded to Dallas.
I’m told #Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter rolled his ankle in practice this week, an injury that has him listed as questionable tomorrow night against Green Bay. A source involved says Porter is hoping to play and that his game status has nothing to with his contract. pic.twitter.com/tEx2Ka7Rdm
The back injury kept Porter out of action for the entire preseason, training camp, and the first three weeks of the season. He played in Week 5 as soon as he was traded to Dallas, but he has been nowhere to be seen since.
Let's just hope that Porter gets back onto the field sooner rather than later, and that it truly has nothing to do with his current contract situation.

title: New Cowboys 2027 Mock Draft Lands Fast-Rising Defensive Lineman
full_text:
Entering Week 6 of the 2026 season for the Dallas Cowboys feels a lot like when they were entering Week 6 of the 2025 season. Their offense is once again one of the more explosive in the NFL, but their defense is an absolute mess .
Dallas spent the offseason trying to correct their defensive issues, signing Christian Parker as their new defensive coordinator and then re-tooling the roster to fit his scheme. Through five games, the Cowboys are just 2-3 and the defense is largely to blame as Parker's unit has not made any progress .
That means the 2027 offseason will also feature plenty of changes on defense, and that's the focus for Pro Football Sports Network's Alec Elijah in his latest NFL mock draft. Elijah has Dallas making its first pick at No. 21 overall, which is where they land Tennessee defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam .
At 6-foot-2 and 305 pounds, Gilliam has the build to play on a three-man line for Dallas. As Elijah says, he's also an incredibly disruptive presence who has been flying up draft boards in recent weeks.
"The Cowboys’ defense ranks near the bottom of the league in total defense, and its struggles have been impossible to miss. Fans have grown more vocal about the unit’s issues after each loss. Fixing the problem starts up front, and Xavier Gilliam has been one of the biggest risers in the class, emerging as one of the most disruptive interior defenders in college football," Elijah wrote.
"Gilliam’s 98.7 PFN DT Impact Score leads all FBS defensive tackles. His ability to collapse the pocket and consistently make plays in the backfield has made him the driving force behind one of the nation’s top defensive lines in Knoxville. He would give Dallas a high-motor interior presence who can generate pressure without blitz help, making life easier for everyone behind him and helping restore some toughness to a defense that badly needs it."
While Gilliam has the size of a run defender, it's been his pass-rushing that has made him a star. The Penn State transfer has exploded for the Volunteers, recording 22 tackles, 10 tackles for loss, five sacks, and two forced fumbles through his first six games. That's the type of production Dallas is missing on their defensive line and could make a huge difference for a defense desperate for playmakers.

title: Cowboys Hoping to Make Change With Caleb Downs' Role in Week 6 vs. Packers
full_text:
With the Dallas Cowboys having been ravaged by injuries in the secondary this season, it has forced them to deploy rookie defensive back Caleb Downs in a less preferred spot.
Through five games, the Cowboys have seen safeties Malik Hooker, P.J. Locke and Jalen Thompson all get hurt, with Thompson and Locke landing on injured reserve .
As a result, Downs has played almost exclusively at safety the last two weeks, with just eight snaps in the slot in that span.
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer admitted that is not where the Cowboys prefer him to play, but they've had to deploy him there because of the aforementioned injuries.
However, Schottenheimer hinted that the team could look to get Downs back into the slot, where he played the majority of his snaps over the first three contests.
“That’s not the design for Caleb,” Schottenheimer said of Downs at safety, according to Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News . “We want Caleb down near the line of scrimmage.”
“We want him around the ball," he added. "We want him playing nickel, but because we’re so beat up at safety, he’s had to play back there and we want to try to get him more involved and he’s able to make a lot more plays when he’s up around the line of scrimmage."
As you would expect, Downs says he is, well, down for whatever the Cowboys want him to do, and for whatever gets him around the ball more.
“Either one,” Downs said. “Wherever the ball is at. So if I get to be around the ball more at nickel, then that’s what it is.”
With the Packers' ability to attack downfield , Downs might actually be near the ball more in Week 6 if he plays at safety, but otherwise having him at the line of scrimmage will typically get him more regularly involved.
Not only does that give Downs more coverage opportunities, but he can also be deployed to blitz more often.
Schottenheimer has promised change this week and we suspect one of those changes will be putting Downs back in the slot, where he can make a bigger impact.
How the Cowboys will cover for moving Downs back to the slot remains to be seen, though, as Locke and Thompson are still sidelined due to injury.
The Cowboys have some options when it comes to a running mate for Hooker, who will start at one safety spot. Markquese Bell and Alijah Clark are ready to go, and Dallas has Juanyeh Thomas as another option on the practice squad.
Downs will still see snaps at safety in base defense, but we'd expect to see more snaps in the slot on Sunday.

title: 4 Dallas Cowboys Facing Make-or-Break Game in Week 6 vs. Green Bay Packers
full_text:
Change is afoot for the Dallas Cowboys going into their Week 6 game against the Green Bay Packers.
During the week, head coach Brian Schottenheimer revealed there would be some "roster adjustments" following the embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week.
"I’m not going to get to a bunch of them. Obviously, there’s a competitive advantage. But there’ll be some roster adjustments you guys will see. Some will be more noticeable than others, and some will be subtle as you look at it," Schottenheimer said, per Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com .
With the Cowboys looking for solutions to fix their issues on the defensive side of the ball, players who have been struggling this season are on the chopping block more now than ever.
On the flip side, changes might lead to increased opportunity for other players and they must make the most of it or else their opportunity may not last long.
Here's four Cowboys who land in either one of those categories.
Bland is a weekly staple on this list and that isn't changing after his horrific performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. We keep hoping Dallas will make a change with Bland struggling as badly as he is, yet that hasn't happened yet.
But with the Cowboys having strong desire for change this week after the Week 5 debacle, perhaps we see Bland's snaps decreased in Week 6.
If not, another poor performance may finally lead to Bland seeing his role reduced the following week, especially if Cobie Durant finally makes it back from injury.
Ameer Speed and Joey Porter Jr. are questionable , and Durant is out once again, so Revel could see a bigger workload against the Packers.
It's very clear the Cowboys are as open to change as ever and if Revel can play at a high level with whatever snaps he's given, a more robust role could be coming his way.
Lawrence played his best game as a pro in Week 5 and was one of the very few bright spots on the team. The rookie notched his first sack and had two pressures in total.
Schottenheimer stated Lawrence should see more playing time this week versus the Packers as a result of last week's showing.
"He's played very well. I think he's starting to show the flash and the acceleration and the ability to rush the passer that we knew we were getting when we drafted him. I think he had a very good game against Tampa Bay, and you'll see him get more opportunities," Schottenheimer said of Lawrence .
If he steps up to help Dallas' struggling pass-rush, Lawrence will remain in a bigger role. If he doesn't, it might be back to his old one, which was already fairly sizeable.
Miller has been a total disappointment, but at least he has taken accountability for that .
"It's time for me to get rolling, too," Miller said. "I would like to point the finger at myself. If I get two plays, I need to find a way to make an impact on those two plays. If I get 10 (plays), I definitely should be able to have an impact on 10 plays.
"And don't let me get 15 and 20 plays. I have to be able to do something. And this Sunday, I'm just pointing the finger at myself. I have to make an impact with the type of burn that I'm able to get."
Last season, Miller notched his first sack with the Washington Commanders at Lambeau Field. He'll be hoping for a repeat this week or else his already dwindling role might get even smaller or cease to exist entirely.

title: J.K. Dobbins Gets Real About What's Ailing Broncos' Offense
full_text:
Entering Thursday night's matchup with the Seattle Seahawks, the Denver Broncos' rushing offense ranked 25th in the NFL, averaging just 86.2 yards per game. And people wonder why Bo Nix hasn't looked like himself.
Against the Seahawks, the Broncos rushed for just 74 yards, but they did score two touchdowns on the ground. That pair of touchdowns created a two-score lead that the Broncos' defense was able to protect for most of the game, forcing Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold to throw the ball 51 times.
Seattles's defense adjusted at halftime, and stopped the Broncos' run game in its tracks in the second half. It was one three-and-out after another, with the Broncos playing an excruciatingly impotent brand of offense.
The game went to overtime, but the Broncos got the win, prevailing 17-14 over the Seahawks . Despite Denver sitting at 4-2 after a brutal first six-week schedule, the narrative around the Broncos has centered on heavy criticism of Nix and the offense.
Echoing his head coach , Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins doesn't sound worried, pointing to how tough Seattle's defense is to explain why the offense could get nothing going in the second half.
"It's the Super Bowl champions," Dobbins said post-game. "They got a great defense. They adjusted... That's part of being in the NFL and part of playing these great teams with great defenses. They adjusted, and they did a good job."
Although Nix only passed for 106 yards, Seattle held the Broncos to just 94 net passing yards, due to a pair of sacks. It was pretty painful to watch at times, but Dobbins isn't wrong about the caliber of defense Seattle plays.
The Seahawks entered Week 6 ranked No. 2 in net yards and passing defense, No. 1 in yards per play and takeaways, and No. 3 on third down. The Broncos struggled to run and pass in the second half, and they obviously couldn't convert on third down much, but they protected the ball. Zero turnovers was a big reason Denver won that game.
Seattle's defense led them to a Super Bowl championship last season and is poised to defend its crown this season, if Darnold and company can get off the schneid. But Seattle was only the latest in a long line of top-tier defenses the Broncos have faced to start this season.
You can look at almost any of the key metrics; the Broncos have a bottom-five offense. Lest we forget, though, the Broncos have faced the second-toughest schedule thus far when it comes to opposing defenses, and the toughest in opposing offenses.
With the worst of it behind the Broncos now, Dobbins sounds optimistic that the offense can finally take flight — if everybody does their part.
"Shoot, we just have to execute," Dobbins said. "You know, we've played some really good defenses. Every single team we've played has a really good defense."
That's not an excuse, by the way. Dobbins is simply pointing out the obvious. He understands that for the Broncos to turn the ship around offensively, the individual players have to bow up, take accountability, and excute.
"You've just got to go to the drawing board, and figure it out and execute," he said. "That is what it comes down to: execution."
Dobbins has carried the ball 81 times this season for 270 yards and two touchdowns. His 3.3 yards-per-carry average would be a career-low, if the rest of this season tracks the way it has started.
The soon-to-be 28-year-old has suffered a torn ACL, a torn Achilles, and a bad plantar fascia injury last season, leading some to wonder whether all the wear and tear has finally caught up to him. But given the level of competition the Broncos have faced so far this season, it's too early to say whether Dobbins has slowed down. The jury is out on that question.
Dobbins doesn't look quite as explosive, and nowhere near as decisive, as he did last year. Meanwhile, the Broncos' offensive line has struggled to consistently get push in the run game, which is all the more reason why he shouldn't be dancing around in the backfield; he needs to hit the hole with burst and get downhill.
Time will tell whether Dobbins and the Broncos' ground game can finally get rolling this season. But becoming more reliable on the ground would offer Nix the best chance to dig out of his slump.
As head coach Sean Payton said last week , "The hardest thing to do in this league is play that position if you're not rushing the ball."
Because the Broncos played on Thursday night, they're now enjoying a "mini-bye" — three extra days of rest and preparation between the Seattle game and Week 7's trip to take on the Arizona Cardinals. That might not be enough time to fully recharge the run game, but not having to play an elite defense for the first time since last season could do wonders for Dobbins and company.
And the same goes for Nix.
If the Broncos don't start producing better on the ground and rise up the rankings to at least somewhere in the teens, it's hard to see them cutting deep into the playoffs, even with a lights-out defense and even if Nix suddenly returns to 2025 form.

title: NFL Insider Reveals Broncos' True Feelings on Bo Nix Amid Bench Talk
full_text:
Since the Denver Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks , the sharks have been circling around Bo Nix.
From NFL On Prime 's Ryan Fitzpatrick criticizing Nix's effort, saying it was "almost disrespectful to the quarterback position," to a former Broncos teammate, Ben DiNucci, piling on , to local and national talking heads (and some fans) calling for Bo to be benched , it's been a rough couple of days for the third-year pro.
Lost in the rush to pile on Nix is the fact that the Broncos are 4-2 after playing the NFL's hardest schedule through the first six weeks. Unsurprisingly, that's what matters most to the Broncos, which is why the team isn't questioning Nix.
Long-time NFL insider Tom Pelissero further emphasized that on Saturday morning.
"The Broncos are 18-3 in Bo Nix’s last 21 starts. And while Nix and the offense clearly need to improve, there are no questions in the building about Nix’s competitiveness, drive and ability to get things rolling again," Pelissero wrote on X .
You'll notice that Pelissero stopped short of reporting that Denver isn't considering benching Nix, but it amounts to the same thing. The Broncos are confident that Nix can and will find his footing as they emerge from this tough first six-week gauntlet.
Since entering the league, Nix has been one of the NFL's winningest quarterbacks. He's 28-12 as a starter in the NFL, and currently sitting on a .700 career winning percentage.
The only active NFL quarterbacks with a better career winning percentage are Patrick Mahomes (.762) and Lamar Jackson (.712). Josh Allen is right behind Nix at .697. Nix has 40 regular-season starts under his belt, plus two playoff games (1-1).
In his second NFL season, Nix led the Broncos to a 14-3 finish, snatching the AFC West crown away from the Kansas City Chiefs, and earning the No. 1 playoff seed in the conference. He outdueled Allen in the divisional round of the playoffs, and we all know he would have gotten past the New England Patriots at home in the AFC championship game if he hadn't broken his ankle.
After what we saw on Thursday night, is there any doubt that Nix and the Broncos would have had every opportunity to beat the Seahawks in the Super Bowl? 2025 was such a magical season; the only thing I could have seen stopping Nix and the Broncos from hoisting the Lombardi Trophy was the injury bug, and sadly, that's exactly what happened.
But it's all water under the bridge. Woulda, shoulda, coulda.
In the present, Nix has the Broncos at 4-2 and very much on target for all their goals, which includes winning the division again, the No. 1 playoff seed, and going all the way. The Broncos' first six-week schedule was the toughest in the NFL, but their remaining schedule? The fourth-easiest.
The Broncos believe in Nix. The stats haven't been there this year, but the victories have. And as Sean Payton often says , it's much easier to fix a team's problems when you're winning.
Nix hasn't been great. He hasn't looked like his pre-injury self, but he's still doing enough to get past some top-tier opponents. Despite his slump, he's finding ways to win, which is another testament to him as a competitor.
Broncos believe Nix will turn things around. And with this remaining schedule, I believe they're poised to go on a run and really capitalize on how well they navigated those first six games, because guess what?
The Chiefs, Chargers, and Raiders still have most of those tough NFC West opponents to play, while the Broncos are through the worst of them, with only a road trip to face the Arizona Cardinals left.
When it comes to the Broncos' immediate schedule, there's really only one tough game to circle: Week 8's rematch against the Chiefs. But that'll be at Mile High, where Nix has never lost to Kansas City.
From there, Denver's road games against the Carolina Panthers (Week 9) and Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday (Week 12) could be tougher than people realize, but compared to what the Broncos have already faced, the scariest thing about those two opponents are that their East Coast away games.
We're still waiting to find out how much of the Raiders' 3-2 start was real. The Broncos will get to cross swords with them in Denver coming out of their Week 10 bye. Meanwhile, the Chargers are already out of the division hunt.
But really, it's all about the final three games, where the Broncos will play the Buffalo Bills at home in Week 16, the Patriots on the road in Week 17, and then the Chargers at Mile High in the season finale. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are undefeated at 4-0, but they still have to face the Seahawks, Rams, 49ers, Bills and Patriots, plus rematch the Broncos at Mile High.
Whatever is going on with Nix, I believe the early schedule has had a bigger effect on his play and statistical production than people realize. He may still be dealing with lingering effects of his ankle fracture, or perhaps something else has happened, but if the best predictor of future outcomes is past outcomes, he'll get it figured out.
There's a reason the Broncos have "no questions" about Nix's ability to get himself and this offense rolling, as Pelissero reported. In a league in which it is exceedingly difficult to win, Nix is 18-3 in his last 21 starts.

title: How Broncos' Week 6 Win Changed Their NFL Trade Deadline Outlook
full_text:
The Denver Broncos sit at 4-2 and are now enjoying a mini-bye after beating the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night .
The Broncos' offense did just enough in that game — establishing a two-score lead in the first half against Seattle's smothering defense — to allow Vance Joseph's unit to pin its ears back and bring home the win.
People are still understandably worried about Bo Nix and Sean Payton's offense, but the Broncos' wounded defense is absolutely rolling right now. And it's possible that game against the Seahawks could have altered the Broncos' outlook ahead of the November 10 NFL trade deadline.
I'll explain why here shortly, but before I do, keep in mind that Denver is unlikely to be a seller at the deadline. The Broncos weathered a brutal first six games and now get to benefit from the NFL's fourth-easiest remaining schedule; they're going to be in the conversation for the AFC West crown and likely the No. 1 conference seed, and such teams rarely go selling off roster pieces.
That being said, Thursday night's 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks gave me two thoughts realitve to the Broncos and the trade deadline.
First off, I am not advocating for the Broncos to trade Moss; I've been pounding the table since the summer for the front office to get him extended. But while he's missed time and was limited on Thursday night with a rib injury (20 snaps out of 85), Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine have stepped into the spotlight .
Against a desperate Seahawks passing offense that featured Sam Darnold as the trigger man and Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp as the receiving targets, Barron and 'K.A.D.' were targeted a combined 26 times (!). The Broncos' duo gave up plenty of completions, but they had their work cut out for them and did enough to limit Darnold and win the game.
KAD had a crucial interception late in the fourth quarter, too, while Barron played 100% of the Broncos' defensive snaps, which amounted to a whopping 85 plays. Neither young cornerback was perfect, but with two-plus games now as starters, the Broncos are realizing just how deep they are at the position.
With Moss in a contract year, it makes me wonder how secure his spot is. I don't think Denver would go looking to actively trade him, but if the phone rang, we know GM George Paton is always down to listen.
Beyond the emergence of Barron and Abrams-Draine, what further complicates the Moss issue is Ja'Quan McMillian's contract year status. As the Broncos' nickel, McMillian is a takeaway machine and one of the NFL's best, most clutch-time defensive backs.
And you can't pay everyone. So if the phone rings at Broncos HQ and the caller is interested in Moss, Paton is likely to listen. But one thing to keep in mind: in each of the past two seasons, the Broncos' cornerback depth has been tested by the injury bug, and without the quality personnel going five-deep, it would make it much harder to weather the storm, if something, say, were to befall the group later this season.
Keeping Moss around through the 2026 season would maintain that five-deep buffer at cornerback.
We've talked a lot about Nix not looking like himself this season, but the same is true of Mims. The fourth-year wideout/returner has dealt with two injuries since training camp started, which could be part of the explanation, but Mims doesn't look like he's giving the same full effort he always has.
Mims's low effort was apparent against the Seahawks. He failed to come down with a deep shot that would have put the Broncos on the goal line (thankfully, they still got there on that drive and scored), and there were several routes on tape where Mims wasn't even looking for the ball.
Now, it's possible some of that not-looking-for-the-ball thing was by design, but I doubt it. Mims's greatest value to the Broncos has always been his returner impact, and even that has been sub-par this season.
Mims's return yardage hasn't been there, even though we know teams try to punt away from him, and he lost a fumble on a return in Week 4 that led directly to the Broncos' second loss of the season. Whether his attitude is being affected by his expiring contract , the injuries, or the arrival of Jaylen Waddle , Mims hasn't looked like the same player of the past.
Given that Denver was very focused on bringing in returners this summer, and has Kolbe Katsis and Cameron Ross on the practice squad, it wouldn't surprise me in the least if Mims was traded before the deadline. If there's a market for his services, that is. But he is a two-time All-Pro/Pro Bowl returner, and he's only 24.
