title: Proposed Seahawks-Titans Trade Could Solve Seattle's RB Concerns
full_text:
Running the ball was easy for the Seattle Seahawks in 2025. Kenneth Walker III led the way with 1,027 yards while Zach Charbonnet added 730 yards. Charbonnet was the touchdown leader on the ground with 12, while Walker added five.
During the postseason, they lost Charbonnet to a torn ACL and Walker became a huge star. He helped carry the offense and was awarded the Super Bowl MVP award before leaving in free agency. With him gone, and Charbonnet not back from his injury, running the ball has become very difficult for Seattle in 2026.
Not only are the Seahawks still waiting for Charbonnet to come back, but they also lost rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price to injury as well. That has them leaning on Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, which has been a struggle. For that reason, CBS Sports' Jared Dubin believes the Seahawks should be willing to make a move for a running back and named Tony Pollard as an option.
Dubin admits that Pollard isn't the explosive threat he once was, but he's been a consistent producer who knows how to follow his blocks. Dubin also believes Pollard could be their answer in a committee if Price misses extensive time.
"The Seahawks cannot run the ball at all, as we have seen throughout this season and that was on full display on Thursday night against the Broncos. Pollard is no great shakes, but he's got 1,000 yards in four consecutive seasons and is at least a professional runner who can get what's blocked and a bit more," Dubin wrote.
"The Seahawks should be getting Zach Charbonnet back fairly soon, but we don't know if or when Jadarian Price will return. Pollard would be an upgrade over Emanuel Wilson and/or George Holani as a complement to Charbs. It's not the sexiest deal in the world and might not even be the best possible use of resources, but the Seahawks do need help in the backfield."
Pollard is in the final year of a three-year, $21.75 million deal signed in 2024. He had 1,000 yards in each of his final two seasons with the Dallas Cowboys and did so again in each of his first two years with the Titans. This year, he's off to a slow start with 273 yards and a touchdown through five games, although he is averaging 4.0 yards per attempt.

title: Early Options at a New Starting Quarterback for Seahawks in 2027
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have given Sam Darnold a chance to be the franchise quarterback. The 12 thought he had earned it after helping the team win a Super Bowl, but not even half a season later, all trust and hope for him are gone. Darnold has regressed significantly and can't be trusted not to turn the ball over.
Darnold's seven turnovers in the last four games are a direct reason why the Seahawks are 3-3 and looking like they will miss the playoffs. He was signed to a team-friendly deal of three years, $100 million in the 2025 offseason. The Seahawks created a potential out this upcoming offseason if they should feel the need to activate it.
There is a chance the Seahawks start over at quarterback going into next season, regardless of whether they might make the playoffs or not. General manager John Schneider and his front office staff have some good options.
​There was a time this 2026 NFL Season when the Seahawks had one of the most efficient quarterbacks and it wasn't Darnold. Through five weeks and the Thursday Night Football game, backup Drew Lock remains at the top of the league in quarterback rating at 127.3. Through most of the game versus the New England Patriots and the entire game versus the Arizona Cardinals, Lock has completed 72.9% of his passes for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions.
​The Seahawks should give Lock a chance to prove to the team that he can’t put the team in danger of losing late off mistakes like Darnold. What is the worst that could happen? Lock could have a late turnover that costs the team a win, but the team already has three of those losses. Lock could be the top option moving forward if Seattle needs a new starter in 2027.
​The 2027 NFL Draft is an option that the front office should take seriously if they need a new franchise quarterback. There are seven quarterbacks in the top 25 of ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr.'s latest board. Oregon's Dante Moore, Missouri's Austin Simmons and Notre Dame's CJ Carr are players the Seahawks should be interested in the most.
​Seattle has 11 picks in the 2027 Draft , but the problem is that if they need to move up for a quarterback, teams won't be interested in one of the multiple late day two or day three picks. If the Seahawks continue to lose, they might find themselves in a favorable spot to draft a quarterback in the first round without having to trade.
​One decision the front office could make that might be less favorable than the 2027 Draft or Lock is getting a temporary option. There is less risk for players who set to be free agents at the end of the season and there aren't great players, but they are serviceable enough to not throw late interceptions. Among the options who are set to be free agents next offseason are Kirk Cousins, Marcus Mariota (who beat the Seahawks in Week 3), Kyler Murray and Mac Jones.
​The Seahawks might look at the trade market too for disgruntled quarterbacks. Some options might include Philadelphia Eagles' Jalen Hurts, Baltimore Ravens' Lamar Jackson, Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow and Houston Texans' CJ Stroud. This is a risky move considering the Seahawks would have to give up a lot for these quarterbacks and pay them a lot of money. All options should be on the table if Darnold single-handedly costs more games.

title: 3 Risers and Fallers After Seahawks' Week 6 Loss vs Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks kicked off Week 6 on the road versus the Denver Broncos on a short week. Much like the Broncos, the Seahawks had the tough task of playing a game four days after another. This 17-14 overtime loss to Denver showed some real concerns for the team moving forward . Three Seahawks’ personnel should start to worry about their status on the team. There were also a couple of players who could have a bigger role on the team after Thursday’s game.
​Once again, linebacker Tyrice Knight showed why he is a quality-level starter for the Dark Side Defense. He started in place of Drake Thomas, who was out with an ankle injury. Knight accounted for eight total tackles. He was aggressive and quick to make plays against the Broncos' defense, who were trying to take advantage of the short passing game. If the Seahawks utilized a traditional 4-3 front as opposed to a 4-2-5, Knight would easily be a full-time starter.
​Both tight ends Eric Saubert and Nick Kallerup could count as one, but they are utilized differently moving forward. The Seahawks changed plans of having Brady Russell as the first-team fullback with Robbie Ouzts out for the year. AJ Barner has been taking that role, along with Saubert and Kallerup at times. Saubert had 16 offensive snaps and 20 special teams snaps while Kallerup had 10 offensive snaps and six special teams snaps.
​Wide receiver Irv Charles finally got his chance to play for the Seahawks after missing the first five games while still recovering from a torn ACL from last year with the New York Jets. Charles showed how much of a reliable player he was as a special teams player by making a big tackle in one of the 15 special teams snaps. The Seahawks like consistent and assertive special teams defenders. He might be proven to be a reliable player to trade for.
​It is time we take some serious thought about benching quarterback Sam Darnold after essentially giving the Seahawks their third loss of the season. He has lost three of the four games that he started and finished for the Seahawks. Seven interceptions in four games is an embarrassing statistic and he and the coaching staff promised the turnovers would stop. As of right now, the only reason the promise could be kept is if Darnold sits and Drew Lock starts.
​Darnold isn’t the only starter who should be worried about regressing. Right tackle Abraham Lucas should be highly concerned about one of the worst performances of the night. Between missing on blitz pickups, poorly facing the opposing edge rusher and being slow/latheratic on screen coverages, Lucas was a problem on Thursday. If he continues to play this poorly , the Seahawks might have a conversation about reducing his salary or replacing him.
​First-year offensive coordinator Brian Fleury went from being clear to being worried about his job to potentially being on the hot seat. Outside of Darnold, Fleury was the biggest reason why the Seahawks’ offense laid an egg until the final half of the fourth quarter.
Fluery continues to go with a power back in Emanuel Wilson, who is slow and has no vision and George Holani, who was awful in the one thing he was supposed to be good at: pass protection. If the Seahawks continue to struggle offensively, his first year as an offensive coordinator might be his only year.

title: The Seahawks Can Not Protect Sam Darnold
full_text:
Brian Fleury. Sam Darnold . John Schneider. Emanuel Wilson. George Holani. Rashid Shaheed. Elijah Arroyo. AJ Barner. Jadarian Price. If you want to fire off some anger and frustration at the offense of the Seattle Seahawks, there are a lot of potential targets. And after Thursday night, you can make an argument for adding the entire offensive line to the list.
I would characterize the Seattle Seahawks offensive line through six games this season as ‘inconsistent’. There have been games where it felt like the pass protection has been way ahead of the run blocking, and then games where the opposite felt accurate. Last night, it was most certainly the opposite (not that I was enamored by the run blocking either).
According to Pro Football Focus, Sam Darnold was pressured 27 times against the Denver Broncos. The six offensive linemen that currently make up Seattle’s front line (Haynes and Stephens rotate at right guard) were credited with 26 pressures allowed (multiple players can take blame for one pressure). Meaning very little was considered Sam’s fault.
Charles Cross, who has been relatively clean in pass protection this year with 7 pressures in the first 5 games, let up 4, including 2 QB hits. Abraham Lucas, admittedly already somewhat leaky this year , had one of his worst games ever with 7 pressures allowed, including 2 sacks, after 11 to start the season. Jalen Sundell threw in 4, ridiculous for a center, after 6 in prior weeks.
Grey Zabel, who seems to be in the midst of something of a sophomore slump (not that the playcalling is helping him), allowed 3, which actually isn’t a season high for him. Christian Haynes got wrecked, allowing a sack and 2 QB hits for 5 total pressures. And Beau Stephens, despite a reduced snap load, gave up 3. Everyone is to blame right now.
The problems aren’t over there. George Holani deserves a lot of criticism here. One of the reasons why you carry Holani on the roster is because of his abilities as a blocker. Supposedly, coming into the season, the team considered him their best pass protector out of the backfield. Through six games, he has been a complete disaster, and Thursday was a new low.
4 pressures on 12 reps. He’s allowed at least one pressure in every game this year, allowed three (including a sack) against the Chargers, and is currently graded at a 19.3 in pass blocking. He might be injured , but at this point Emmanuel Wilson (clean in 11 reps) and Jadarian Price (clean in 8 reps) are clearly superior options. And at that point, why even have George?
There’s a lot of stuff that needs to improve, fast, if this offense is going to right the ship. So the last thing we need is for the offensive line to become a liability. Maybe we need more max protect, but these players need to play better too. Fleury and Darnold can get it together all they want to , but if those guys can’t figure it out, you can forget about it.

title: Seahawks Defensive Dominance vs. Broncos Shouldn't Be Overlooked
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are disappointed after their 17-14 loss against the Denver Broncos in Week 6, but it shouldn't take away from the dominant defensive performance they put together, especially in the second half.
While the Seahawks surrendered a pair of touchdown drives in the second quarter, they managed to hold the team scoreless throughout the second half. The field goal they gave up in overtime to end the game was largely fueled by Sam Darnold's interception , which gave Denver great field position.
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald praised the defense after the game.
"I am really, really proud of our guys," Macdonald said postgame.
"Really, just the resolve. I think they executed a really high level for what we were asking them to do today. It's a really good offense, especially in the second half. Their offense, they did a great job. They played together, and our coaches did a great job of finding some solutions there after those two drives. So, it was great second half by those guys."
The Seahawks allowed just 168 total yards against the Broncos. Bo Nix threw for just 94 yards, while the rushing game managed only 74. For additional context, the Broncos gained just 32 yards in their final 29 plays, which is usually the ingredient for a victory. Unfortunately, the offense was not able to muster enough points to help them out.
The defense has always been the backbone of the Seahawks, and this season has proven that it will remain the same. The defense will only continue to play at a high level as offenses get more injured throughout the season and rely more on the ground game, which Seattle looks to feast upon.
The defense is why the Seahawks shouldn't worry too much about their record at this point in the season. While they already have as many losses as they did during the 2025 regular season, their defense has the tools to win a lot more games down the line.
The Seahawks are back in action in Week 7 when they take on Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III, and the Kansas City Chiefs. Kickoff is scheduled for 5:20 pm ET inside Lumen Field for Sunday Night Football.

title: 2 Reasons Why Seahawks Should Bench Sam Darnold (And 1 Reason Why They Aren't)
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are frustrated after a 17-14 loss against the Denver Broncos , where Sam Darnold threw two interceptions late in the game that ultimately cost them the victory.
Darnold has thrown seven interceptions in four games this season, which doesn't include his Week 1 drive, during which he suffered a glute injury that held him out for Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals. Ultimately, Darnold's struggles have prompted some to call for a quarterback change, but head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that he wouldn't be going to Drew Lock.
Here's a look at why Macdonald and the Seahawks coaching staff could be making a mistake, but also why they are sticking to their guns:
One could make the argument that the Seahawks could be 6-0 at this point in the season. The team is 3-3, with all of their losses coming by three points or less. In games like that, the smallest margins make the biggest difference, and that could be the case with Darnold's interceptions.
In each of his starts, Darnold has vowed to clean up the turnovers, but that has not happened yet. The team is losing its grasp on its spot in the standings, and a quarterback change could be what the team needs to wake the offense up.
It would be one thing if the Seahawks had an unproven backup behind Darnold who would spark something unknown. However, Lock is the quarterback the Seahawks would turn to if they did decide to move on from Darnold.
Lock proved in the first two weeks that he is capable of leading this team to victory, pulling off a comeback in Week 1, and looking like a starter in Week 2. The team ultimately has decided to keep Darnold under center, but they have a strong backup option if they were to make a change.
Ultimately, the Seahawks have struggled a lot , but Darnold is not the only reason. The offensive line struggled against the Broncos, and the run game has yet to come into its own. While Darnold is shouldering a lot of blame for the team's losses, it is far from the only thing keeping Seattle from winning these games.
Darnold has a higher ceiling than Lock, and that is ultimately why the team is keeping him in that position. The Seahawks may get desperate later on in the year if their spot in the playoffs becomes compromised, but for now, Darnold is their best option to win football games.
He just needs to take care of the football, which he has proven to do before. During the playoffs last season, Darnold never gave the ball up to the opposing team, which fueled their Super Bowl run. If he can find that energy and apply it to the 2026 season, the Seahawks could have a similar result.

title: Seahawks Get Good, Bad News Regarding Injuries
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are fresh off of a 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos where they could have benefitted from having some of their offensive depth healthy for the game.
The team has dealt with some injuries in the first half of the season, but a few players could be nearing a return in the coming games. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald spoke with "Brock and Salk" on Seattle Sports 710 AM and provided some clarity on players' availability.
Seattle Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price has missed the last three games due to a chest injury, but there is reason to believe he is going to be able to come back soon because he was placed on injured reserve.
Price has to miss a minimum of four games, which means he is out for the team's Week 7 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs. The team can, however, open his 21-day window to return from injured reserve very soon. There's a good chance that Price could be available for the team's Week 8 contest on Monday Night Football against the Chicago Bears on November 2.
Bradford, the team's starting right guard, is also on injured reserve, but Week 6 marked the fourth game of his absence. This means he is eligible to return from injured reserve and move back to the 53-man roster in time for the team to take on the Chiefs. Given that the Seahawks surrendered five sacks against the Broncos, having Bradford back in the lineup will be a big boost for the team.
The Seahawks activated Charbonnet on October 1, which means he has 21 days to join the 53-man roster, giving him until October 22, next Thursday. This means he will likely be on the roster at some point ahead of the Chiefs game, but it also doesn't mean he'll be ready to go.
The team has to put him on the active roster because if they do not, he will be out for the rest of the season. Seattle could move him to the roster but keep him inactive until he is ready to come back, which could be the direction the team ends up going in.
Macdonald did not have a clear update on his status, which means not much has changed, and it didn't sound very optimistic for him to return.
Arroyo left the team's Week 6 contest with a shoulder injury, but he is continuing to get some imaging and testing done to determine how long he will be out. It's not great news for the Seahawks, who don't have a ton of tight end depth on the roster. Arroyo's status is up in the air when the team plays the Chiefs in their next game on Sunday Night Football in Week 7.

title: Seahawks Won't Bench Sam Darnold After Loss to Broncos
full_text:
Through six games, Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold isn’t writing a great sequel to his Super Bowl-winning campaign from last season.
Darnold threw two back-breaking interceptions in the fourth quarter and overtime of the Seahawks’ loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday night, giving him seven picks in essentially four games played. However, head coach Mike Macdonald is standing by his quarterback.
Macdonald was asked about potentially making a quarterback change on his weekly radio appearance with Seattle Sports’ Brock Huard and Mike Salk, and he quickly said it wouldn’t be happening.
Later, Macdonald addressed reporters and doubled down on sticking with Darnold moving forward.
Are the #Seahawks in any way considering making a change at QB? "No." HC Mike Macdonald assesses his team's quarterback situation after Seattle's week 6 loss vs the Broncos on w/ @BrockHuard & @TheMikeSalk pic.twitter.com/GCyCSGUgPe
“I think we have a lot of faith in Sam,” Macdonald said. “Sam’s played great football for us. He’s done a lot of great things this year. We’ve obviously turned the ball over way more than we want to. I feel like there’s things on our end that can help him play better football, and I think he’s definitely part of the solution rather than the opposite.”
Macdonald said there’s a “sense of urgency” to improve in multiple areas, and especially on offense. The coaching staff is optimistic it can find solutions to the issues and help Darnold succeed.
“We just won a world championship with him. We believe in the guy; we see him every day, we see what he does, we see the plays that he’s been able to make, we see the actual talent. All those things. That’s where my mind is.”
Drew Lock essentially made three starts for the Seahawks when Darnold suffered a glute injury on the first drive of the season against the New England Patriots. Lock completed 72.9 of his 48 pass attempts for 422 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions.
Seattle is 1-3 since Darnold returned, largely because his interceptions have come at critical junctions in the game when Seattle has an opportunity to win the game. It’s hard not to look at the two sample sizes and wonder if the offense would perform better with Lock under center.
Macdonald, while acknowledging that Lock is a potential starting-caliber backup, shot down the idea that it’s as simple as a quarterback issue.
“I don’t think that’s doing the whole thing justice; there’s definitely more to the equation … I understand the question, but I think there’s more to it than just who’s playing quarterback,” Macdonald said.
Darnold will try to prevent the Seahawks from falling to 3-4 when they face the Kansas City Chiefs at 5:20 p.m. on Sunday, Oct. 25, at Lumen Field.

title: Should Seahawks Bench Sam Darnold? Seattle Legend Says Yes
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are losers of three of their last four games, including a 17-14 overtime loss at the hands of the Denver Broncos in Week 6.
The Seahawks had a chance to win, much like their other two losses, but two costly Sam Darnold interceptions in the fourth quarter and overtime led to the loss. With Darnold throwing seven interceptions in his last four games, it begs the question whether the team would be better with someone else, including backup Drew Lock.
Bruce Irvin, who won a Super Bowl with the Seahawks in 2013, wants Lock in at quarterback over Darnold.
There is a timeline in which the Seahawks could be 6-0, which would be their greatest start in franchise history. Still, they have lost three of their last four games by a combined eight points, which should be frustrating for a defense that is performing at a very high level. The Seahawks gave up just 168 total yards of offense against the Broncos, yet they were still unable to pull out a win. If the Seahawks had more consistent quarterback play, these losses would turn into wins.
After Darnold suffered an injury during the team's season opener against the New England Patriots, Lock stepped in and did what he needed to do. In his first game with the Seahawks, he completed 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and a touchdown. Most importantly, he did not throw an interception.
The following week against the Arizona Cardinals, he also played extremely well, completing 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns while also not turning the ball over.
Seattle doesn't need a wow factor at the quarterback position. Last year was full evidence of that. They just need someone who can keep the ball in Seattle's hands and kill the clock. With the running game not as consistent as it was last season, the importance of the quarterback not turning the ball over becomes that much more crucial.
Unfortunately for the Seahawks, they haven't gotten that level of play from Darnold this season, but they have gotten it from Lock.
I believe when the Seahawks play the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7, Darnold will be under center. It's hard to bench a Super Bowl-winning quarterback just a handful of games into the following season. Darnold has the ability to clean up this mess, but after several consistent weeks of the same mistakes being made, it does beg the question of whether his job is fully safe or not.

title: 5 Biggest Questions Facing 49ers Ahead of Week 6
full_text:
As the San Francisco 49ers get ready for a chance to go 6-0, what are some of the biggest questions on the roster entering their Week 6 matchup with the Washington Commanders.
The 49ers receiver room has been getting thin, and the team is going to be without Deebo Samuel in Week 6, making the group even thinner. With Samuel out, the team essentially shuffled Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, and Brandin Cooks as the second through fourth receivers behind Mike Evans.
Can the two young names step up, or will they lean on the veteran Cooks?
When Juszczyk suffered a knee injury in Week 4, the expectation was that he would be missing a couple of weeks. However, after missing one week, he is not only at practice; he is practicing in full . The 49ers' lack of skill players is going to push the team to get Juszczyk on the field for a significant role if he is healthy. What does that look like?
Dre Greenlaw is suspended for Week 6, and Garrett Wallow is likely to miss due to an injury. The team is going to give rookie Jaden Dugger his first look as an every-down linebacker in Week 6. Dugger was supposed to be a high-ceiling project, but playing so much as a rookie has raised the floor as well. How does he look with even more put on his plate?
The 49ers eased former first-round pick Mykel Williams back into action after he tore his ACL last year. Williams played 23 snaps, which amounted to about one-third of the defensive snaps. Williams hardly rushed from the interior in his debut, which is where he was most dynamic as a rookie. Will Williams step into a bigger role, and will they use him in a more versatile manner?
Colby has been better than expected through the first four weeks. However, once he had to step up in competition against the Seahawks, he fell back to earth. Now, he gets Daron Payne of the Washington Commanders. This could end up being an issue for Colby. San Francisco’s backup, Carver Willis, is currently injured, so they have to ride with Colby.

title: 49ers QB Brock Purdy's Reaction to Potentially Historic Stat Says It All
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has completed impressive stats since becoming the starter.
It's crazy to think that, in just his fifth season, Brock Purdy has already led San Francisco to a Super Bowl, an NFC Championship Game and a Divisional Round appearance in three of the last four years.
Having put up impressive efficiency numbers throughout his career, Purdy is on the brink of history, sitting just five pass attempts away from reaching the 1,500-pass threshold that would make him eligible to rank first all-time in passer rating.
His response upon hearing this stat line is relatively simple: "To be honest, I don't really know. Obviously, when you look at your stats, are you efficient with your completions and, I guess, not turning the ball over, throwing touchdowns, things like that. "
"I guess, yeah, your rating of course is going to be good. I guess it's, yeah, it's a good thing. But at the same time, I'm not getting done with games going, 'Alright, was my rating at least 100 and something?' I could really care less about that. It's more so, did I do my job well for my teammates? Did I compete and do everything I could to help this team win?
"I know it sounds cheesy, but that's the reality. That's what I'm thinking about and it's what matters. I guess that maybe reflects, though, playing pretty good quarterback play, so I'm not trying to act like it's nothing.
"But, it is cool. If I could answer that again too, I would say obviously it goes more into just me (laughter). I've got great coaches, a great team, dudes that help me be who I am and I'm just grateful that I get to be the quarterback for the 49ers so, yeah, it's cool."
And that's why he's deeply respected within the organization. He doesn't care about the stats. He only wants to be the best version of himself.
Purdy has made it clear in the past that his sole focus is bringing a sixth Super Bowl title back to the City by the Bay . Whether he achieves that remains to be seen, but his approach to the game is refreshing in an era where that kind of single-minded focus can feel increasingly rare.
This mentality extends further in trying to improve. He's on the cusp of something quite special, yet he doesn't care. He simply wants to win football games.

title: Brock Purdy Explains How 49ers DC Raheem Morris Helped Him Improve
full_text:
Brock Purdy has been playing extremely well this season. His performance has played a key role in the San Francisco 49ers' 5-0 start.
Purdy seems to be playing sharper and more comfortably than ever before. Part of that is the help he has, as well as the work he put in the offseason. However, there’s another factor that helped him out.
Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris is someone whom Purdy has credited with his improvement this year. Now, you may wonder how a defensive coach is helping an offensive player?
Morris isn’t working one-on-one with Purdy like quarterbacks coach Mick Lombardi is, or even Klint Kubiak and Kyle Shanahan. But what he did do was give him quality reps in training camp that forced him to elevate his game.
“A lot more man-match technique and tighter windows. It felt like everything for me had to be on time and it had to be aggressive,” Purdy said. “I don't know if there was as many layered kind of throws, just because of how they run things. Everything for me, it seemed like it was just always tight and the vision zones of dropping back and dropping it in the bucket over hook defenders and stuff like that.
“You get that every once in a while, but for the most part, man, he made me have to play aggressive. And I appreciated that, actually. I think that's translated into the season for me to throw with that, I know we've talked about this, but that aggressive mindset and everything. So, it's a big credit to Raheem.”
If it wasn’t clear before, it's definitely clear now that Morris is an upgrade over Robert Saleh . Not only has he gotten the 49ers’ secondary to raise their game — he’s gotten Purdy to as well.
It’s like the cliché saying, “iron sharpens iron.” That’s exactly what training camp was for Purdy, going up against the 49ers’ new defense under Morris. This is why he looks so sharp.
Morris’ defense forced Purdy to play at a high level. And as he said, it translated to the regular season. If you look back at reports during training camp, it was rare for Purdy to turn the ball over.
He was also cited as taking some nice shots and playing within himself. That’s exactly what he’s been doing through five games this season. Adding Mike Evans has helped Purdy out a ton.
But Morris is the one who’s had the greater impact on him.

title: One 49ers Player is Emerging as a Breakout Star
full_text:
A significant reason for the San Francisco 49ers starting the season 5-0 is because of how sweet countless players are performing.
All eyes are on Brock Purdy as arguably the 49ers' best performer, which is why he's being crowned as the MVP already. It's undeniable that Purdy is playing great.
However, there's another 49ers player who deserves recognition. This player is easily emerging as a breakout star and is the 49ers' breakout player of the year so far.
It's none other than cornerback Renardo Green. He's picking up where he left off in his promising 2024 rookie season. Last year, he fell off.
He had a handful of blown assignments that allowed an explosive play or a touchdown. Green didn't look comfortable playing for Robert Saleh.
But under Raheem Morris , he's flourishing. Green had by far his greatest performance of his career in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks.
He picked off Sam Darnold twice, marking his first-ever multi-interception game. His first interception was by far his most impressive, as he was defending against Jaxson Smith-Njigba.
It wasn't a tricky route run, but most defensive backs struggle to stay tight in coverage on Smith-Njigba. Green has stepped it up big-time this year, and the stats back it up.
Green has been targeted 21 times this season and allowed a 52.4% completion rate – a career low and the lowest among cornerbacks on the 49ers, per Next Gen Stats .
His five passes defended are a career high through the first five games of a season and this is the first year he has recorded multiple interceptions in a season (3).
His 23.8% ball hawk rate is the highest of his career and the highest on the team among cornerbacks, and he is the only 49er cornerback who has yet to allow a passing touchdown this season.
Call me crazy, but I'd say that is pretty darn good. Green is easily the 49ers' best defensive back this year. He's even better than Deommodore Lenoir.
Morris will get the credit for why Green is playing so well, but it's also a major credit to the work Green put in, and it all started early in the offseason.
"The way Renardo came to day one of Phase One, you could tell that he had put work in away, which prepared him so much more for the month that we got with him," Kyle Shanahan said. "He had an awesome Phase One, Two and Three... You could tell he'd been working all year and really locked in to getting better at everything."
Green is performing at a Pro Bowl level. If he keeps this up, he'll have a case to be named an All-Pro player. And to think, he was mentioned in offseason trade rumors.

title: The Most Impressive Part About the 49ers’ 5-0 Start
full_text:
Seeing the San Francisco 49ers open up the season with five straight wins is nothing short of impressive.
Now, they were expected to be a good team this season, but anytime you start off the year 5-0, especially notching a win over the Seattle Seahawks , who whooped the 49ers the last two times, it deserves applause.
It’s not just the wins that are awesome to see; it’s how the 49ers are doing. Brock Purdy is playing very sharp, along with Mike Evans , and the 49ers’ defense under Raheem Morris has been lights-out.
However, it’s not the most impressive part of their 5-0 start.
They haven’t needed to rely on Christian McCaffrey. Last year, the 49ers were McCaffrey or bust. They might as well have renamed themselves the San Francisco McCaffreys at that point.
That’s how heavy and insane his usage was, but it was also incredible, even if he wasn’t efficient. Without McCaffrey, it’s unlikely the 49ers make it to the playoffs.
Deviating from a player who’s been the star of the offense is risky and easier said than done, but the 49ers knew they couldn’t replicate his workload in 2026. Not even close to it.
During the offseason, Kyle Shanahan pointed out that the 49ers need to help him out. He’s said that before in previous offseasons, so it was tough to fully take stock of his words.
However, unlike in previous offseasons, McCaffrey wasn’t coming off unreal usage. He’s also not the same player he was in 2023 when he won the Offensive Player of the Year award.
That played a role in the running game’s ineffectiveness last year. Shanahan knows that, which led them to draft Kaelon Black. The rookie has done a solid job of filling in for McCaffrey in spurts.
But Black isn’t the only one helping McCaffrey out. Purdy is doing his part as well. Shanahan is dialing up more passing plays than in previous years.
Their passing game has been more responsible for how great their offense is clicking than the running game. They’re relying more on Purdy and his receivers than on McCaffrey.
It's a surprising yet magnificent sight to see. The best part of it all is that it preserves McCaffrey for when the 49ers need to use him heavily late in the season.
Shanahan surely has that card ready to use when the need arises. Until then, their offense is operating soundly with their newfound identity.

title: One 49ers Player is an Afterthought Despite Impressive Debut
full_text:
With injuries thinning out their wide receiver depth , the San Francisco 49ers have needed their young players to step up.
One player who did that well in Week 3 against the Arizona Cardinals was Jordan Watkins. He caught two explosive passes for 60 yards in his season debut.
He was also blocking amazingly well. That game raised Watkins' stock, and it should've earned him more playing time with the 49ers dealing with injuries.
However, Watkins has been a ghost despite his impressive debut. He hasn't registered a single catch, and that's because he isn't being targeted. Watkins is an afterthought in the 49ers' offense, but if you ask Kyle Shanahan, he doesn't think so.
“He's just gotten more opportunities since his injuries and keep doing what he's doing," Shanahan said. "Guys just run routes and sometimes the ball goes to them, sometimes it doesn't. His opportunity percentages go up with the guys that have been hurt. He was backing up Deebo last week and Mike at times. We had Cooks doing the same. But, when guys go out, you get more opportunities.”
Shanahan is correct that the ball sometimes goes to a receiver and sometimes it doesn't. The thing is, he's the head coach and the offensive play caller.
If he wants Watkins involved, it will happen. One way he can help Watkins be featured more is by having him run more routes. Against the Seattle Seahawks, Watkins only ran eight routes.
Meanwhile, Brandin Cooks, who only just arrived less than a few weeks ago, ran 12. It's clear that Watkins isn't a player that Shanahan wants to use.
In hindsight, maybe Watkins' involvement against the Cardinals was for Shanahan to see how he would respond after he approached Shanahan about playing more.
It's not like he failed that test. Otherwise, Shanahan wouldn't have spoken so highly of him. Even now, Shanahan still speaks highly of Watkins.
"We've been really happy with how he's played in these games. I think he's earned a lot of respect in these three games and with us it doesn't have to do with the stats. I know he's had two catches and stuff in his first game, and those are two really good plays, but because he hasn't had any in the other two games doesn't really mean much to us."
It seems like the only way Watkins will see opportunities with the ball again is if the 49ers are desperate at wide receiver. You'd think that would be the case now with Deebo Samuel out .
But that doesn't appear to be the case. I wouldn't bank on much involvement as a pass catcher from Watkins anytime soon, if at all, this season.

title: Why 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan is Surprised About Brock Purdy and Mike Evans' Connection
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers’ quarterback-wide receiver partnership of Brock Purdy and Mike Evans has taken the NFL by storm.
Five games into the season, FOX Sports reports Purdy has completed 24 of 34 passes targeting Evans this season for 406 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions.
Purdy has a 149.9 passer rating when targeting Evans , the highest among the 55 QB-receiver duos with at least 25 attempts this season.
This prompted a question to the 49ers' head coach, Kyle Shanahan, about whether he's surprised by that instant success. He gave an interesting response.
“Yeah, a little bit. I mean, yes and no," he told reporters on Thursday .
"Mike has been so obviously that good to anybody who watches him and especially to me watching him over the years. He’s always been right there as the best and some people can match with him, but he’s just such a first-ballot Hall of Famer.
"To get him here, just things that we weren’t used to doing as much not having a guy like him. I remember always telling Brock and stuff like, ‘Hey, there’s times you’re just going to sit there and wait and Mike will get it done. You don’t need to progress even if your feet tell you to. If the coverage doesn’t go there, you just wait and give him time because he’ll come down with it.’
"I remember saying to him a ton like, ‘This can be really important that you two have a lot of one-on-one. You guys do that stuff a lot because that’s just about you guys talking to each other.’
"Each one’s going to be different. It’s not like coach talk and telling you, ‘Hey, it’s going to be at this yard line or this hitch.’ It’s stuff you guys have just got to get used to each other.
"I remember going up to Brock in the middle of Australia. I was like, ‘Hey, all that stuff I asked you to work with Mike, are you guys there yet? Are you good?’ I did that jokingly because I knew Mike hadn’t had any reps in like two weeks and Brock got all stressed. He’s like, ‘Well, I haven’t got to yet.’ And I was like, ‘I’m just joking, dude.’ I was like, like, ‘We’ve ran out of time. We’ll see how it goes this week.’
"That fade they threw in Australia that they scored on, I think we had done that full speed once live and that’s just a different drop and different stuff that we hadn’t done.
"So those guys didn’t get a ton of reps out of it, but it just shows how natural Mike is, how natural Brock is, and that it seems like they’ve been working on that stuff for a long time.”

title: 49ers Coach Sounds Off on Mykel Williams' Debut
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' former first-round pick Mykel Williams made his 2026 debut after tearing his ACL to end his rookie season. Williams only played 36% of the defensive snaps with 23 snaps overall. Head coach Kyle Shanahan noted that while Williams did not flash, he did show them what they wanted to see fresh off the injury.
"Yeah, that was our goal to get him around that area," Shanahan said of playing Williams just 23 snaps. "I thought he did a real good job. It was a real good first game back. He didn't have any bad plays.”
Williams had two tackles and added one pressure, according to PFF.
"He had two good plays of sniffing out a screen twice,” added Shanahan. “I thought he had a real good first step for him coming back."
The question now is how much more will the team put on Williams' plate in Week 6? They did not use him much in his versatile role sliding inside on pass-rushing downs. He played on early downs and then would come off the field for sub-package football.
In 2025, the 49ers aligned Williams along the interior defensive line for 54 snaps. That was a 14% rate. In Week 5, he did not have any snaps along the interior. This is where he had his best work as a pass rusher, so the thought is that the 49ers will start to get him mixed in more often.
The next question is how much this means for the 49ers' edge rusher room. They are expected to get Nick Bosa back in the next week or two as well. Williams should be closer to a full-time player in the next two weeks.
So, the 49ers will have two starters locked in. Rookie third-round pick Romello Height has been taking on a bigger role with those two sidelined. It has been a lot to ask of him, but if he can shift into the third edge rusher and just rush on passing downs, he could become more valuable thanks to the experience he gained.
San Francisco also has Keion White, who can serve as a solid fourth option in a rotation. On one hand, this is all in theory, and none of it has come together.  On the other hand, there is a chance this room can become a strength by Week 10.

title: Why 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan has Struggled vs. Commanders HC Dan Quinn
full_text:
After their defeat to the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LI, the careers of then Atlanta Falcons offensive coordinator Kyle Shanahan and head coach Dan Quinn have gone in rather different directions.
Now in his tenth season as the head coach of the San Francisco 49ers, Shanahan has led his team to two NFC West titles, four NFC championship games and two Super Bowl appearances.
But for Quinn, the defensive-minded coach has had to go through the NFL coaching cycle. He was fired as Falcons head coach midway through the 2020 regular season. His Atlanta squad started out 0-5 and now 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris was named the interim head coach after Quinn was let go.
Quinn found his next role quickly, spending the next three seasons as the defensive coordinator for the Dallas Cowboys and being voted the Assistant Coach of the Year in 2021. Prior to Shanahan and the 49ers taking on the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LVIII, Quinn was named head coach of the Washington Commanders.
“I’m so pumped for Dan, I’m so pumped for Washington,” Shanahan said at Super Bowl LVIII Opening Night. “Dan’s a hell of a coach, they got a hell of a one… Dan taught me so much in Atlanta, I’m very grateful for how much he’s helped my career…”
Shanahan’s tenure alongside Quinn in Atlanta lasted just two years but it catapulted his coaching career following their Super Bowl run and directing Matt Ryan to a Most Valuable Player award in 2016.
The Week 6 matchup between Washington and San Francisco will be the fifth time that the two will square off since their split and the first since Quinn has been the head coach of the Commanders.
Here is a recap of the prior four games:
2019 Week 15, Falcons 29-22 win vs. San Francisco
Quinn’s lone win came in their first-ever meeting. Already eliminated from playoff contention, the Falcons put up 19 points in the fourth quarter and outscored the 49ers by ten to steal a win.
The Atlanta defense forced four fumbles but only two were recovered. George Kittle had 13 catches on 17 targets for 134 yards.
Despite the loss, the 49ers still clinched a playoff spot after the Los Angeles Rams loss to the Cowboys. Julio Jones’ 5-yard goal-line touchdown to give Atlanta a one-point lead with two seconds left has been forgotten thanks to Dre Greenlaw’s goal-line stop of Jacob Hollister in Week 17.
2021 NFC Wild Card, 49ers 23-17 win vs. Dallas
Shanahan got his revenge, ending Quinn and his seventh-ranked defense in the 2021 NFC Wild Card. Deebo Samuel was in the midst of the best four-game stretch of his career, accounting for 110 yards on 13 touches. Samuel’s 26-yard touchdown run following a K’Waun Williams interception of Dak Prescott proved to be the game-winner.
On offense, Jimmy Garoppolo finished with 172 passing yards, but Shanahan ultimately took the ball out of his hands with the running game finishing with 169 yards on 38 attempts.
A late comeback from Dallas was not enough as time ran out on the final possession of the game, similar to Jayden Daniels this past week for Washington in overtime.
2022 NFC Divisional, 49ers 19-12 win vs. Dallas
The two met again in the playoff for a second straight year, and again it was Shanahan coming out on top. With Brock Purdy now at quarterback, San Francisco didn’t find the end zone until the first play of the fourth quarter, which was a 2-yard run by Christian McCaffrey.
Quinn’s defense generated two sacks, but San Francisco’s two interceptions off Prescott flipped things as one resulted in a Robbie Gould field goal and one ended a Dallas drive that reached the red zone.
2023 Week 5, 49ers 42-10 win vs. Dallas
Shanahan’s best performance against his former fellow coach came in a Sunday night thumping.
Purdy threw for four touchdowns, finding Kittle for three of them. McCaffrey was bottled up on the ground, averaging just 2.7 yards on 19 carries. He did rush for a touchdown, as did his backup, Jordan Mason, who finished with 69 yards on 10 carries.
The result put the 49ers at 5-0, tied with the Eagles for the best record in the NFC.
In the four games against Quinn, Shanahan and his offense is averaging 26.5 points and 346.7 yards per game. While a majority of this came against a Dallas defense that boasted Trevon Diggs, Micah Parsons and DeMarcus Lawrence, Shanahan has shown that no matter the defensive playmakers that Quinn has at his disposal, he can still move the ball and find the end zone.
Quinn, alongside defensive coordinator and playcaller Daronte Jones, has yet to find their footing so far in 2026, ranking 23rd in total defense (350.4 yds/g) throughout the first five weeks of the regular season.
Shanahan has the 49ers offense ranked ninth in total offense (365 yds/g), but as the team is down multiple wide receivers heading into Monday night’s showdown, we’ll have to see if the 49ers head coach can find similar success against the man he shared two seasons with on the sideline.

title: All Eyes Are Now on This 49ers WR Returning From Injury
full_text:
It's Week 5 and the San Francisco 49ers have many injuries on offense.
Deebo Samuel hurt his hamstring in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks. Jake Tonges will miss the whole season because of a torn MCL he picked up in Week 1. Demarcus Robinson's ankle sprain in Week 2 means he will miss up to 6 games, maybe more.
Rookie De'Zhaun Stribling suffered a left ankle deltoid ligament sprain/rupture and will be back at the end of November/early December.
They desperately need bodies. Regardless of how severe these injuries are, the 49ers are still 5-0 for the season. All things considered, it's very impressive, but it doesn't change the fact that they are relying too much on their older veterans.
Christian Kirk's return should be intriguing. The 49ers have opened the practice window after battling a calf injury.
Kirk arrived in free agency on an incredibly cheap deal considering his career stats, but it couldn't have been a worse start to the San Francisco life after picking up his injury on the very first day of training camp.
"Just felt like I kind of got over that hump and feeling like myself again," Kirk said to 49erswebzone . "Body starting to respond to just the training and the recovery and whatnot.
"And so, just wanted to communicate that to them, and tell them that I was ready to go, and get back out there.
"So, excited to get out there. It's obviously been a while, and just ready to attack this week."
Kirk has yet to play a snap or be integrated into Kyle Shanahan's offense, but he believes his experience will help him adapt quickly.
"I think it's like riding a bike," Kirk said. "I've been doing it for a while, and so, for me, it's just getting back out there, getting integrated with the guys. Obviously, it's been hard not being out there, but been really cool to watch day in and day out how this team comes to work every single day, and for it to be able to carry over on Sundays.
"I'm just excited, like I said, to get in the mix, and hopefully, provide some other production to help us win some more games."
Kirk will need to step up and help ease the pressure on San Francisco's remaining receiving options. Although his return date remains uncertain, don't rush him because his importance to the 49ers is growing as injuries leave the team dangerously thin at wide receiver.

title: New Report Reveals When Baker Mayfield Could Return for Buccaneers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will look to improve to 2-4 on the year when they face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. When they do, they won't be playing their starting quarterback.
Undrafted free agent rookie has been deputizing starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for the last two games as Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb he suffered in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings. Daniels hasn't been bad in the role, and he's set to play another game on Sunday under center as Mayfield continues to recover.
This is Mayfield's team, though, and the team's three-year, $165 million extension of him this offseason proves it. Mayfield has been itching to get back to action ever since his injury, and one NFL insider pinpointed the exact game that could happen — and it's coming up very soon.
NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that there's "optimism" in Tampa Bay that Mayfield could return for the team's Week 7 game against the Carolina Panthers.
Bucs QB Baker Mayfield will miss a third consecutive game since dislocating his thumb in Week 3. But there’s optimism he’ll return next week — just in time for Tampa Bay’s first division game of the season at Carolina. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/hVvUAJDNjT pic.twitter.com/HwpFcNzTQY
Mayfield tried to throw on Wednesday afternoon after Bucs practice. It's unknown how that throwing session went, but the team clearly did not think he was ready enough to get back to practice this week, so Daniels gets the start once again for Tampa Bay.
This return timeline makes sense for a lot of reasons, however. To begin, Bowles' initial assessment of Mayfield's injury was three weeks minimum — it will be past that assessment once the Bucs play the Steelers this Sunday, so Mayfield's window has opened up.
Additionally, this will be Tampa Bay's first NFC South game. The team, despite being 1-4, is one and a half games out of the NFC South lead, so it's crucial to gain some ground in that division. Tampa Bay will want its starting quarterback out there when it does, so it's understandable that Mayfield would try to get back in time for it.
Finally, Mayfield used to play for Carolina in 2022, and the experience was an overall negative one for him. He's made it very clear that he pays particular attention to revenge games on the schedule, so there's probably some extra incentive there as well.
Before he got hurt, Mayfield had thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. He's struggled in a few different respects, though, as he's fumbled the ball three times this year and lost all of them. He'll look to bounce back from his recent stretch of play when he gets back under center for the Bucs.
Tampa Bay — led by Daniels — will play the Steelers on Sunday at 1 p.m. in Raymond James Stadium. But don't expect Mayfield to be away for long.

title: Former Super Bowl Champion Believes Jalon Daniels Is Bucs' Best Option at QB
full_text:
Baker Mayfield has had a rough start to the 2026 season.
Not only did Mayfield fail to lead his team to a single victory in each of his four starts this year, but his individual performance has predominantly been defined by turnovers, poor accuracy and a lack of poise in the pocket. To make matters worse, Mayfield suffered a brutal dislocation of his right thumb in the final moments of his team's home loss to the Cleveland Browns a few weeks ago, forcing him to the sidelines for an undetermined period of time.
Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who surprisingly beat out veteran free agent signing Jake Browning for the backup QB job in training camp, has been tasked with holding down the fort after Mayfield's injury. And that's exactly what he's done.
After a narrow defeat at the hands of the Green Bay Packers in his first NFL game, Daniels showed out in Dallas on Thursday Night Football in Week 5, leading his team to an impressive and improbable victory against one of the most prolific offenses in the NFL.
Meanwhile, although he's been very supportive of Daniels, Mayfield has been dead set on returning to the lineup as soon as possible. In fact, he recently resumed throwing in hopes of fast-tracking his path back onto the field.
But would that really be good for the team?
At least one member of the Buccaneers Super Bowl winning team in 2020 doesn't think so.
On a recent episode of his podcast hosted with Jarvis Landry, 4th and South, Fournette had quite a hot take about the Bucs' current quarterback situation.
"I think, me personally, Jalon Daniels is the perfect fit for the Bucs right now," Fournette said. "They're winning! When Baker was back there, they weren't winning nothing. So I think it was a blessing and a curse. I'm not wishing nobody gets hurt, but at the same time, he's giving them more opportunity to win."
Fournette believes that Daniels is the team's best option to win right now.
"And I'm not saying Jalon's decision-making is better than Baker," he said. "To me it's even, because Baker throws picks, he fumbles, he does a lot. But at the end of the day, what can you do for me now? They're winning. I say keep Daniels in until we figure it out. Yes, Baker's got $100 million contract, but damn that, we want to win, coach."
Lenny wants Jalon Daniels to KEEP the QB job in Tampa 😳 Jarvis isn’t buying it 👀 Jalon Daniels might be the winning fit... #4thAndSouth #GoBucs #NFL pic.twitter.com/eysRVLdDFm
Fournette is certainly entitled to his opinion. That being said, as good as Daniels looked last week against the Cowboys and as bad as Mayfield looked in the first month of the season, the Buccaneers are going to be at their best for a longer period of time with Mayfield under center.
Not only that, but there isn't a chance that the Buccaneers would even consider relegating a healthy Mayfield to the bench because of the massive contract they awarded him just over a month ago.
The Buccaneers believe in Mayfield. And with every positive performance they get out of Daniels, their belief in him will continue to increase as well. But this is Mayfield's team, and the Bucs are prepared to sink or swim with him as the captain of their ship.

title: 3 Most Dangerous Steelers Players Buccaneers Will Face
full_text:
Even though they're only 5 games into the regular season, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have already entered 'must-win' territory. As would be the case for any team that opened the season with 4 consecutive losses.
The Bucs do have some positive momentum, though, as they're coming off an impressive victory in Dallas over the Cowboys last Thursday night. Not only did undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels impress in his second NFL game, but the Bucs managed to contain the Cowboys' most dangerous weapons, holding each of Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens well below their expected output and allowing the Bucs to secure a much needed victory on the road.
If the Buccaneers hope to kickstart a winning streak, they'll need to do the same against the Steelers at home and limit the damage from Pittsburgh's most dangerous players. Let's take a closer look at who those players are and how the Bucs could achieve that:
There's little doubt about which player Todd Bowles' defense should be most concerned about on Sunday.
Jaylen Warren has always had explosive ability, but he was mostly used as a change of pace back under Mike Tomlin. Now that he's finally been given the keys to the backfield, Warren has taken that opportunity and run with it... literally.
Warren currently ranks third in the NFL in total yards from scrimmage with 640 and he's undoubtedly established himself as the team's most dynamic offensive weapon. Not only is Warren averaging an impressive 5.7 yards per carry running the football, but he's also been the team's greatest weapon as he leads the team in both receptions (19) and receiving yards (230).
Warren appears to be gaining confidence as he continues to earn more touches. He had arguably his best game as a pro last week vs. Indianapolis, where he exploded for 188 yards and 1 TD.
Despite having a relatively quiet 2025 season (at least by his standards) T.J. Watt has wasted no time reminding everyone why he remains one of the NFL's truly elite edge defenders. Although his 4.5 sacks are tied for the sixth most in the league, Watt is impacting the game in other ways this year, too.
According to PFF, Watt has been the best run defender among all edge rushers so far this year with an outstanding 92.1 run defense grade. Watt has been an extremely well-rounded player in 2026, producing 13 tackles, 6 TFLs and 7 QB hits to go along with 1 forced fumble and 1 fumble recovery.  Watt also has an interception this year, which he returned 35 yards for a TD to help seal a Steelers' victory against the Falcons back in Week 1.
The point is that T.J. Watt is still a game wrecker, and the Buccaneers will need to account for his presence at all times. If not? Watt could single-handedly turn the tide in his team's favor.
Some people may roll their eyes when they see Aaron Rodgers listed as one of the Steelers' most dangerous players, but the truth is, he's still got what it takes to lead his team to victories.
Rodgers has quietly played some pretty good football over the past few weeks, as the 42-year-old has now thrown three TD passes in each of his last three games. Rodgers is currently fifth in the league with 11 TD passes this year and 11th in total passing yards with 1,234.
Although Rodgers is very much immobile at this point of his career, he's still got more than enough arm talent to make every throw on the field. He also processes the game at an elite level, which is a big reason why he's been able to find so much success this season despite a really underwhelming group of pass catchers to work with.
If the Bucs aren't strategic with the looks they give Rodgers, both in coverage and pressure packages , he will make them pay.

title: If Buccaneers Can’t Sack Aaron Rodgers, They Have a Major Problem
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' pass rush has been struggling to get off the ground this season.
The defense stands at only six sacks through five games this season, with two coming from inside linebackers Alex Anzalone and Josiah Trotter and three coming from backup pass rushers David Walker and Anthony Nelson. While it's good that young players like Walker and Trotter are showcasing their abilities and proving that they are bright prospects for the team, many did not expect them to be the leading men in this unit.
Two players who have yet to notch a stat are starters Yaya Diaby and Rueben Bain Jr., both players whom many Bucs fans were excited about this season. This isn't fully their fault, as Bain Jr. has missed a couple of games due to injury and Diaby has had a couple of nagging ailments of his own.
However, the results to this point are certainly not what Bucs fans had in mind when they thought of the revamped pass rush the team made throughout the course of this offseason, and the players present are too good to be in the situation that they are in.
Along with Diaby and Bain Jr., veteran pass rusher Al-Quadin Muhammad has yet to step in as well, which is surprising considering he had 11 sacks in a rotational role with the Detroit Lions last season.
The quarterback they are going to try to take down? Aaron Rodgers, one of the best to do it in the NFL and someone who knows how to deal with pressure when faced with it.
However, Rodgers has actually been mortal against the Bucs, posting a 3-3 record through six career games with ten touchdowns to a matching ten interceptions.
If the Buccaneers are able to force Rodgers to make some mistakes and we see players like Diaby, Bain Jr., and Muhammad rise to the occasion, we could see the Bucs come away with the upset win during Week 6.
But if the pass rush continues to be lackluster and players like Walker, Nelson and the inside linebackers are the only ones who can keep the pass rush alive, it could be a very long day for the team.

title: Buccaneers' Todd Bowles Rules Out 2 Players vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers in a game that could arguably make or break their season this early in the year. A win gets the Bucs to 2-4 and keeps them hanging on in the NFC South, but a loss drops them to 1-5 and puts them even further down the NFL ladder.
Tampa Bay will be mostly healthy when they face the Steelers, but there are two big players who won't be playing, according to head coach Todd Bowles. Thankfully for Tampa Bay, it's two players that the team wasn't expecting to rely on anyway this Sunday.
There are only two players out against the Steelers on Sunday, and it's two players that were assumed to be out anyway.
Bowles said Friday that quarterback Baker Mayfield and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. will be out on Sunday. Both players have been dealing with long-term injuries and were not expected to play on Sunday regardless.
Todd Bowles says that only Baker Mayfield and Antoine Winfield are OUT. Sean Tucker will be a game-time decision, he says. pic.twitter.com/BcipWIMqSm
Mayfield dislocated his thumb against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3 and has been out since. He's been pushing to play against the Steelers since the Bucs beat the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football, but he isn't quite ready to return to football action this weekend. Expect him to start ramping up to play next week when the Bucs face off against the Panthers.
Winfield fractured his ribs against the Green Bay Packers, and he was expected to be out for 2-4 weeks. This is the second week he'll be out, but he was working on the side with a trainer on Friday — that could be an encouraging sign for future games.
Running back Sean Tucker and Ayden Garnes were both working with trainers on Wednesday, but both have been participating on Thursday and Friday — Bowles said Tucker would be a game-time decision. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison and linebacker SirVocea Dennis both missed last week's game against the Cowboys, but both are expected to be available against the Steelers.
The Bucs will face the Steelers at 1 p.m. on Oct. 18 at Raymond James Stadium.

title: Buccaneers' Biggest Advantage Over Steelers Could Be the Difference in Week 6
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are coming off their first win of the 2026 season. After stumbling out of the gate winless through their first four games, though, this isn't exactly an achievement that should be celebrated, but rather something they are hoping will translate into some momentum as they prepare to host the 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers at Raymond James Stadium this Sunday.
Despite the Bucs' struggles this season and the fact that they're still without their starting quarterback Baker Mayfield, the Steelers are still only slightly favored to win this football game.
There is no doubt that the Buccaneers possess more talent on paper than your standard 1-4 team, and Tampa Bay absolutely has a chance to take down the Steelers at home.
If the Bucs are going to reel off a second consecutive victory this weekend, there's a strong chance it will be in large because of one distinct advantage they have over the Steelers.
Heading into this season, many expected the Buccaneers' cornerback room to be the team's weakest position group. So far? They've been the best.
Despite coming off a down year in 2025, fifth-year outside CB Zyon McCollum has been one of the most impressive shutdown corners in the entire league. Despite having to match up against some of the best WRs in the league, including Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Justin Jefferson, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, McCollum has thrived so far this year, using the size, speed and instincts that earned him the three-year, $48 million contract he signed prior to last season to completely stifle some of the league's most talented wideouts.
So far this season, McCollum has had 62 matchups against 'top receivers' and allowed just a single reception. He also has four passes defended and an incredible 39.6 passer rating when targeted in coverage.
Zyon McCollum has been lockdown 🆚 top receivers in 2026 🔒 62 matchups. 7 targets. 1 reception for 18 yards. 4 passes defensed. 39.6 passer rating when targeted. pic.twitter.com/sRDcRCxlqZ
Jacob Parrish, meanwhile, has made a seamless transition from the slot, where he excelled as a rookie, to the outside. Listed at just 5'10", there was plenty of doubt regarding whether or not Parrish could hold up on the outside, but so far, he's looked the part. Parrish is a feisty pest of a CB and his elite agility and movement skills have allowed him to irritate opposing WRs who are much bigger.
On the other side, the Pittsburgh Steelers' wide receiver room has been a complete disaster so far this year.
As a group, the Steelers are dead last in the NFL in terms of separation against man coverage. Michael Pittman Jr., the team's primary free-agent acquisition in the offseason, is currently on the injured reserve.
Meanwhile, D.K. Metcalf — who the team is paying over $30 million per season — has looked like a sunk cost. Through five games this year, Metcalf is averaging fewer than four receptions and just 45 yards per contest. He has one receiving TD this season.
The #Steelers can't have DK Metcalf continuing to have the season he's having so far. In the game yesterday he had the following stat line: 28 routes, 4 targets, 3 catches and 12 yards. He had a Rec EPA of -0.8 His YACOE was -7 Average AY/Tgt was 3.3 These numbers aren't good…
With no Antoine Winfield Jr. on the back end of the defense, the Buccaneers will need other players to step up to ensure they can limit the Steelers' passing attack on Sunday, just like the Steelers will need players like Germie Bernard to step up at the receiver position due to injury.
Either way, it's impossible to deny that the Buccaneers should have a strong advantage when it comes to how their cornerbacks match up against the Steelers' wide receivers on Sunday. As long as the Bucs' young corners continue to play how they have been, Pittsburgh could have a real challenge generating any sort of production through the air.
If that happens? It would also be a real challenge for them to win this football game against a Buccaneers team that needs to start racking up some wins.

title: 3 Questions Facing Buccaneers Against Steelers in Week 6: Will Tampa Bay Stop This Crucial Steelers Player?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a tough task on Sunday. They're looking to move to 1-4, but they'll try and do it against a stout 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers team heading into Tampa Bay.
The Bucs got their first win of the year against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5, but now, they'll have another test. Here are three questions we have for head coach Todd Bowles' squad as Sunday rolls around:
It's rare that one player leads a team in both rushing and receiving, but Jaylin Warren is a rare player. Warren has 410 yards and one touchdown on the ground, but he also has 230 yards and a touchdown receiving, too.
At +0.131 EPA/play, Warren is the sixth-best running back in the NFL by that metric, and he's slated to do some serious damage on Sunday. The Bucs have to know where he is at all times and be able to contain him on the ground and through the air, and Bowles knows very well how good Warren is.
“I mean, he's been playing outstanding at running, blocking and pass receiving. You really don't see [all of that] from one guy," Bowles said. "He's doing everything. He's a very good pass protector. He's an outstanding runner, and he can catch the ball very well, and he makes you miss. [If] you miss a tackle, a guy like that, if you don't wrap up, he's going to take it to the house. So, he's been playing great football.”
Bucky Irving went off for 165 yards against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday night. He probably won't do that again (probably) — but how well will he and the Bucs do?
The Steelers give up 103.4 rushing yards per game on average. They rank 13th there and 17th in the NFL in yards per rush (4.0), so they're a decent run-stopping unit. Tampa Bay had a great game in Week 5 to inflate the average, but they're fifth in the NFL in yards per rush (4.9) and they're seventh in rush yards per game (133.0).
If Tampa Bay is going to win this game against the Steelers, they'll simply have to get the ground game rolling. Irving instills a lot of confidence that this will happen, but it remains to be seen until game day comes around.
Aaron Rodgers, so far this season, has a sack rate of 6.97%, the 11th-most-sacked quarterback in the NFL. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers can't really get to the quarterback at all — the entire defense has a sack rate of 3.49%, which is good for 30th in the league.
Rodgers is largely immobile at his age, but the Bucs haven't been able to generate a pass rush at all. It will be Rodgers' instinct to get rid of the ball quickly, which will make it harder for Tampa Bay to bring him down. That obviously includes the edge rushers, but interior pass rushers like Calijah Kancey could have a day against Rodgers — if the middle collapses, Rodgers has nowhere to go.
Tampa Bay has been trying to figure out its pass rush for years now. Rodgers is a prime candidate to do so, but can players like Kancey, Yaya Diaby and Rueben Bain Jr. get home on Sunday?

title: Todd Bowles May Have Revealed The Buccaneers’ Next Breakout Star
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers expected a lot out of their rookie class in 2026. They really focused on defense and drafted an edge rusher in the first round, bringing in Rueben Bain Jr. from Miami, and they also selected a linebacker in the second round by picking Missouri's Josiah Trotter.
Some of those picks, like Bain, haven't yet panned out the way the Bucs have hoped. Others, like Trotter, have looked really strong so far this season — but there's one defensive rookie who may have impressed more than any Bucs draft pick.
Head coach Todd Bowles spoke to media on Wednesday, and he revealed which Bucs player he thinks has been one of the best players on the team so far — and it's one of Tampa Bay's drafted rookies.
Bowles said that nickel cornerback Keionte Scott, whom the Bucs drafted in the fourth round in April out of Miami, has been one of his best players so far in 2026, and he commended his ability to tackle and his work ethic throughout the week.
“[Scott has] been one of our best players this year. I mean, he doesn't say much. He's been very solid with his fundamentalist technique, and he tackles way more than he weighs. He tackles almost like a linebacker. He's a very tough kid, wants to be good, wants to be great, extremely tough, puts in the work during the week. That's what you really like about him. He really studies and gets it down for Sunday, and he executes well.”
Scott has played well at the nickel position so far. The Bucs defense puts up −0.179 EPA with him on the field and +0.011 with him off, showing that the team is more effective when he is playing. So far this season, he has 24 solo tackles (one tackle for loss) and two passes defended.
"I think first is the want-to," Scott said. "That's something you can just tell right away about a back, if he wants to stick his head in the fan... I'm one of those guys that's proud to have that in my toolbox, have that in my game — I just wanna get in there."
Scott will continue to get snaps at nickel as the defense starts to gel. He'll have a big test on Sunday when the Bucs face off against the Steelers in Raymond James Stadium at 1 p.m.

title: Buccaneers Thursday Practice All But Confirms Starting Quarterback vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers play the Pittsburgh Steelers in just three days. Every game for the Bucs is important from here on out, as the team is 1-4 and needs to start stacking wins if it has any hope of making the playoffs.
Head coach Todd Bowles said after the team's win against the Dallas Cowboys last Thursday that undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who is filling in for starter Baker Mayfield as he recovers from a dislocated thumb, was preparing to start again against the Steelers.
But Mayfield was reportedly pushing to play, per NFL insider James Palmer, and the Buccaneers tested his grip ability by watching him throw on Wednesday afternoon.
Coach Baker Mayfield could return to player Baker Mayfield next week against the Steelers. I'm told Mayfield is pushing to play but it's 10 days out and it's too early for the Bucs to know medically if he can go. The stitches were taken out Monday and it's a matter of his thumb…
The Buccaneers conducted practice on Thursday, though, and that practice virtually confirmed Mayfield's status against the Steelers this Sunday.
Mayfield once again did not practice on Thursday, with Jalon Daniels taking the brunt of the first-team reps. It's unknown how Mayfield's throwing session went, but the team doesn't seem to want him back at practice just yet.
With that, Daniels is set for his third NFL start. Daniels comes into the game having thrown for 337 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions — he's also run for 87 yards. The undrafted rookie hasn't played perfectly, but he's impressed with his ability to run the offense competently, and he's gone a long way to prove the Bucs made the right decision to have him as QB2.
A likely target for Mayfield's return will be in Week 7. The Buccaneers play the Carolina Panthers in their first divisional game, and Mayfield will be beyond the three-week minimum that Bowles previously revealed after he was injured against the Minnesota Vikings.
For now, though, the Bucs remain Daniels' team to lead heading into Week 6. The Bucs will face off against the Steelers at 1 p.m. on Oct. 18 in Raymond James Stadium and will look to continue what would be the start of a long and grueling turnaround in 2026.

title: Have the Buccaneers Found Their Offensive Identity for the 2026 Season?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got their first win of the season against the Dallas Cowboys. It was a back-and-forth game where the defense was able to do enough to help get the win, but a bigger storyline coming out of the game is the offense.
It feels like for the first time this season, the Bucs offense was in sync and able to find its footing. This was mainly due to the work of Zac Robinson, which limited what Jalon Daniels needed to do for this offense and the great running ability of back Bucky Irving.
Irving really has come back to form this season, posting 21 carries for 165 yards and a rushing touchdown against Dallas as well as two catches for ten yards and a touchdown as well. Irving already has 77 carries for 406 rushing yards and two touchdowns this season, only 182 yards away from his total last year in 2025, playing in half as many games to this point.
I believe that the Bucs' offensive identity in 2026 will literally run through Bucky Irving, something that shouldn't be too surprising when we look at Zac Robinson's history as offensive coordinator in Atlanta.
Robinson ran both Bijan Robinson and Tyler Allgeier wild in 2024 and 2025, with both backs combined having 441 carries for 2100 rushing yards and 17 rushing touchdowns as well as 74 receptions for 519 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown in 2024. In 2025, it was 430 carries for 1992 rushing yards and 15 rushing touchdowns along with 93 receptions for 916 receiving yards and four receiving touchdowns.
I think that the team does need to see more usage from Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker going forward, but it's very clear that Robinson plans to use Irving in some type of Bijan role going forward with this team.
There are pros and cons to this type of identity, as many expected players like Baker Mayfield, Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. to lead the way for this offense this season. However, the positive is that it could help Mayfield button up some of the offensive struggles he had before his injury this season and limit turnovers overall.
Time will tell if this formula will work for Tampa Bay in the long run, but it seems like we've had a glimpse into what Robinson wants to do going forward.
